Covers (1) whether the project triggers a site plan under LDC Chapter 25-5 and which procedural path (administrative vs. commission vs. Site Plan Lite); (2) site-and-building form requirements under LDC Subchapter E and any superseding regulating plan (NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD, Waller Creek District, Downtown Austin Plan, Airport Boulevard Corridor); (3) frontage build-to, entrance orientation, transparency/glazing, articulation, screening, and streetscape (clear/planting/supplemental zones); (4) overlay-driven design review (Waterfront Overlay, UNO, Downtown Creeks, DDBP/Design Commission).

    11→- LDC Chapter 25-5 — Site plan procedures, classifications, exemptions
    12→- LDC Chapter 25-2, Subchapter E — Design Standards and Mixed Use (Article 1 applicability; Article 2 site; Article 3 building; Article 4 VMU; Article 5 CTC definitions)
    13→- LDC § 25-2-721 et seq. — Waterfront Overlay general + 16 subdistricts (§ 25-2-738 North Shore Central; § 25-2-739 Rainey; § 25-2-733 Butler Shores)
    14→- LDC § 25-2-586 — Downtown Density Bonus Program (DDBP)
    15→- LDC § 25-2-167, § 25-2-643 — Downtown Creeks Combining District
    16→- LDC § 25-2-753 et seq. + BCM 12.1 — University Neighborhood Overlay (UNO)
    17→- ERC Regulating Plan (LDC § 25-2-149) — Articles 1–6
    18→- NBG, Plaza Saltillo TOD, East MLK TOD, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD Regulating Plans
    19→- Waller Creek District Design Guidelines
    20→- Great Streets Master Plan (downtown program)
    21→- City of Austin Standard Details — street furniture, sidewalk, dumpster enclosure
    22→
    23→## Regulatory pathway
    24→
    25→| Procedural path | Trigger | Decision body | Typical timeline |
    26→|---|---|---|---|
    27→| Building permit only — no site plan | Single-family / duplex on existing platted lot; interior remodel; ADA sidewalk projects; specific § 25-5 exemptions | DSD plan review | 4–8 wk |
    28→| **Site Plan Lite** (single-family, two-family, small commercial) | Eligible small projects under § 25-5; specific use list and size caps | Administrative (DSD) | 8–12 wk |
    29→| **Administrative site plan** (standard) | Default for most commercial / mixed-use / multifamily not requiring waivers | DSD staff | 6–9 mo from intake to release; 3+ rounds of comments common |
    30→| **Commission site plan** | Variances from § 25-5 standards; certain conditional uses; some overlays | Land Use Commission / Planning Commission | 9–14 mo; public hearing required |
    31→| **Design Commission / DDBP review** | Downtown DDBP bonus projects; certain Great Streets sites | Design Commission (advisory) + DDBP gatekeeper | Add 2–4 mo *before* site plan submittal |
    32→| **Waterfront Planning Advisory Board** | Any site plan in a WO subdistrict | Director requests recommendation per § 25-5-143(C) | Add 1–2 mo |
    33→| **PARD director sign-off** | Required for every site plan in WO | PARD director (§ 25-2-721(A)(2)) | Concurrent with admin site plan |
    34→| **AEC (Alternative Equivalent Compliance)** | Numeric Subchapter E deviation beyond Minor Modification scope; only for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, Article 3 | Director-approved concept plan | Concept plan due ≥ 10 days before pre-app; expires 3 yr (one 1-yr extension) |
    35→
    36→Site plan is the **envelope contract**; building permit follows and inherits the approved site plan's site form. Don't confuse the two — building permit alone cannot fix a site-plan-level form non-compliance.
    37→
    38→## Constraints to evaluate
    39→
    40→### Site plan trigger and path
    41→
    42→- **Verify site plan is required at all**. Pure interior remodel and certain minor projects are permit-only under § 25-5 exemptions. For everything commercial/multifamily/MU expect a site plan.
    43→- **Site Plan Lite eligibility** is restrictive and tied to a specific use list and size caps — don't assume eligibility from project narrative; confirm against the current § 25-5 Lite list before factoring the shorter timeline.
    44→- **Commission-level escalation** is triggered by waivers from § 25-5 standards (e.g., compatibility, parking, access). Identify the waivers needed at concept stage — every commission item adds 3–6 months and public-hearing risk.
    45→
    46→### Subchapter E applicability and compliance tier (LDC Subchapter E, § 1.2)
    47→
    48→- Subchapter E applies if (a) project requires a site plan under Chapter 25-5, (b) site is **not** in a categorically exempt regulating plan area, and (c) the specific standard is triggered by the project's principal street type per Table A.
    49→- **Categorically exempt regulating plans** (§ 1.2.4.A.12): NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo TOD, East MLK TOD, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD, Waller Creek District, Downtown Austin Plan, Airport Boulevard Corridor Plan. These plans *each impose their own* form standards — exemption from Subchapter E ≠ exemption from form rules.
    50→- **Other carve-outs:** AG, AV, TN zoning, UNO (§ 1.2.4.A.2–3); industrial uses *only when not on a CTC* (§ 1.2.4.A.6); warehouse with <25% non-industrial GFA *only when not on a CTC* (§ 1.2.4.A.9). PUD supersedes Subchapter E only to the extent of conflict (§ 1.2.5.B.2.g) — PUD silence ≠ exemption.
    51→- **Compliance tier:** Full Compliance (§ 1.2.2) for new construction on undeveloped land or full-demo redevelopment; Partial Compliance (§ 1.2.3) for additions / Level 3 remodels >50% work-area where principal-street façade is remodeled. Partial Compliance allows existing-condition waivers; document on cover sheet.
    52→
    53→### Principal street hierarchy (Subchapter E § 2.1)
    54→
    55→Principal street priority: **CTC > Internal Circulation Route > Urban Roadway > Suburban Roadway > Highway/Hill Country Roadway**. Determines build-to %, glazing %, entrance orientation, and parking-placement restrictions. **Sidewalk and supplemental zone standards apply to all abutting frontages** independently (§ 2.2.1.B), each governed by its own roadway type.
    56→
    57→- 20 enumerated CTC segments; CTC is defined by name **and** segment limits — confirm the parcel falls within stated geographic endpoints, not just on the named street.
    58→- Sites with frontage on multiple equal-class streets: Director designates principal based on transit service; if equal/absent, owner designates.
    59→
    60→### Build-to / frontage occupation
    61→
    62→Net Frontage Length (NFL) = lot line minus ICR ROW, compatibility setbacks, easements, drive aisles, sidewalks, and stairs at building perimeter. Parking structures, canopies, accessory structures **do not count** toward build-to.
    63→
    64→| Frontage type | Build-to (min % of NFL) | Source |
    65→|---|---|---|
    66→| Subchapter E CTC | 75% | Subchapter E § 2.2.2 |
    67→| Subchapter E Urban Roadway | 40% | Subchapter E § 2.2.3 |
    68→| NBG / ERC Active Edge | 100% | NBG 5.8 / ERC 5.6 |
    69→| NBG / ERC CTC (basic) | 75% | NBG 4.3.3 / ERC 4.3.3 |
    70→| NBG / ERC Pedestrian Priority Collector | 75% | NBG 4.3.3 / ERC 4.3.3 |
    71→| NBG / ERC Urban Roadway (basic) | 50% | NBG 4.3.3 / ERC 4.3.3 |
    72→| TOD CTC (Plaza Saltillo / East MLK) | 75% | TOD plan 4.3.3 |
    73→| TOD Pedestrian Priority Street | 50% | TOD plan 4.3.3 |
    74→| TOD Local Street | 40% | TOD plan 4.3.3 |
    75→
    76→No 80% tier exists in current ERC/NBG/TOD plans — outdated references should be treated with suspicion.
    77→
    78→### Building entrance (Subchapter E § 2.4)
    79→
    80→- ≥1 customer entrance must face the principal street and connect directly to the clear or supplemental zone via an unobstructed exterior path.
    81→- Each separate ground-floor commercial tenant along the principal-street elevation needs its own entrance.
    82→- Advisory 75-ft entrance interval (§ 2.4.B.2): exceeding triggers long-wall pedestrian treatment (shade, glazing, articulation, awnings) — not a hard violation but is a real cost.
    83→- Non-street-facing entrance exception (§ 2.4.B.1(a)–(d)) requires **all four** conditions: ≥80% NFL built to clear/supplemental zone; continuous shaded sidewalk principal-street→entrance; entrance within 100 ft of street-facing façade line; shade trees ≤30 ft o.c. between building and any parking.
    84→- **AEC is not available for § 2.4 entry requirements** (§ 1.5.2). Plan the entrance correctly at concept; you cannot buy a deviation later.
    85→
    86→### Sidewalk: clear / planting / supplemental zones (Subchapter E § 2.2)
    87→
    88→- Three-zone system: planting (curb-adjacent, trees + utilities) → clear (unobstructed pedestrian travel) → optional supplemental (active uses adjacent to building face).
    89→- Widths vary by principal street class; dimensions must be labeled on site + landscape plan, at narrowest point where variable.
    90→- Build-to can be satisfied at edge of properly designated supplemental zone rather than clear zone.
    91→- Great Streets program participation exempts downtown sites (bounded by MLK, Lady Bird Lake, IH-35, Lamar) from CTC/Urban Roadway sidewalk + supplemental zone standards per § 2.2.2.B and § 2.2.3.B — but Great Streets has its own (typically richer) streetscape spec.
    92→
    93→### Ground-floor transparency / glazing (Subchapter E § 3.2)
    94→
    95→| Condition | Min glazing | Source |
    96→|---|---|---|
    97→| Principal street, 2–10 ft above grade (non-residential, Sub. E) | 40% | § 3.2.2.A.1 |
    98→| Other street-facing façades, 2–10 ft | 25% | § 3.2.2.C |
    99→| Principal street, 10–30 ft above entry level | 25% | § 3.2.2.A.2 |
   100→| Principal-street ground-floor glazing — share with VT ≥ 0.6 | ≥ 50% | § 3.2.2.E |
   101→| UNO inhabited non-residential ground-level facing street | ≥ 70% | BCM 12.1.3(a) |
   102→| UNO inhabited residential ground-level facing street | ≥ 40% | BCM 12.1.3(a) |
   103→| Butler Shores WO adjacent to Town Lake parkland (2–10 ft) | ≥ 60% clear/lightly tinted | § 25-2-733(E)(1) |
   104→| North Shore Central WO park-visible non-residential (2–10 ft) | ≥ 60% clear/lightly tinted | § 25-2-738(F)(1) |
   105→| Waller Creek Pedestrian Activity Streetfront (2–10 ft) | ≥ 60% | Waller Creek District-Wide Standards |
   106→| Downtown Parks (DP) combining district, first-floor | VT ≥ 0.6, no glare | § 25-2-643(A)(1) |
   107→
   108→Reflectance limits: 20% general compatibility cap; HCR overlay bans mirrored glass >20% reflectance (§ 25-2-1126(B)); WO bans exterior mirrored or glare-producing glass at all floors (§ 25-2-721(E)(1)).
   109→
   110→### Articulation, basewall, step-back
   111→
   112→- WO: no façade unbroken >160 ft horizontal (§ 25-2-721(E)(4)); buildings >45 ft need distinctive top (§ 25-2-721(E)(2)); basewall ≤45 ft (35 ft south of Barton Springs or Riverside in Butler Shores / South Shore Central).
   113→- North Shore Central: 70° building envelope from a horizontal plane 45 ft above the property boundary nearest Town Lake, Shoal Creek, or Waller Creek (§ 25-2-738(E)).
   114→- NBG: façades >40 ft need material/color/texture change at 20–100 ft intervals or architectural elements; façades >100 ft on principal streets need a ≥24-in vertical plane change at 20–100 ft spacing (NBG 5.6.2); 6th-story-and-above step-back ≥30 ft from street-facing façade line (NBG 5.9.2).
   115→- Waller Creek: ≥55% of building mass above 90 ft must step back ≥8 ft.
   116→- Compatibility plan note required wherever compatibility is triggered: "Highly reflective materials will not be used. Materials may not exceed 20% reflectivity. This requirement shall not apply to solar panels or to copper or painted metal roofs."
   117→
   118→### Parking placement and structure design (Subchapter E § 2.2; CBD/DMU; UNO)
   119→
   120→- No parking between building and street on CTC, Urban Roadway, ICR, active edges, or corners (varies by regime).
   121→- Parking structures need headlight screening, crash wall, pedestrian-scale facade treatment, ground-floor activation, and architectural integration with the principal building.
   122→
   123→### Block circulation and large-site rules (Subchapter E § 2.2.5, § 2.3.1.B.2)
   124→
   125→- Sites ≥ 5 acres on CTC or Urban Roadway (any zoning), or ≥ 5 acres on Suburban/HCR (non-residential), must comply with internal block + ICR standards.
   126→- Max block size 5 acres; max block face 800 ft intersection-to-intersection.
   127→- ≥15-acre sites may have one block up to 10 acres per 30 acres of site area (800-ft face still applies).
   128→- Suburban residential-only >5 acres: exempt from § 2.2.5.A–G but internal block perimeter capped at 2,700 ft.
   129→- **Table B connectivity** (§ 2.3.1.B.2): non-residential ≥3 ac must satisfy ≥2 options; ≥3 options if surface parking >125% of Appendix A minimum.
   130→
   131→### Mechanical / refuse / screening (Subchapter E § 2.6)
   132→
   133→- Equipment, transformers, dumpsters must be screened from public streets, adjacent residential, and parkland.
   134→- Dumpster enclosures per City of Austin standard detail.
   135→- **AEC not available for § 2.6** — must comply or use Minor Modification.
   136→
   137→### Overlay-driven approval gates
   138→
   139→- **Waterfront Overlay** (any "-WO" suffix): PARD director sign-off (§ 25-2-721(A)(2)); Waterfront Planning Advisory Board recommendation; North Shore Central has 70° envelope and natural-materials rules; Rainey Street has 150-ft Lake / 50-ft Waller Creek setbacks (§ 25-2-739(B)); pedestrian-oriented use ≥ 50% of net usable ground floor adjacent to Town Lake in NSC, SSC, Auditorium Shores, Butler Shores, City Hall subdistricts (§ 25-2-692). Pedestrian-oriented uses are a **closed enumerated list** (§ 25-2-691(C)) — pedestrian-scale design alone does not qualify.
   140→- **Waller Creek District** (geographic, no zoning suffix): exempt from Subchapter E, requires Urban Design Division coordination + Waller Creek Design Group review.
   141→- **UNO**: BCM 12.1 articulation point system; § 25-2-759 ≥42% occupant space; Urban Design Division design guidelines compliance determined by NPZD director.
   142→- **Downtown Creeks (DC)**: within 60 ft of downtown creek centerlines on CBD/DMU; max height 60 ft; first-floor glass VT ≥ 0.6 (§ 25-2-643(E)).
   143→- **DDBP** (Downtown Density Bonus Program, § 25-2-586): pre-approval *before* site plan submittal for any FAR/height above base. Rainey enters DDBP only above 8:1 FAR or 350 ft (§ 25-2-739(C)(5)). DDBP = Downtown Density Bonus Program — never "Design Build Plan."
   144→- **TOD / NBG / ERC regulating plans**: each has its own Active Edge map, building placement, building design, AEC, and compatibility rules — read the plan, not Subchapter E.
   145→
   146→### CBD/DMU specifics
   147→
   148→- Max front and street-side yard setback 10 ft for first four stories above grade (§ 25-2-594) — i.e., build-to at the property line.
   149→
   150→### Pre-application meeting
   151→
   152→- Strongly advisable for any project with overlays, AEC pursuit, or large-site block circulation. Lock in principal-street designation, Subchapter E applicability/tier, and AEC path.
   153→- Required for AEC: concept plan ≥ 10 days before pre-app conference.
   154→
   155→## Opportunities to evaluate
   156→
   157→- **Site Plan Lite** — confirm against current § 25-5 use list and size caps. If eligible, saves ~3–6 months.
   158→- **Categorical Subchapter E exemption** — sites in NBG/ERC/Plaza Saltillo/East MLK/Lamar-Justin/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport Boulevard areas swap Subchapter E for the regulating plan; net effect often *more* design demand but a single coherent ruleset and clearer AEC pathways.
   159→- **Great Streets program participation** (downtown) — exempts site from CTC/Urban Roadway sidewalk + supplemental zone obligations under § 2.2.2.B and § 2.2.3.B; trade is the Great Streets streetscape build, often value-add for marketing.
   160→- **DDBP** — purchases FAR + height above base zoning entitlement in exchange for community benefits (affordability, open space). Plan early; gatekeeper requirements precede site plan.
   161→- **Minor Modification** (Subchapter E § 1.4) — up to 10% deviation from any numeric Subchapter E standard; up to 20% to protect a natural feature; unlimited to preserve a Heritage Tree. Director-approved in writing — much faster than AEC.
   162→- **AEC** (§ 1.5) — alternative equivalent compliance for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, Article 3. Not available for § 2.4 entrances or § 2.6 screening. Needs concept plan ≥10 days pre-app; expires 3 yr (one 1-yr ext).
   163→- **Industrial / warehouse off-CTC exemption** — confirm GFA breakdown and CTC status; full Subchapter E exemption available if criteria met.
   164→- **PUD** — if site is in a PUD, PUD standards govern *to the extent of conflict*; can selectively avoid specific Subchapter E provisions but doesn't categorically exempt.
   165→- **Mueller PUD** — categorically exempt from Subchapter E (§ 1.2.4.A.5) and Subchapter F (§ 1.3.2); governed by Mueller Design Book.
   166→- **ERC Hubs (Figure 1-6)** — exempt from ERC compatibility (§ 4.2.4) and eligible for ERC development bonus (Article 6).
   167→- **VMU / DB90 / DBETOD / Affordability Unlocked overlays** (cross-reference `zlu`) — affect setbacks/height that interact with build-to and parking placement. Pull from `programs.md`.
   168→
   169→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   170→
   171→- **zoning-pathway.md** (`zlu`) — base district, all combining/overlay districts (WO, HCR, DC, UNO suffixes), regulating plan area (NBG/ERC/TOD/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport), CTC frontage flag, PUD status, vested-rights determinations.
   172→- **programs.md** — Site Plan Lite eligibility check, DDBP eligibility, Great Streets boundary check, Mueller PUD check, ERC Hub check, density bonus stack (DB90, DBETOD, VMU, AU).
   173→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — net site area; building GFA + per-use GFA breakdown (especially for industrial/warehouse exemption test); proposed building footprint and frontage occupation %; entrance location(s); curb cuts / drive aisles; parking count + structure type; rough massing (basewall height, total height, step-back assumptions); planned use mix (commercial vs. residential vs. industrial).
   174→- **adjacent_context** (surveyor) — abutting street classifications (ASMP level, named-corridor segment match), adjacent zoning (compatibility triggers), parkland adjacency, creek adjacency.
   175→- **property_profile** (surveyor COA GIS) — regulating plan layers, CTC layer, etod-subdistricts layer, parkland-deficient layer, watershed regulation areas, historic district intersect.
   176→
   177→## Output structure
   178→
   179→Standard discipline output shape. See `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.
   180→
   181→## Severity heuristics
   182→
   183→| Finding | Severity |
   184→|---|---|
   185→| Site falls within categorically exempt regulating plan (NBG/ERC/TOD/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport Blvd) and applicant has not loaded the alternate ruleset | `significant` (re-plan required) |
   186→| Project triggers commission-level review or DDBP gatekeeper not yet engaged | `significant` (3–6 mo schedule + public-hearing risk) |
   187→| Principal street is a CTC segment that owner has misidentified or missed | `significant` (build-to, parking, entrance all change) |
   188→| Build-to % unmet on principal street | `significant` (form fix typically requires re-massing) |
   189→| Entrance placement violates § 2.4 — no AEC path available | `significant` |
   190→| WO subdistrict triggers PARD sign-off, WPAB review, or pedestrian-oriented-use 50% rule not factored | `significant` |
   191→| North Shore Central 70° envelope or Rainey 150/50 ft setbacks reduce buildable envelope | `significant` |
   192→| Mechanical / refuse screening missing from concept (cannot AEC § 2.6) | `moderate` |
   193→| Glazing %, VT, articulation, basewall step-back deviations within Minor Modification (≤10%) | `moderate` (path exists) |
   194→| Large site (≥ 5 ac) on CTC/Urban Roadway needs internal block + ICR + Table B layout | `moderate` |
   195→| Active Edge designation on a frontage drives 100% build-to and active-use mandate | `moderate` to `significant` |
   196→| Site Plan Lite eligibility (confirmed against use list + size caps) | `opportunity` |
   197→| Great Streets participation available for downtown sites | `opportunity` |
   198→| DDBP, ERC Bonus, Mueller PUD, off-CTC industrial exemption available | `opportunity` |
   199→| Project triggers permit-only path, no site plan required | `note` (favorable) |
   200→| Principal-street designation ambiguous on multi-frontage site | `data-gap` |
   201→| Subchapter E applicability tier (Full vs Partial) not determinable from facts | `data-gap` |
   202→| Active Edge designation cannot be confirmed without regulating plan map reference | `data-gap` |
   203→
   204→## Common pitfalls
   205→
   206→- **Treating "PUD" as a blanket Subchapter E exemption.** PUD supersedes only to the extent of conflict (§ 1.2.5.B.2.g). Provisions the PUD is silent on (often § 2.5 lighting, § 2.6 screening, Article 3 building design) still apply.
   207→- **Citing § 1.2.4.A.12 exemption while still loading Subchapter E notes on the cover sheet.** If the site is in NBG/ERC/TOD/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport Blvd, all Subchapter E references must be removed and the regulating plan loaded instead.
   208→- **Claiming the industrial / warehouse exemption without verifying CTC status and GFA breakdown.** Both exemptions vanish on a CTC. Warehouse exemption needs <25% non-industrial GFA per building, documented.
   209→- **Asserting Chapter 245 vested rights without a Director-issued Vested Rights Determination letter** (§ 25-1-541). Even with a valid VRD, Subchapter E design standards still apply.
   210→- **Pursuing AEC for § 2.4 entrances or § 2.6 screening.** Categorically unavailable; must comply or use Minor Modification.
   211→- **Building to 50% on a CTC** because of an outdated 50% reference. CTC build-to is 75% in current Subchapter E and current regulating plans.
   212→- **Confusing principal street with frontages.** Principal street drives build-to, parking, entrance; *every* abutting frontage drives its own sidewalk + supplemental zone (§ 2.2.1.B).
   213→- **Missing the 75-ft entrance interval long-wall treatment.** Not a hard fail but adds substantial façade cost that should be budgeted at concept.
   214→- **Designating Active Edge from project narrative alone.** Confirm against the regulating plan figure (NBG Fig 1-2; ERC Fig 1-4; Plaza Saltillo / East MLK / Lamar-Justin Fig 2-1).
   215→- **Misidentifying admin-eligible projects as commission-required, or vice versa.** Build a defensible reading at concept; budget commission timeline if any waiver is contemplated.
   216→- **Missing WO subdistrict-specific rules** (Butler Shores 60% glazing facing Town Lake parkland; North Shore Central 70° envelope; Rainey 150/50 ft setbacks). All "-WO" sites get general WO; subdistrict overlays stack on top.
   217→- **Treating "pedestrian-scale" design as satisfying "pedestrian-oriented use."** The latter is a closed list in § 25-2-691(C).
   218→- **Skipping pre-application meeting on overlay-heavy sites.** Cheapest insurance against late-stage staff reinterpretation.
   219→- **Expanding DDBP as "Downtown Design Build Plan."** It is "Downtown Density Bonus Program" (§ 25-2-586(A)(1)).
   220→- **Confusing site plan with building permit.** Site plan establishes the envelope (build-to, entrance, sidewalk, screening); building permit follows and inherits.
   221→

# Site Development / Use / Form Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

The bridge between zoning (`zlu`) and engineering (`sde`). Covers (1) whether the project triggers a site plan under LDC Chapter 25-5 and which procedural path (administrative vs. commission vs. Site Plan Lite); (2) site-and-building form requirements under LDC Subchapter E and any superseding regulating plan (NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD, Waller Creek District, Downtown Austin Plan, Airport Boulevard Corridor); (3) frontage build-to, entrance orientation, transparency/glazing, articulation, screening, and streetscape (clear/planting/supplemental zones); (4) overlay-driven design review (Waterfront Overlay, UNO, Downtown Creeks, DDBP/Design Commission).

Boundary with neighbors: zoning entitlement (FAR, height, base use) lives in `zlu`; civil/engineering envelope (drainage, water/wastewater, ESC) lives in `sde`; this guide covers the urban-form contract the project signs at site plan.

## Authoritative sources

- LDC Chapter 25-5 — Site plan procedures, classifications, exemptions
- LDC Chapter 25-2, Subchapter E — Design Standards and Mixed Use (Article 1 applicability; Article 2 site; Article 3 building; Article 4 VMU; Article 5 CTC definitions)
- LDC § 25-2-721 et seq. — Waterfront Overlay general + 16 subdistricts (§ 25-2-738 North Shore Central; § 25-2-739 Rainey; § 25-2-733 Butler Shores)
- LDC § 25-2-586 — Downtown Density Bonus Program (DDBP)
- LDC § 25-2-167, § 25-2-643 — Downtown Creeks Combining District
- LDC § 25-2-753 et seq. + BCM 12.1 — University Neighborhood Overlay (UNO)
- ERC Regulating Plan (LDC § 25-2-149) — Articles 1–6
- NBG, Plaza Saltillo TOD, East MLK TOD, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD Regulating Plans
- Waller Creek District Design Guidelines
- Great Streets Master Plan (downtown program)
- City of Austin Standard Details — street furniture, sidewalk, dumpster enclosure

## Regulatory pathway

| Procedural path | Trigger | Decision body | Typical timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Building permit only — no site plan | Single-family / duplex on existing platted lot; interior remodel; ADA sidewalk projects; specific § 25-5 exemptions | DSD plan review | 4–8 wk |
| **Site Plan Lite** (single-family, two-family, small commercial) | Eligible small projects under § 25-5; specific use list and size caps | Administrative (DSD) | 8–12 wk |
| **Administrative site plan** (standard) | Default for most commercial / mixed-use / multifamily not requiring waivers | DSD staff | 6–9 mo from intake to release; 3+ rounds of comments common |
| **Commission site plan** | Variances from § 25-5 standards; certain conditional uses; some overlays | Land Use Commission / Planning Commission | 9–14 mo; public hearing required |
| **Design Commission / DDBP review** | Downtown DDBP bonus projects; certain Great Streets sites | Design Commission (advisory) + DDBP gatekeeper | Add 2–4 mo *before* site plan submittal |
| **Waterfront Planning Advisory Board** | Any site plan in a WO subdistrict | Director requests recommendation per § 25-5-143(C) | Add 1–2 mo |
| **PARD director sign-off** | Required for every site plan in WO | PARD director (§ 25-2-721(A)(2)) | Concurrent with admin site plan |
| **AEC (Alternative Equivalent Compliance)** | Numeric Subchapter E deviation beyond Minor Modification scope; only for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, Article 3 | Director-approved concept plan | Concept plan due ≥ 10 days before pre-app; expires 3 yr (one 1-yr extension) |

Site plan is the **envelope contract**; building permit follows and inherits the approved site plan's site form. Don't confuse the two — building permit alone cannot fix a site-plan-level form non-compliance.

## Constraints to evaluate

### Site plan trigger and path

- **Verify site plan is required at all**. Pure interior remodel and certain minor projects are permit-only under § 25-5 exemptions. For everything commercial/multifamily/MU expect a site plan.
- **Site Plan Lite eligibility** is restrictive and tied to a specific use list and size caps — don't assume eligibility from project narrative; confirm against the current § 25-5 Lite list before factoring the shorter timeline.
- **Commission-level escalation** is triggered by waivers from § 25-5 standards (e.g., compatibility, parking, access). Identify the waivers needed at concept stage — every commission item adds 3–6 months and public-hearing risk.

### Subchapter E applicability and compliance tier (LDC Subchapter E, § 1.2)

- Subchapter E applies if (a) project requires a site plan under Chapter 25-5, (b) site is **not** in a categorically exempt regulating plan area, and (c) the specific standard is triggered by the project's principal street type per Table A.
- **Categorically exempt regulating plans** (§ 1.2.4.A.12): NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo TOD, East MLK TOD, Lamar/Justin Lane TOD, Waller Creek District, Downtown Austin Plan, Airport Boulevard Corridor Plan. These plans *each impose their own* form standards — exemption from Subchapter E ≠ exemption from form rules.
- **Other carve-outs:** AG, AV, TN zoning, UNO (§ 1.2.4.A.2–3); industrial uses *only when not on a CTC* (§ 1.2.4.A.6); warehouse with <25% non-industrial GFA *only when not on a CTC* (§ 1.2.4.A.9). PUD supersedes Subchapter E only to the extent of conflict (§ 1.2.5.B.2.g) — PUD silence ≠ exemption.
- **Compliance tier:** Full Compliance (§ 1.2.2) for new construction on undeveloped land or full-demo redevelopment; Partial Compliance (§ 1.2.3) for additions / Level 3 remodels >50% work-area where principal-street façade is remodeled. Partial Compliance allows existing-condition waivers; document on cover sheet.

### Principal street hierarchy (Subchapter E § 2.1)

Principal street priority: **CTC > Internal Circulation Route > Urban Roadway > Suburban Roadway > Highway/Hill Country Roadway**. Determines build-to %, glazing %, entrance orientation, and parking-placement restrictions. **Sidewalk and supplemental zone standards apply to all abutting frontages** independently (§ 2.2.1.B), each governed by its own roadway type.

- 20 enumerated CTC segments; CTC is defined by name **and** segment limits — confirm the parcel falls within stated geographic endpoints, not just on the named street.
- Sites with frontage on multiple equal-class streets: Director designates principal based on transit service; if equal/absent, owner designates.

### Build-to / frontage occupation

Net Frontage Length (NFL) = lot line minus ICR ROW, compatibility setbacks, easements, drive aisles, sidewalks, and stairs at building perimeter. Parking structures, canopies, accessory structures **do not count** toward build-to.

| Frontage type | Build-to (min % of NFL) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Subchapter E CTC | 75% | Subchapter E § 2.2.2 |
| Subchapter E Urban Roadway | 40% | Subchapter E § 2.2.3 |
| NBG / ERC Active Edge | 100% | NBG 5.8 / ERC 5.6 |
| NBG / ERC CTC (basic) | 75% | NBG 4.3.3 / ERC 4.3.3 |
| NBG / ERC Pedestrian Priority Collector | 75% | NBG 4.3.3 / ERC 4.3.3 |
| NBG / ERC Urban Roadway (basic) | 50% | NBG 4.3.3 / ERC 4.3.3 |
| TOD CTC (Plaza Saltillo / East MLK) | 75% | TOD plan 4.3.3 |
| TOD Pedestrian Priority Street | 50% | TOD plan 4.3.3 |
| TOD Local Street | 40% | TOD plan 4.3.3 |

No 80% tier exists in current ERC/NBG/TOD plans — outdated references should be treated with suspicion.

### Building entrance (Subchapter E § 2.4)

- ≥1 customer entrance must face the principal street and connect directly to the clear or supplemental zone via an unobstructed exterior path.
- Each separate ground-floor commercial tenant along the principal-street elevation needs its own entrance.
- Advisory 75-ft entrance interval (§ 2.4.B.2): exceeding triggers long-wall pedestrian treatment (shade, glazing, articulation, awnings) — not a hard violation but is a real cost.
- Non-street-facing entrance exception (§ 2.4.B.1(a)–(d)) requires **all four** conditions: ≥80% NFL built to clear/supplemental zone; continuous shaded sidewalk principal-street→entrance; entrance within 100 ft of street-facing façade line; shade trees ≤30 ft o.c. between building and any parking.
- **AEC is not available for § 2.4 entry requirements** (§ 1.5.2). Plan the entrance correctly at concept; you cannot buy a deviation later.

### Sidewalk: clear / planting / supplemental zones (Subchapter E § 2.2)

- Three-zone system: planting (curb-adjacent, trees + utilities) → clear (unobstructed pedestrian travel) → optional supplemental (active uses adjacent to building face).
- Widths vary by principal street class; dimensions must be labeled on site + landscape plan, at narrowest point where variable.
- Build-to can be satisfied at edge of properly designated supplemental zone rather than clear zone.
- Great Streets program participation exempts downtown sites (bounded by MLK, Lady Bird Lake, IH-35, Lamar) from CTC/Urban Roadway sidewalk + supplemental zone standards per § 2.2.2.B and § 2.2.3.B — but Great Streets has its own (typically richer) streetscape spec.

### Ground-floor transparency / glazing (Subchapter E § 3.2)

| Condition | Min glazing | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Principal street, 2–10 ft above grade (non-residential, Sub. E) | 40% | § 3.2.2.A.1 |
| Other street-facing façades, 2–10 ft | 25% | § 3.2.2.C |
| Principal street, 10–30 ft above entry level | 25% | § 3.2.2.A.2 |
| Principal-street ground-floor glazing — share with VT ≥ 0.6 | ≥ 50% | § 3.2.2.E |
| UNO inhabited non-residential ground-level facing street | ≥ 70% | BCM 12.1.3(a) |
| UNO inhabited residential ground-level facing street | ≥ 40% | BCM 12.1.3(a) |
| Butler Shores WO adjacent to Town Lake parkland (2–10 ft) | ≥ 60% clear/lightly tinted | § 25-2-733(E)(1) |
| North Shore Central WO park-visible non-residential (2–10 ft) | ≥ 60% clear/lightly tinted | § 25-2-738(F)(1) |
| Waller Creek Pedestrian Activity Streetfront (2–10 ft) | ≥ 60% | Waller Creek District-Wide Standards |
| Downtown Parks (DP) combining district, first-floor | VT ≥ 0.6, no glare | § 25-2-643(A)(1) |

Reflectance limits: 20% general compatibility cap; HCR overlay bans mirrored glass >20% reflectance (§ 25-2-1126(B)); WO bans exterior mirrored or glare-producing glass at all floors (§ 25-2-721(E)(1)).

### Articulation, basewall, step-back

- WO: no façade unbroken >160 ft horizontal (§ 25-2-721(E)(4)); buildings >45 ft need distinctive top (§ 25-2-721(E)(2)); basewall ≤45 ft (35 ft south of Barton Springs or Riverside in Butler Shores / South Shore Central).
- North Shore Central: 70° building envelope from a horizontal plane 45 ft above the property boundary nearest Town Lake, Shoal Creek, or Waller Creek (§ 25-2-738(E)).
- NBG: façades >40 ft need material/color/texture change at 20–100 ft intervals or architectural elements; façades >100 ft on principal streets need a ≥24-in vertical plane change at 20–100 ft spacing (NBG 5.6.2); 6th-story-and-above step-back ≥30 ft from street-facing façade line (NBG 5.9.2).
- Waller Creek: ≥55% of building mass above 90 ft must step back ≥8 ft.
- Compatibility plan note required wherever compatibility is triggered: "Highly reflective materials will not be used. Materials may not exceed 20% reflectivity. This requirement shall not apply to solar panels or to copper or painted metal roofs."

### Parking placement and structure design (Subchapter E § 2.2; CBD/DMU; UNO)

- No parking between building and street on CTC, Urban Roadway, ICR, active edges, or corners (varies by regime).
- Parking structures need headlight screening, crash wall, pedestrian-scale facade treatment, ground-floor activation, and architectural integration with the principal building.

### Block circulation and large-site rules (Subchapter E § 2.2.5, § 2.3.1.B.2)

- Sites ≥ 5 acres on CTC or Urban Roadway (any zoning), or ≥ 5 acres on Suburban/HCR (non-residential), must comply with internal block + ICR standards.
- Max block size 5 acres; max block face 800 ft intersection-to-intersection.
- ≥15-acre sites may have one block up to 10 acres per 30 acres of site area (800-ft face still applies).
- Suburban residential-only >5 acres: exempt from § 2.2.5.A–G but internal block perimeter capped at 2,700 ft.
- **Table B connectivity** (§ 2.3.1.B.2): non-residential ≥3 ac must satisfy ≥2 options; ≥3 options if surface parking >125% of Appendix A minimum.

### Mechanical / refuse / screening (Subchapter E § 2.6)

- Equipment, transformers, dumpsters must be screened from public streets, adjacent residential, and parkland.
- Dumpster enclosures per City of Austin standard detail.
- **AEC not available for § 2.6** — must comply or use Minor Modification.

### Overlay-driven approval gates

- **Waterfront Overlay** (any "-WO" suffix): PARD director sign-off (§ 25-2-721(A)(2)); Waterfront Planning Advisory Board recommendation; North Shore Central has 70° envelope and natural-materials rules; Rainey Street has 150-ft Lake / 50-ft Waller Creek setbacks (§ 25-2-739(B)); pedestrian-oriented use ≥ 50% of net usable ground floor adjacent to Town Lake in NSC, SSC, Auditorium Shores, Butler Shores, City Hall subdistricts (§ 25-2-692). Pedestrian-oriented uses are a **closed enumerated list** (§ 25-2-691(C)) — pedestrian-scale design alone does not qualify.
- **Waller Creek District** (geographic, no zoning suffix): exempt from Subchapter E, requires Urban Design Division coordination + Waller Creek Design Group review.
- **UNO**: BCM 12.1 articulation point system; § 25-2-759 ≥42% occupant space; Urban Design Division design guidelines compliance determined by NPZD director.
- **Downtown Creeks (DC)**: within 60 ft of downtown creek centerlines on CBD/DMU; max height 60 ft; first-floor glass VT ≥ 0.6 (§ 25-2-643(E)).
- **DDBP** (Downtown Density Bonus Program, § 25-2-586): pre-approval *before* site plan submittal for any FAR/height above base. Rainey enters DDBP only above 8:1 FAR or 350 ft (§ 25-2-739(C)(5)). DDBP = Downtown Density Bonus Program — never "Design Build Plan."
- **TOD / NBG / ERC regulating plans**: each has its own Active Edge map, building placement, building design, AEC, and compatibility rules — read the plan, not Subchapter E.

### CBD/DMU specifics

- Max front and street-side yard setback 10 ft for first four stories above grade (§ 25-2-594) — i.e., build-to at the property line.

### Pre-application meeting

- Strongly advisable for any project with overlays, AEC pursuit, or large-site block circulation. Lock in principal-street designation, Subchapter E applicability/tier, and AEC path.
- Required for AEC: concept plan ≥ 10 days before pre-app conference.

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **Site Plan Lite** — confirm against current § 25-5 use list and size caps. If eligible, saves ~3–6 months.
- **Categorical Subchapter E exemption** — sites in NBG/ERC/Plaza Saltillo/East MLK/Lamar-Justin/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport Boulevard areas swap Subchapter E for the regulating plan; net effect often *more* design demand but a single coherent ruleset and clearer AEC pathways.
- **Great Streets program participation** (downtown) — exempts site from CTC/Urban Roadway sidewalk + supplemental zone obligations under § 2.2.2.B and § 2.2.3.B; trade is the Great Streets streetscape build, often value-add for marketing.
- **DDBP** — purchases FAR + height above base zoning entitlement in exchange for community benefits (affordability, open space). Plan early; gatekeeper requirements precede site plan.
- **Minor Modification** (Subchapter E § 1.4) — up to 10% deviation from any numeric Subchapter E standard; up to 20% to protect a natural feature; unlimited to preserve a Heritage Tree. Director-approved in writing — much faster than AEC.
- **AEC** (§ 1.5) — alternative equivalent compliance for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, Article 3. Not available for § 2.4 entrances or § 2.6 screening. Needs concept plan ≥10 days pre-app; expires 3 yr (one 1-yr ext).
- **Industrial / warehouse off-CTC exemption** — confirm GFA breakdown and CTC status; full Subchapter E exemption available if criteria met.
- **PUD** — if site is in a PUD, PUD standards govern *to the extent of conflict*; can selectively avoid specific Subchapter E provisions but doesn't categorically exempt.
- **Mueller PUD** — categorically exempt from Subchapter E (§ 1.2.4.A.5) and Subchapter F (§ 1.3.2); governed by Mueller Design Book.
- **ERC Hubs (Figure 1-6)** — exempt from ERC compatibility (§ 4.2.4) and eligible for ERC development bonus (Article 6).
- **VMU / DB90 / DBETOD / Affordability Unlocked overlays** (cross-reference `zlu`) — affect setbacks/height that interact with build-to and parking placement. Pull from `programs.md`.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **zoning-pathway.md** (`zlu`) — base district, all combining/overlay districts (WO, HCR, DC, UNO suffixes), regulating plan area (NBG/ERC/TOD/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport), CTC frontage flag, PUD status, vested-rights determinations.
- **programs.md** — Site Plan Lite eligibility check, DDBP eligibility, Great Streets boundary check, Mueller PUD check, ERC Hub check, density bonus stack (DB90, DBETOD, VMU, AU).
- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — net site area; building GFA + per-use GFA breakdown (especially for industrial/warehouse exemption test); proposed building footprint and frontage occupation %; entrance location(s); curb cuts / drive aisles; parking count + structure type; rough massing (basewall height, total height, step-back assumptions); planned use mix (commercial vs. residential vs. industrial).
- **adjacent_context** (surveyor) — abutting street classifications (ASMP level, named-corridor segment match), adjacent zoning (compatibility triggers), parkland adjacency, creek adjacency.
- **property_profile** (surveyor COA GIS) — regulating plan layers, CTC layer, etod-subdistricts layer, parkland-deficient layer, watershed regulation areas, historic district intersect.

## Output structure

Standard discipline output shape. See `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.

## Severity heuristics

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| Site falls within categorically exempt regulating plan (NBG/ERC/TOD/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport Blvd) and applicant has not loaded the alternate ruleset | `significant` (re-plan required) |
| Project triggers commission-level review or DDBP gatekeeper not yet engaged | `significant` (3–6 mo schedule + public-hearing risk) |
| Principal street is a CTC segment that owner has misidentified or missed | `significant` (build-to, parking, entrance all change) |
| Build-to % unmet on principal street | `significant` (form fix typically requires re-massing) |
| Entrance placement violates § 2.4 — no AEC path available | `significant` |
| WO subdistrict triggers PARD sign-off, WPAB review, or pedestrian-oriented-use 50% rule not factored | `significant` |
| North Shore Central 70° envelope or Rainey 150/50 ft setbacks reduce buildable envelope | `significant` |
| Mechanical / refuse screening missing from concept (cannot AEC § 2.6) | `moderate` |
| Glazing %, VT, articulation, basewall step-back deviations within Minor Modification (≤10%) | `moderate` (path exists) |
| Large site (≥ 5 ac) on CTC/Urban Roadway needs internal block + ICR + Table B layout | `moderate` |
| Active Edge designation on a frontage drives 100% build-to and active-use mandate | `moderate` to `significant` |
| Site Plan Lite eligibility (confirmed against use list + size caps) | `opportunity` |
| Great Streets participation available for downtown sites | `opportunity` |
| DDBP, ERC Bonus, Mueller PUD, off-CTC industrial exemption available | `opportunity` |
| Project triggers permit-only path, no site plan required | `note` (favorable) |
| Principal-street designation ambiguous on multi-frontage site | `data-gap` |
| Subchapter E applicability tier (Full vs Partial) not determinable from facts | `data-gap` |
| Active Edge designation cannot be confirmed without regulating plan map reference | `data-gap` |

## Common pitfalls

- **Treating "PUD" as a blanket Subchapter E exemption.** PUD supersedes only to the extent of conflict (§ 1.2.5.B.2.g). Provisions the PUD is silent on (often § 2.5 lighting, § 2.6 screening, Article 3 building design) still apply.
- **Citing § 1.2.4.A.12 exemption while still loading Subchapter E notes on the cover sheet.** If the site is in NBG/ERC/TOD/Waller Creek/Downtown/Airport Blvd, all Subchapter E references must be removed and the regulating plan loaded instead.
- **Claiming the industrial / warehouse exemption without verifying CTC status and GFA breakdown.** Both exemptions vanish on a CTC. Warehouse exemption needs <25% non-industrial GFA per building, documented.
- **Asserting Chapter 245 vested rights without a Director-issued Vested Rights Determination letter** (§ 25-1-541). Even with a valid VRD, Subchapter E design standards still apply.
- **Pursuing AEC for § 2.4 entrances or § 2.6 screening.** Categorically unavailable; must comply or use Minor Modification.
- **Building to 50% on a CTC** because of an outdated 50% reference. CTC build-to is 75% in current Subchapter E and current regulating plans.
- **Confusing principal street with frontages.** Principal street drives build-to, parking, entrance; *every* abutting frontage drives its own sidewalk + supplemental zone (§ 2.2.1.B).
- **Missing the 75-ft entrance interval long-wall treatment.** Not a hard fail but adds substantial façade cost that should be budgeted at concept.
- **Designating Active Edge from project narrative alone.** Confirm against the regulating plan figure (NBG Fig 1-2; ERC Fig 1-4; Plaza Saltillo / East MLK / Lamar-Justin Fig 2-1).
- **Misidentifying admin-eligible projects as commission-required, or vice versa.** Build a defensible reading at concept; budget commission timeline if any waiver is contemplated.
- **Missing WO subdistrict-specific rules** (Butler Shores 60% glazing facing Town Lake parkland; North Shore Central 70° envelope; Rainey 150/50 ft setbacks). All "-WO" sites get general WO; subdistrict overlays stack on top.
- **Treating "pedestrian-scale" design as satisfying "pedestrian-oriented use."** The latter is a closed list in § 25-2-691(C).
- **Skipping pre-application meeting on overlay-heavy sites.** Cheapest insurance against late-stage staff reinterpretation.
- **Expanding DDBP as "Downtown Design Build Plan."** It is "Downtown Density Bonus Program" (§ 25-2-586(A)(1)).
- **Confusing site plan with building permit.** Site plan establishes the envelope (build-to, entrance, sidewalk, screening); building permit follows and inherits.

     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Base zoning district, combining districts and overlays (CO, MU, V/VMU, ETOD, NCCD, UNO, WO, CVC, ERC, TODs, HCRC, AO, NBG, DB90), conditional and special use processes, use classification under LDC Chapter 25-2, dimensional standards (height, FAR, building coverage, impervious cover, site area per unit), Compatibility Standards (Article 10), parking, density bonus programs, and site plan procedural path. Excludes site engineering (sde), site form (sduf), environmental layers (el/eptp/fwp/sde), transportation (ta), and wastewater/water (wwp) even where coded in Chapter 25-2 or Subchapter E.

     7→## Authoritative sources
     8→
     9→- **Land Development Code (LDC), Chapter 25** — Austin Municode. Most-cited chapters: 25-1 (definitions, applications), 25-2 (zoning), 25-5 (site plan), 25-6 (parking and ROW), 25-8 (environmental), 25-13 (airport).
    10→- **Subchapter E (Design Standards & Mixed Use)** — design standards, connectivity, VMU, AEC.
    11→- **Subchapter B, Article 2** — PUD framework.
    12→- **General Site Plan Notes for COA (DSD)** — required notes, signature blocks, forms; modification prohibited.
    13→- **Zoning map (COA GIS, "zoning" layer)** — base district + suffixes. Zoning strings are compound: `GR-MU-CO-NP-DB90` = General Retail + Mixed Use + Conditional Overlay + Neighborhood Plan + DB90 density bonus.
    14→- **Adopted overlays (COA GIS layers)** — CVC, Capitol Dominance, Hill Country Roadway, AO-1/2/3 (Airport), WO subdistricts, NCCD ordinances, TODs (NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane), UNO, ETOD subdistricts.
    15→- **AMANDA / DSD permit system** — case history, prior approvals, vested rights determinations.
    16→- **Imagine Austin (comp plan) / Future Land Use Map** — *policy, not regulatory.* FLUM does not establish zoning; zoning changes require LDC § 25-2-281 rezoning.
    17→
    18→## Regulatory pathway
    19→
    20→| Path | Trigger | Timeline | Decision body |
    21→|---|---|---|---|
    22→| Administrative site plan approval (Director) | Site plan complies with all title requirements; no commission action required | 6–12 months from intake through release | DSD Director (LDC § 25-5-112) |
    23→| Conditional use permit | Use is "C" in district use table (§ 25-2-491), incl. Large Retail (≥100,000 sf, § 25-2-815), late-hours cocktail lounge, etc. | 4–9 months before site plan can be finalized | Land Use Commission / Planning Commission (LDC § 25-5-142) |
    24→| Rezoning (incl. site-specific Article 10 amendment) | Proposed use prohibited in base district, or modification of Article 10 height/buffer | 6–12 months | P&Z recommendation → City Council |
    25→| BOA variance | Hardship from a dimensional standard (setback, parking, fence) | 3–6 months | Board of Adjustment (LDC §§ 25-2-472, 25-2-474) |
    26→| Density bonus (DDBP, DB90, ETOD, VMU, AU, NBG, Plaza Saltillo, ERC) | Site is eligible per program-specific maps + affordability/community-benefit compliance | Concurrent with site plan (DDBP must be **approved before site plan submittal** per § 25-2-586(H)) | DSD Director (DDBP); NHCD/HPD (others) |
    27→| Alternative Equivalent Compliance (AEC) | Subchapter E deviation; available only for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, and Article 3 | 1–4 months | Director (concept plan); expires 3 years from approval |
    28→| F1/F2 staged site plan | DSD administrative practice for large multifamily/mixed-use: F1 = horizontal, F2 = vertical | Two separate case numbers, sequential approvals | DSD (no Planning Commission or phasing fees) |
    29→| Formal § 25-5-21 phased site plan | Single case number with phasing plan; final-phase start >3 years post-approval → Planning Commission | Adds 2–4 months if PC required | DSD Director or Planning Commission |
    30→| Site plan correction / minor revision to released plan | LDC § 25-5-61(C)–(D): no significant effect, ROW relocation, or ADA | 1–3 months | Director (written approval) |
    31→
    32→Site plan approval is valid **3 years from date of approval** (LDC § 25-5-81(B)), extendable by issued building permits or active site work.
    33→
    34→## Constraints to evaluate
    35→
    36→### Use compatibility
    37→
    38→- **Confirm proposed use against base district use table** (§ 25-2-491). Use the **exact LDC name** from Chapters 25-2-3 through 25-2-6 (residential, commercial, industrial, civic). "Office," "Retail," "Restaurant," "School" alone are insufficient.
    39→- **Restaurant (General)** (§ 25-2-4(B)(64)) requires ≥51% gross income from prepared food (§ 25-2-808(B)(1)); below that, the use reclassifies to **Cocktail Lounge** (conditional, LUC approval required).
    40→- **Large Retail** (≥100,000 sf of any single enumerated use including its accessory uses, § 25-2-815) is a conditional use requiring Land Use Commission approval.
    41→- **LR (Neighborhood Commercial) restrictions** (§ 25-2-587): Restaurant (General) ≤4,000 sf, 7 a.m.–11 p.m. hours, no drive-through; General Retail (General) ≤5,000 sf, no local-street access; no outdoor entertainment or amplified sound.
    42→- **Multifamily in CS** requires MU overlay or rezone.
    43→- **W/LO** requires ≥20% of GFA or 1,000 sf (lesser) as office facing the primary street (§ 25-2-584).
    44→- **Civic use chapter** — schools, child care, adult care, community recreation are in § 25-2-6, NOT § 25-2-3 or 25-2-4. Common misclassification.
    45→
    46→### Dimensional envelope (zoning capacity table)
    47→
    48→Building Austin's zoning capacity table requires the **base district from § 25-2-492** *plus* every overlay/combining-district modifier. Selected base district maxima:
    49→
    50→| District | Use list (representative) | Max height | Max FAR | Max IC | Min parking (post-Nov 2023) |
    51→|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    52→| SF-3 / SF-5 / SF-6 | SF, duplex (SF-3+), 2/3-unit (SF-3+) | 35 ft | none | 40% / 45% / 50% (varies) | None citywide |
    53→| MF-1 / MF-2 / MF-3 / MF-4 / MF-5 / MF-6 | Multifamily, condo, townhouse, group residential | 40 / 40 (3 stry) / 40 / 60 / 60 / 90 ft | none / none / 0.75:1 / 0.75:1 / 1:1 / none | 45–70% | None citywide |
    54→| NO / LO / GO | Office sub-tiers | 35 / 40 (3 stry) / 60 ft | 0.35 / 0.7 / 1:1 | 50 / 70 / 80% | None citywide |
    55→| LR | Neighborhood commercial (capped uses) | 40 ft (3 stry) | 0.5:1 | 80% | None citywide |
    56→| GR | General commercial | 60 ft | 1:1 | 90% | None citywide |
    57→| CS / CS-1 | Commercial services | 60 ft | 2:1 | 95% | None citywide |
    58→| CH | Commercial highway | 60 ft (per § 25-2-582) | 3:1 | 95% | None citywide |
    59→| DMU | Downtown mixed use | 120 ft (8:1 with DDBP) | 5:1 | 100% | None citywide |
    60→| CBD | Central business district | 350 ft | 8:1 | 100% | None citywide |
    61→| IP / LI / MI / R&D | Industrial sub-tiers | 60 / 60 / 120 / 60 ft | 1:1 | 80% | None citywide |
    62→| LA | Lake Austin | 35 ft | none | per § 25-2-551 | None citywide |
    63→
    64→**Citywide parking minimums were eliminated November 13, 2023** by Ord. No. 20231102-028 (LDC § 25-6-471(A)). Exceptions: (1) PUDs with parking exhibits in their ordinance (e.g., Goodnight Ranch Exhibit J) continue to control; (2) UNO sets a 60% **maximum ceiling** (not minimum) on Appendix A; (3) accessibility (ADA) spaces still required. The repeal also abolished the "Type CT" plan designation and the mandatory shower-facility requirement under § 25-6-478(D)(1).
    65→
    66→**Where IC, FAR, height, and coverage are calculated:**
    67→
    68→- **FAR = GFA ÷ Gross Site Area** (§§ 25-1-21(43), (48)). GSA is the full unmodified site area — no deductions for floodplain, CWQZ, slopes, or environmental overlays.
    69→- **GFA** (§ 25-1-21(47)) includes loading docks, excludes atria airspace, parking, driveways, enclosed loading berths. The bulk-purpose GFA differs from parking-calculation GFA (which additionally excludes bike rooms and showers per § 25-6-472(C)) — don't conflate.
    70→- **Building coverage** (§ 25-1-21(14)) excludes ground-level paving, eaves, balconies. Building coverage and IC are distinct and cannot be equal where any paving exists outside buildings.
    71→- **Building height** (§ 25-1-21(50)) is measured from the **average of highest and lowest grades adjacent to the building** (AAG) to a roof-type-specific reference point (top of coping for flat; deck line for mansard; average of highest gable for pitched/hip). Measuring from lowest grade alone is a common error that maximizes apparent allowable height.
    72→- **§ 25-2-531 rooftop height exception** allows parapets, mechanicals, stairs/elevator overruns, ornamental structures to exceed by the greater of 15% of permitted height, federal/state compliance amount, engineering standard (stacks), or 30% (spires). **Inapplicable within Capitol View Corridors.**
    73→- **2-foot projection exemption** (§ 25-8-63(C)(13)) does **not** apply to site plan IC — only to residential building permits (ECM § 1.8.1(C)).
    74→
    75→### Overlays and combining districts
    76→
    77→Each one materially modifies what's allowed and must be identified before applying any single standard.
    78→
    79→- **Conditional Overlay (CO)** — site-specific use prohibitions, trip caps, height/coverage restrictions in the adopting ordinance; supersedes base-district table where stricter. Pull ordinance from AMANDA.
    80→- **Mixed Use (MU)** — adds multifamily to a commercial base district; sets per-unit site area thresholds (Subch. E § 4.2.1(D)(6)) ranging from 800 sf/unit (GO-MU, GR-MU, CS-MU efficiency) to 4,400 sf (NO-MU 2BR+).
    81→- **VMU / V** — Vertical Mixed Use. Commercial sites on a Core Transit Corridor or Future CTC. VMU buildings need at least one residential floor + ≥75% pedestrian-oriented commercial frontage (§ 4.3.3.B–C). Dimensional exemptions cover site area, FAR, coverage, setbacks — **not height**. 60% parking reduction (§ 4.3.3.E.3) requires affordability per § 4.3.3.F (5%+5% owner at ≤80%/≤100% AMI, 99-yr; or 10% rental at ≤80% AMI, 40-yr) and cannot stack with any other parking reduction.
    82→- **ETOD (Equitable Transit-Oriented Development), § 25-2-182 + DBETOD** — combining district for sites near transit corridors. Subdistrict 1 (station-adjacent) allows greater height than Subdistrict 2 (60/90/120 ft tier depending on combined zoning). Identified by "ETOD" suffix or `etod-subdistricts` GIS layer.
    83→- **DB90 (Density Bonus 90)** — bonus combining district on CS-1, CS, GR, LR, GO, or LO; +30 ft height to cap of 90 ft, plus FAR/coverage/setback exemptions in exchange for affordability (12% rental ≤60% MFI or 10% ≤50% MFI; 12% ownership ≤80% MFI). Amended late 2024 by Ord. 20240229-073 and 20240829-158.
    84→- **UNO (University Neighborhood Overlay)** — west of UT campus. Affordability required (§ 25-2-765): 10% units at ≤60% AMFI **and** 10% at ≤50% AMFI (conjunctive — total 20%, 40-yr). Parking: 60% of Appendix A is the **maximum**.
    85→- **NCCD (Neighborhood Conservation Combining District)** — identified by "NCCD" suffix; each NCCD has its own adopting ordinance with bespoke use/dimensional restrictions and may include pedestrian-oriented use requirements (LDC § 25-2-691(C) closed list). Each NCCD's adopting ordinance must be obtained — they are not in Bureau's code library.
    86→- **CVC (Capitol View Corridor), § 25-2-642** — 26 named corridors. Max height = lesser of base district maximum and CVC plane elevation (in feet above mean sea level). Plans must use AMSL, not "feet from grade." A sealed CVC documentation package from a Registered Professional Surveyor or Engineer + City Height Determination Letter required. **§ 25-2-531 exceptions do NOT apply.**
    87→- **Capitol Dominance (CD), § 25-2-641** — separate from CVC. Within ¼-mile of Capitol dome center (653 ft AMSL). Max elevation = 653 + (0.04366 × horizontal distance) ft AMSL.
    88→- **Hill Country Roadway Corridor (HCRC), §§ 25-2-1102–1126** — within 1,000 ft of ROW of Loop 360 (US 290W–US 183), RM 620 (SH 71–Anderson Mill), RM 2222 (Highland Hills–RM 620), RM 2244 (Loop 360–SH 71), or Southwest Parkway. Exception: sites within 1,000 ft of US 183 or US 290W only are excluded. Requires ≥40% natural area (§ 25-2-1025), slope-based FAR caps in Moderate Intensity Zones (§ 25-2-1122), Hill Country building materials, ≤20% mirrored glass reflectance.
    89→- **Airport Overlay (AO-1/2/3), Chapter 25-13** — concentric noise contours around ABIA. Restricts use, requires Aviation Department signature, height limits per § 25-13-22 imaginary surfaces.
    90→- **Waterfront Overlay (WO), §§ 25-2-721–746** — 16 subdistricts along Lady Bird Lake (Town Lake) and the Colorado River. PARD Director review required. Shoreline setbacks vary by subdistrict (e.g., Rainey 150 ft from Town Lake, North Shore Central 100 ft, South Lakeshore 65 ft). North Shore Central and South Shore Central impose 70-degree angle-plane envelopes; Lamar uses straight caps. Primary setback area = no parking; secondary setback area = ≤30% IC.
    91→- **TOD Regulating Plans** — NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane. Each supersedes base LDC and Subchapter E within its boundary. ERC uses 5 subdistricts (CMU, IMU, NMU, UR, NR) with subdistrict-specific dimensional and use rules + a development bonus program (PAOS required).
    92→- **PUDs (Subch. B Art. 2)** — Council-adopted ordinance + Land Use Plan supersede the LDC tables for that property. Tier One requirements include ≥10/15/20% open space (residential/industrial/non-residential), ≥2-star Austin Energy Green Building, and **affirmative Subchapter E compliance for commercial/retail/mixed-use PUDs (§ 2.3.2(A))**. PUD-specific parking exhibits survive the citywide parking elimination.
    93→
    94→### Compatibility Standards (Article 10) — repealed and replaced July 15, 2024
    95→
    96→> **Critical 2024 change.** The former Article 10 used a four-tier framework at 50/100/300/540 ft with a "compatibility waiver" mechanism (former §§ 25-2-1081/1082). The Ord. No. 20240516-004 replacement effective July 15, 2024 uses only **two distance thresholds (50 ft and 75 ft)**. Plans citing the old distance bands, the waiver mechanism, or §§ 25-2-1064/1066/1067 are relying on repealed authority. Plans submitted before July 15, 2024 may retain Chapter 245 vesting to prior standards.
    97→
    98→**Applicability (§ 25-2-1051):** Site is (1) zoned MF-4 or less restrictive (MF-4, MF-5, MF-6, any commercial/industrial) AND (2) within 75 ft of a **triggering property** = 1–3 dwelling units zoned SF-5 or more restrictive (LA, RR, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, SF-4A, SF-4B, SF-5 only — SF-6 does NOT qualify; vacant lots do NOT qualify).
    99→
   100→**Exceptions (§ 25-2-1052):** CBD/DMU sites; structural alteration without size/height increase; sites used exclusively for duplex, SF attached, SF residential, small-lot SF, two-unit, three-unit, adult care, or child care.
   101→
   102→**Height limits (§ 25-2-1061):** <50 ft from triggering property = 40 ft max; 50–74 ft = 60 ft max; ≥75 ft = base zoning applies.
   103→
   104→**Buffer (§ 25-2-1062 + § 25-8-700):** 25 ft along shared triggering property line (15 ft if site is <75 ft wide), subdivided into a 10-ft **screening zone** (no vertical structures, parking, driveways, or mechanical equipment) and a 15-ft **restricted zone** (parking/drives permitted). Plantings per § 25-8-700(D): every 25 LF = 1 large shade tree + 1 small understory + 10 shrubs. Buffer NOT required for condo/townhouse use, ≤16-DU residential-only sites, or NO/LO/LR sites with ≤40 ft height cap.
   105→
   106→**Screening, noise, design (§ 25-2-1063):** Hooded/shielded lighting; mechanical noise ≤70 dB at shared property line; refuse slab ≥15 ft from triggering property; resident-only amenities ≥25 ft. Vehicle lights from parking, rooftop mechanical, storage, refuse, common amenity areas must all be screened from the shared property line.
   107→
   108→**Relief paths (current code):** BOA variance with hardship findings (§§ 25-2-472/474), OR site-specific amendment treated as a rezoning (§ 25-2-1054 — not available for special-purpose base districts, DB combining districts, or UNO).
   109→
   110→### Setbacks, screening, miscellaneous
   111→
   112→- **Standard setbacks**: § 25-2-492 by district. Industrial setbacks adjacent to residential/office/commercial: § 25-2-601 (10–50 ft depending on adjacency).
   113→- **Lake Austin (LA) shoreline setback**: 75 ft from 492.8-ft contour; 25 ft for pre-April 22, 1982 lots where shoreline-to-front-lot-line ≤200 ft.
   114→- **CWQZ**: 100 ft from Lady Bird Lake 429.0-ft contour or Lake Austin 492.8-ft contour (75 ft for detached SF residential).
   115→- **Hazardous pipeline (§ 25-2-516)**: applies only to ≥8" ID pipes carrying hazardous liquid per 49 CFR § 195.2 (natural gas excluded). Restricted area 25 ft; new construction zone 200 ft requires Fire Chief determination; evacuation-assistance use restriction 500 ft requires Council resolution for 200–500 ft range.
   116→- **Fence height**: 6 ft standard, 7 ft with grade change ≥1 ft, 8 ft under § 25-2-899(F)–(H). Post-July 2023 design restrictions in § 25-2-899(I).
   117→- **Parking area screening**: § 25-6-563 — 4 ft fence non-residential parking abutting residential; 6 ft for residential parking >10 spaces abutting residential property.
   118→
   119→### Site plan procedural triggers
   120→
   121→- **Site Plan Lite (Phase 1)** — recently launched DSD admin track for small residential projects (3–16 units) streamlining site plan review. Confirm current applicability with DSD Development Assistance Center; criteria and process are evolving.
   122→- **F1/F2 staging** — DSD administrative; two case numbers, no phasing fees. Distinct from formal § 25-5-21 phasing.
   123→- **Land Status Determination (LSD)** — required when legal description is "a portion of" a lot, metes-and-bounds without plat reference, or unplatted tract. Must be a Director-signed letter with case number.
   124→- **Demolition permit + 120-day tenant notification** for multifamily ≥5 units (BCM 16.3(F); LDC § 25-1-712); 270-day notification for mobile home parks (operates at site plan stage).
   125→
   126→## Opportunities to evaluate
   127→
   128→- **HOME Initiative Phase 1 (Ord. 20231207-001, eff. December 2023)**: in single-family residential zoning (SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, SF-4A, SF-4B, SF-5, SF-6), now allows up to 3 units per lot on what were SF-only lots, reduces minimum lot sizes, and recalibrates setbacks for missing-middle infill. Most relevant to small/infill developers; not a multifamily entitlement. Check current code for any Council amendments since adoption.
   129→- **HOME Initiative Phase 2 (Ord. 20240516-008, eff. mid-2024)**: further reduces minimum lot size for new SF-3 lots to ~1,800 sf with corresponding development standards, enabling small-lot SF subdivisions. Coupled with the Phase 2 Article 10 replacement, opens previously infeasible infill sites.
   130→- **ETOD Phase 1 / DBETOD**: layered density bonus along Project Connect transit corridors. Subdistrict 1 stations (e.g., Orange/Blue Line stops) allow 60/90/120 ft tiers in exchange for affordability. Pair with Affordability Unlocked for deepest entitlement.
   131→- **Site Plan Lite (Phase 1)**: small residential infill (typically 3–16 units) bypasses full Consolidated Site Plan review for a faster admin track. Useful for HOME-aligned projects.
   132→- **Citywide parking minimum elimination (Nov 13, 2023)**: parking is a free variable for almost all projects — design for utility, not for code. Plan for unbundled or shared parking if multifamily; small-format infill no longer carries parking cost.
   133→- **Density bonus programs** (decide before site plan submittal):
   134→  - **DDBP (downtown, § 25-2-586)** — FAR/height above primary entitlement in exchange for menu of community benefits (affordable housing, open space, public art, streetscape). Must obtain Director's written notice **before site plan submittal**.
   135→  - **DB90 (suburban commercial)** — +30 ft height + dimensional relief on CS/CS-1/GR/LR/GO/LO. Requires rezone to add DB90 combining district.
   136→  - **Affordability Unlocked (AU)** — most affordability-intensive: ≥50% units affordable. Type I = 1.25× base height; Type II = 1.5× base. **Exempt from Article 10 compatibility** (§ 25-2-518(D)(1)) and all parking minimums (§ 25-6-471(G)).
   137→  - **VMU 60% parking reduction** with affordability compliance (§ 4.3.3.F).
   138→  - **NBG Development Bonus** — SMART Housing + 10% of bonus area affordable; fee-in-lieu at $6/sf (NHCD Director approval; Council NOT required).
   139→  - **Plaza Saltillo TOD bonus** — 25% sf affordable; fee-in-lieu requires **City Council** approval.
   140→  - **Rainey Street WO** — 8:1 FAR for 5% residential GFA at ≤80% MFI (40-yr rental / 99-yr ownership covenant).
   141→  - **SMART Housing** — fee waivers (25/50/75/100% by reasonably-priced unit share), parkland exemption, reduced tree mitigation ($75/in vs $200/in). 1-yr owner / 5-yr rental affordability — NOT a 40-yr covenant.
   142→- **Redevelopment exception (§§ 25-8-25/26/27)** — sites whose existing development exceeds current watershed IC may retain that IC in redevelopment. Section depends on watershed: 25-8-25 (urban/suburban, no trip cap), 25-8-26 (BSZ, commercial only, Council if >2,000 trips/day), 25-8-27 (WSR/WSS).
   143→- **Alternative Equivalent Compliance (Subch. E § 1.5)** — design-flex pathway for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, Article 3. Requires Director-issued concept plan approval (3-yr expiration, one-year extension available).
   144→- **VMU streetscape ROW credit toward open space** (Subch. E § 2.7.3.D.9) — except clear zone area or where City participates in streetscape cost.
   145→- **Pre-application meetings** — DSD intake conferences can lock in expectations and identify deal-breakers before formal application; valuable when overlays stack or PUD is in play.
   146→
   147→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   148→
   149→- **zoning-pathway.md** — Base district, all suffixes (MU, V/VMU, CO, NP, NCCD, ETOD, DB90, UNO, WO, CVC, AO), watershed classification, jurisdiction (full purpose / limited purpose / ETJ), DDZ vs DWPZ.
   150→- **neighborhood-plan.md** — NP combining district notes, FLUM designation (note: policy only).
   151→- **overlays.md** — All overlay layers from COA GIS (Capitol View, Capitol Dominance, Hill Country, Airport, WO subdistrict if applicable, TOD subdistrict, ETOD subdistrict, HCRC intensity zone).
   152→- **adjacency.md** — Adjacent parcels' zoning *and* dwelling unit counts within 75 ft (for Article 10 triggering property test); existing structure heights and locations on triggering properties.
   153→- **programs.md** — DDBP eligibility (downtown Figure 2), DB90 eligibility, VMU/V opt-in status, AU eligibility, SMART Housing eligibility, ETOD subdistrict, NBG/ERC/Plaza Saltillo TOD status, ERC Hub status.
   154→- **property-records.md** — Recorded restrictive covenants (height, use, parking), Unified Development Agreement, prior approved site plans (may impose tighter standards than current zoning), conditional overlay ordinances, NCCD ordinance.
   155→- **case-history.md (AMANDA)** — Prior cases, pending amendments, Vested Rights Determination (written Director determination required to operate a Chapter 245 vesting claim), Land Status Determination case number.
   156→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — Proposed use(s) by LDC name, building dimensions per building, total GFA, unit count by bedroom type, parking count, building footprint, IC/coverage estimates.
   157→
   158→## Output structure
   159→
   160→```markdown
   161→# Zoning & Land Use Findings — <property>
   162→
   163→## Summary
   164→- Base district: <code> (full zoning string)
   165→- Overlays / combining districts: <list with citations to GIS layers and ordinances>
   166→- Proposed use compatibility: <by-right | conditional | prohibited>
   167→- Procedural path: <admin | conditional use | rezoning | density bonus + admin>
   168→- Critical 2024 code changes affecting this site: <Article 10 replacement, HOME Phase 1/2, ETOD, parking elimination, etc.>
   169→
   170→## Zoning capacity table
   171→| Standard | Code limit | Modifier (overlay, bonus) | Effective limit | Proposed | Status |
   172→| Use | <permitted list> | <CO restrictions> | <effective> | <use> | <pass/conditional/prohibited> |
   173→| Height | <ft from § 25-2-492> | <CVC plane, AU bonus, DB90, Compatibility cap> | <effective ft> | <proposed ft> | <pass/fail/data-gap> |
   174→| FAR | <X:1 from § 25-2-492> | <DDBP/DB90/VMU exemption> | <effective> | <proposed> | ... |
   175→| Building coverage | <% from § 25-2-492> | ... | ... | ... | ... |
   176→| Impervious cover | <% from watershed table> | <redevelopment exception> | ... | ... | ... |
   177→| Parking | None (eliminated 2023) or <PUD exhibit> | <UNO max 60% Appendix A> | ... | <proposed> | <pass/note> |
   178→| Min site area / unit | <§ 25-2-560 to 563 or Subch E § 4.2.1.D.6> | ... | ... | ... | ... |
   179→| Setbacks (front / side / rear / street side) | <§ 25-2-492 / § 25-2-601> | <Compatibility § 25-2-1062, WO setback> | ... | ... | ... |
   180→
   181→## Findings
   182→### Use compatibility
   183→### Dimensional standards
   184→### Compatibility Standards (Article 10) — apply current post-July 2024 framework
   185→### Overlays (CVC, HCRC, WO, AO, NCCD, etc.)
   186→### Density bonus opportunity assessment (DDBP / DB90 / ETOD / VMU / AU / NBG / Plaza Saltillo / SMART Housing)
   187→### Procedural path
   188→### Site plan trigger and track (full Consolidated, Site Plan Lite, F1/F2, formal § 25-5-21 phased)
   189→
   190→## Plan-specific findings (only if concept plan provided)
   191→## Open questions for the engineer
   192→```
   193→
   194→## Severity heuristics
   195→
   196→| Finding type | Severity |
   197→|---|---|
   198→| Proposed use is prohibited in base district and no rezoning path exists | `significant` |
   199→| Proposed use conditional (Large Retail, late-hours CL, Child Care General); LUC/PC approval adds 4–9 months | `moderate` |
   200→| Building height/FAR exceeds limit by >10% without identified density bonus | `significant` |
   201→| Building height/FAR exceeds limit by ≤10% and a density bonus is plausibly available | `moderate` |
   202→| Article 10 height limit (40 ft within 50 ft; 60 ft within 75 ft) violated and no AU exemption | `significant` |
   203→| Article 10 compatibility buffer violated (encroachment of vertical structure, parking, or mechanical in 10-ft screening zone) | `moderate` |
   204→| CVC plane elevation exceeded by any element (incl. mechanical — no § 25-2-531 exception) | `significant` |
   205→| Hill Country natural-area minimum (40%) not met | `significant` |
   206→| WO primary setback violated (e.g., 150 ft from Town Lake in Rainey) | `significant` |
   207→| WO secondary setback IC >30% | `moderate` |
   208→| Hazardous pipeline 200-ft new construction zone, no Fire Chief determination | `significant` |
   209→| HOME Phase 1/2 eligibility unlocks 2–3 unit infill on what looks like an SF-only lot | `opportunity` |
   210→| Citywide parking elimination — concept plan still showing minimums | `opportunity` (drop the parking; reclaim site area) |
   211→| ETOD Subdistrict 1 eligibility with 90–120 ft height tier | `opportunity` |
   212→| AU eligibility (≥50% affordable) unlocks 1.5× height and Article 10 exemption | `opportunity` |
   213→| VMU 60% parking reduction available with affordability covenant | `opportunity` |
   214→| DDBP available but FAR/height already at primary entitlement (no bonus needed) | `note` |
   215→| Overlay adds design-review with predictable conditions (e.g., PARD WO review, ABIA AO review) | `note` |
   216→| Adjacent dwelling-unit count not in GIS — Article 10 triggering test requires field verification | `data-gap` |
   217→| Zoning case recently approved but not yet on GIS | `data-gap` |
   218→| PUD ordinance not in Bureau or NCCD adopting ordinance not retrievable | `data-gap` |
   219→| Vested rights claimed without written Director determination | `data-gap` |
   220→
   221→## Common pitfalls
   222→
   223→- **Confusing FLUM (Imagine Austin policy) with zoning.** FLUM does not establish zoning; rezones still require § 25-2-281 process.
   224→- **Applying repealed Article 10 (50/100/300/540 ft bands)** to post-July 2024 plans. Current code: 50 ft and 75 ft only. Compatibility waivers under former §§ 25-2-1081/1082 no longer exist.
   225→- **Citing § 25-2-1064 / 25-2-1066 / 25-2-1067** for lighting, parking screening, or noise — all repealed; current authority is § 25-2-1063.
   226→- **Treating SF-6 as a triggering property.** SF-6 is less restrictive than SF-5. Only LA, RR, SF-1 through SF-5 qualify, AND the lot must contain 1–3 dwelling units.
   227→- **Applying parking minimums anywhere except inside a PUD with a parking exhibit, or under UNO (where it's a maximum).** Minimums were eliminated November 13, 2023.
   228→- **Citing "Type CT" site plan designation.** Abolished November 13, 2023 along with parking minimums. Only relevant for amendments to pre-Nov 2023 plans.
   229→- **Measuring building height from finished floor or from the lowest grade.** § 25-1-21(50) requires the *average* of highest and lowest adjacent grades at the building perimeter.
   230→- **Citing § 25-2-531 height exceptions on CVC sites.** Inapplicable per § 25-2-642(B). All rooftop elements (mechanical, parapets, elevator overruns) count against the CVC plane.
   231→- **Confusing § 25-2-641 (Capitol Dominance) with § 25-2-642 (CVC).** They are different overlays with different geometry.
   232→- **Counting overlay setbacks as additive to base setbacks** when the overlay replaces them, or vice versa. Check the overlay text — usually the more restrictive governs (§ 25-2-492(B)) but PUDs/regulating plans may supersede.
   233→- **Including atria airspace or enclosed loading berths in GFA.** § 25-1-21(47) excludes them. Loading docks (not berths) ARE included.
   234→- **Treating bulk-purpose GFA and parking-calculation GFA as the same number.** Bike rooms and shower facilities only reduce GFA for parking purposes (§ 25-6-472(C)), not for FAR or benchmarking.
   235→- **Subtracting floodplain, CWQZ, or slopes from Gross Site Area for FAR.** GSA is the unmodified site area; only formally dedicated ROW is excluded.
   236→- **Treating SMART Housing as a 40-year covenant.** SMART Housing affordability is 1 yr owner / 5 yr rental (§ 25-1-705). 40-year obligations come from UNO, VMU, AU, DDBP, NBG, Plaza Saltillo, or Rainey programs.
   237→- **Submitting a Conditional Approval letter from Austin Energy Green Building in place of the Letter of Intent at site plan stage.** LOI must be co-signed by AEGB staff at site plan stage (BCM 7.1.3.2).
   238→- **Asserting Chapter 245 vesting in a narrative without a Director's written Vested Rights Determination under § 25-1-541.** The claim is inoperative until issued.
   239→- **Citing a PUD ordinance number without confirming it is the most recently amended version.** Tracking tables (DU, IC, GFA, VTD/PHT) must reflect the current ordinance after all amendments.
   240→- **Assuming Subchapter E categorically does not apply to PUD sites.** Subch. E § 1.2.5(B) is provision-by-provision; commercial/retail/mixed-use PUDs were required to comply with Subch. E as a Tier One condition (§ 2.3.2(A)).
   241→- **Citing the wrong IFC edition in fire-related notes.** Austin adopted the **2024 IFC** per Ord. 20250410-039, effective July 10, 2025 (superseded 2021 IFC).
   242→- **Using the form "Watershed Protection and Development Review Department," "PDRD," or other predecessor names** in approval blocks or AW construction notes — the department name is **Development Services Department**.
   243→
