# Zoning & Land Use Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Base zoning district, combining districts and overlays (CO, MU, V/VMU, ETOD, NCCD, UNO, WO, CVC, ERC, TODs, HCRC, AO, NBG, DB90), conditional and special use processes, use classification under LDC Chapter 25-2, dimensional standards (height, FAR, building coverage, impervious cover, site area per unit), Compatibility Standards (Article 10), parking, density bonus programs, and site plan procedural path. Excludes site engineering (sde), site form (sduf), environmental layers (el/eptp/fwp/sde), transportation (ta), and wastewater/water (wwp) even where coded in Chapter 25-2 or Subchapter E.

## Authoritative sources

- **Land Development Code (LDC), Chapter 25** — Austin Municode. Most-cited chapters: 25-1 (definitions, applications), 25-2 (zoning), 25-5 (site plan), 25-6 (parking and ROW), 25-8 (environmental), 25-13 (airport).
- **Subchapter E (Design Standards & Mixed Use)** — design standards, connectivity, VMU, AEC.
- **Subchapter B, Article 2** — PUD framework.
- **General Site Plan Notes for COA (DSD)** — required notes, signature blocks, forms; modification prohibited.
- **Zoning map (COA GIS, "zoning" layer)** — base district + suffixes. Zoning strings are compound: `GR-MU-CO-NP-DB90` = General Retail + Mixed Use + Conditional Overlay + Neighborhood Plan + DB90 density bonus.
- **Adopted overlays (COA GIS layers)** — CVC, Capitol Dominance, Hill Country Roadway, AO-1/2/3 (Airport), WO subdistricts, NCCD ordinances, TODs (NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane), UNO, ETOD subdistricts.
- **AMANDA / DSD permit system** — case history, prior approvals, vested rights determinations.
- **Imagine Austin (comp plan) / Future Land Use Map** — *policy, not regulatory.* FLUM does not establish zoning; zoning changes require LDC § 25-2-281 rezoning.

## Regulatory pathway

| Path | Trigger | Timeline | Decision body |
|---|---|---|---|
| Administrative site plan approval (Director) | Site plan complies with all title requirements; no commission action required | 6–12 months from intake through release | DSD Director (LDC § 25-5-112) |
| Conditional use permit | Use is "C" in district use table (§ 25-2-491), incl. Large Retail (≥100,000 sf, § 25-2-815), late-hours cocktail lounge, etc. | 4–9 months before site plan can be finalized | Land Use Commission / Planning Commission (LDC § 25-5-142) |
| Rezoning (incl. site-specific Article 10 amendment) | Proposed use prohibited in base district, or modification of Article 10 height/buffer | 6–12 months | P&Z recommendation → City Council |
| BOA variance | Hardship from a dimensional standard (setback, parking, fence) | 3–6 months | Board of Adjustment (LDC §§ 25-2-472, 25-2-474) |
| Density bonus (DDBP, DB90, ETOD, VMU, AU, NBG, Plaza Saltillo, ERC) | Site is eligible per program-specific maps + affordability/community-benefit compliance | Concurrent with site plan (DDBP must be **approved before site plan submittal** per § 25-2-586(H)) | DSD Director (DDBP); NHCD/HPD (others) |
| Alternative Equivalent Compliance (AEC) | Subchapter E deviation; available only for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, and Article 3 | 1–4 months | Director (concept plan); expires 3 years from approval |
| F1/F2 staged site plan | DSD administrative practice for large multifamily/mixed-use: F1 = horizontal, F2 = vertical | Two separate case numbers, sequential approvals | DSD (no Planning Commission or phasing fees) |
| Formal § 25-5-21 phased site plan | Single case number with phasing plan; final-phase start >3 years post-approval → Planning Commission | Adds 2–4 months if PC required | DSD Director or Planning Commission |
| Site plan correction / minor revision to released plan | LDC § 25-5-61(C)–(D): no significant effect, ROW relocation, or ADA | 1–3 months | Director (written approval) |

Site plan approval is valid **3 years from date of approval** (LDC § 25-5-81(B)), extendable by issued building permits or active site work.

## Constraints to evaluate

### Use compatibility

- **Confirm proposed use against base district use table** (§ 25-2-491). Use the **exact LDC name** from Chapters 25-2-3 through 25-2-6 (residential, commercial, industrial, civic). "Office," "Retail," "Restaurant," "School" alone are insufficient.
- **Restaurant (General)** (§ 25-2-4(B)(64)) requires ≥51% gross income from prepared food (§ 25-2-808(B)(1)); below that, the use reclassifies to **Cocktail Lounge** (conditional, LUC approval required).
- **Large Retail** (≥100,000 sf of any single enumerated use including its accessory uses, § 25-2-815) is a conditional use requiring Land Use Commission approval.
- **LR (Neighborhood Commercial) restrictions** (§ 25-2-587): Restaurant (General) ≤4,000 sf, 7 a.m.–11 p.m. hours, no drive-through; General Retail (General) ≤5,000 sf, no local-street access; no outdoor entertainment or amplified sound.
- **Multifamily in CS** requires MU overlay or rezone.
- **W/LO** requires ≥20% of GFA or 1,000 sf (lesser) as office facing the primary street (§ 25-2-584).
- **Civic use chapter** — schools, child care, adult care, community recreation are in § 25-2-6, NOT § 25-2-3 or 25-2-4. Common misclassification.

### Dimensional envelope (zoning capacity table)

Building Austin's zoning capacity table requires the **base district from § 25-2-492** *plus* every overlay/combining-district modifier. Selected base district maxima:

| District | Use list (representative) | Max height | Max FAR | Max IC | Min parking (post-Nov 2023) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SF-3 / SF-5 / SF-6 | SF, duplex (SF-3+), 2/3-unit (SF-3+) | 35 ft | none | 40% / 45% / 50% (varies) | None citywide |
| MF-1 / MF-2 / MF-3 / MF-4 / MF-5 / MF-6 | Multifamily, condo, townhouse, group residential | 40 / 40 (3 stry) / 40 / 60 / 60 / 90 ft | none / none / 0.75:1 / 0.75:1 / 1:1 / none | 45–70% | None citywide |
| NO / LO / GO | Office sub-tiers | 35 / 40 (3 stry) / 60 ft | 0.35 / 0.7 / 1:1 | 50 / 70 / 80% | None citywide |
| LR | Neighborhood commercial (capped uses) | 40 ft (3 stry) | 0.5:1 | 80% | None citywide |
| GR | General commercial | 60 ft | 1:1 | 90% | None citywide |
| CS / CS-1 | Commercial services | 60 ft | 2:1 | 95% | None citywide |
| CH | Commercial highway | 60 ft (per § 25-2-582) | 3:1 | 95% | None citywide |
| DMU | Downtown mixed use | 120 ft (8:1 with DDBP) | 5:1 | 100% | None citywide |
| CBD | Central business district | 350 ft | 8:1 | 100% | None citywide |
| IP / LI / MI / R&D | Industrial sub-tiers | 60 / 60 / 120 / 60 ft | 1:1 | 80% | None citywide |
| LA | Lake Austin | 35 ft | none | per § 25-2-551 | None citywide |

**Citywide parking minimums were eliminated November 13, 2023** by Ord. No. 20231102-028 (LDC § 25-6-471(A)). Exceptions: (1) PUDs with parking exhibits in their ordinance (e.g., Goodnight Ranch Exhibit J) continue to control; (2) UNO sets a 60% **maximum ceiling** (not minimum) on Appendix A; (3) accessibility (ADA) spaces still required. The repeal also abolished the "Type CT" plan designation and the mandatory shower-facility requirement under § 25-6-478(D)(1).

**Where IC, FAR, height, and coverage are calculated:**

- **FAR = GFA ÷ Gross Site Area** (§§ 25-1-21(43), (48)). GSA is the full unmodified site area — no deductions for floodplain, CWQZ, slopes, or environmental overlays.
- **GFA** (§ 25-1-21(47)) includes loading docks, excludes atria airspace, parking, driveways, enclosed loading berths. The bulk-purpose GFA differs from parking-calculation GFA (which additionally excludes bike rooms and showers per § 25-6-472(C)) — don't conflate.
- **Building coverage** (§ 25-1-21(14)) excludes ground-level paving, eaves, balconies. Building coverage and IC are distinct and cannot be equal where any paving exists outside buildings.
- **Building height** (§ 25-1-21(50)) is measured from the **average of highest and lowest grades adjacent to the building** (AAG) to a roof-type-specific reference point (top of coping for flat; deck line for mansard; average of highest gable for pitched/hip). Measuring from lowest grade alone is a common error that maximizes apparent allowable height.
- **§ 25-2-531 rooftop height exception** allows parapets, mechanicals, stairs/elevator overruns, ornamental structures to exceed by the greater of 15% of permitted height, federal/state compliance amount, engineering standard (stacks), or 30% (spires). **Inapplicable within Capitol View Corridors.**
- **2-foot projection exemption** (§ 25-8-63(C)(13)) does **not** apply to site plan IC — only to residential building permits (ECM § 1.8.1(C)).

### Overlays and combining districts

Each one materially modifies what's allowed and must be identified before applying any single standard.

- **Conditional Overlay (CO)** — site-specific use prohibitions, trip caps, height/coverage restrictions in the adopting ordinance; supersedes base-district table where stricter. Pull ordinance from AMANDA.
- **Mixed Use (MU)** — adds multifamily to a commercial base district; sets per-unit site area thresholds (Subch. E § 4.2.1(D)(6)) ranging from 800 sf/unit (GO-MU, GR-MU, CS-MU efficiency) to 4,400 sf (NO-MU 2BR+).
- **VMU / V** — Vertical Mixed Use. Commercial sites on a Core Transit Corridor or Future CTC. VMU buildings need at least one residential floor + ≥75% pedestrian-oriented commercial frontage (§ 4.3.3.B–C). Dimensional exemptions cover site area, FAR, coverage, setbacks — **not height**. 60% parking reduction (§ 4.3.3.E.3) requires affordability per § 4.3.3.F (5%+5% owner at ≤80%/≤100% AMI, 99-yr; or 10% rental at ≤80% AMI, 40-yr) and cannot stack with any other parking reduction.
- **ETOD (Equitable Transit-Oriented Development), § 25-2-182 + DBETOD** — combining district for sites near transit corridors. Subdistrict 1 (station-adjacent) allows greater height than Subdistrict 2 (60/90/120 ft tier depending on combined zoning). Identified by "ETOD" suffix or `etod-subdistricts` GIS layer.
- **DB90 (Density Bonus 90)** — bonus combining district on CS-1, CS, GR, LR, GO, or LO; +30 ft height to cap of 90 ft, plus FAR/coverage/setback exemptions in exchange for affordability (12% rental ≤60% MFI or 10% ≤50% MFI; 12% ownership ≤80% MFI). Amended late 2024 by Ord. 20240229-073 and 20240829-158.
- **UNO (University Neighborhood Overlay)** — west of UT campus. Affordability required (§ 25-2-765): 10% units at ≤60% AMFI **and** 10% at ≤50% AMFI (conjunctive — total 20%, 40-yr). Parking: 60% of Appendix A is the **maximum**.
- **NCCD (Neighborhood Conservation Combining District)** — identified by "NCCD" suffix; each NCCD has its own adopting ordinance with bespoke use/dimensional restrictions and may include pedestrian-oriented use requirements (LDC § 25-2-691(C) closed list). Each NCCD's adopting ordinance must be obtained — they are not in Bureau's code library.
- **CVC (Capitol View Corridor), § 25-2-642** — 26 named corridors. Max height = lesser of base district maximum and CVC plane elevation (in feet above mean sea level). Plans must use AMSL, not "feet from grade." A sealed CVC documentation package from a Registered Professional Surveyor or Engineer + City Height Determination Letter required. **§ 25-2-531 exceptions do NOT apply.**
- **Capitol Dominance (CD), § 25-2-641** — separate from CVC. Within ¼-mile of Capitol dome center (653 ft AMSL). Max elevation = 653 + (0.04366 × horizontal distance) ft AMSL.
- **Hill Country Roadway Corridor (HCRC), §§ 25-2-1102–1126** — within 1,000 ft of ROW of Loop 360 (US 290W–US 183), RM 620 (SH 71–Anderson Mill), RM 2222 (Highland Hills–RM 620), RM 2244 (Loop 360–SH 71), or Southwest Parkway. Exception: sites within 1,000 ft of US 183 or US 290W only are excluded. Requires ≥40% natural area (§ 25-2-1025), slope-based FAR caps in Moderate Intensity Zones (§ 25-2-1122), Hill Country building materials, ≤20% mirrored glass reflectance.
- **Airport Overlay (AO-1/2/3), Chapter 25-13** — concentric noise contours around ABIA. Restricts use, requires Aviation Department signature, height limits per § 25-13-22 imaginary surfaces.
- **Waterfront Overlay (WO), §§ 25-2-721–746** — 16 subdistricts along Lady Bird Lake (Town Lake) and the Colorado River. PARD Director review required. Shoreline setbacks vary by subdistrict (e.g., Rainey 150 ft from Town Lake, North Shore Central 100 ft, South Lakeshore 65 ft). North Shore Central and South Shore Central impose 70-degree angle-plane envelopes; Lamar uses straight caps. Primary setback area = no parking; secondary setback area = ≤30% IC.
- **TOD Regulating Plans** — NBG, ERC, Plaza Saltillo, East MLK, Lamar/Justin Lane. Each supersedes base LDC and Subchapter E within its boundary. ERC uses 5 subdistricts (CMU, IMU, NMU, UR, NR) with subdistrict-specific dimensional and use rules + a development bonus program (PAOS required).
- **PUDs (Subch. B Art. 2)** — Council-adopted ordinance + Land Use Plan supersede the LDC tables for that property. Tier One requirements include ≥10/15/20% open space (residential/industrial/non-residential), ≥2-star Austin Energy Green Building, and **affirmative Subchapter E compliance for commercial/retail/mixed-use PUDs (§ 2.3.2(A))**. PUD-specific parking exhibits survive the citywide parking elimination.

### Compatibility Standards (Article 10) — repealed and replaced July 15, 2024

> **Critical 2024 change.** The former Article 10 used a four-tier framework at 50/100/300/540 ft with a "compatibility waiver" mechanism (former §§ 25-2-1081/1082). The Ord. No. 20240516-004 replacement effective July 15, 2024 uses only **two distance thresholds (50 ft and 75 ft)**. Plans citing the old distance bands, the waiver mechanism, or §§ 25-2-1064/1066/1067 are relying on repealed authority. Plans submitted before July 15, 2024 may retain Chapter 245 vesting to prior standards.

**Applicability (§ 25-2-1051):** Site is (1) zoned MF-4 or less restrictive (MF-4, MF-5, MF-6, any commercial/industrial) AND (2) within 75 ft of a **triggering property** = 1–3 dwelling units zoned SF-5 or more restrictive (LA, RR, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, SF-4A, SF-4B, SF-5 only — SF-6 does NOT qualify; vacant lots do NOT qualify).

**Exceptions (§ 25-2-1052):** CBD/DMU sites; structural alteration without size/height increase; sites used exclusively for duplex, SF attached, SF residential, small-lot SF, two-unit, three-unit, adult care, or child care.

**Height limits (§ 25-2-1061):** <50 ft from triggering property = 40 ft max; 50–74 ft = 60 ft max; ≥75 ft = base zoning applies.

**Buffer (§ 25-2-1062 + § 25-8-700):** 25 ft along shared triggering property line (15 ft if site is <75 ft wide), subdivided into a 10-ft **screening zone** (no vertical structures, parking, driveways, or mechanical equipment) and a 15-ft **restricted zone** (parking/drives permitted). Plantings per § 25-8-700(D): every 25 LF = 1 large shade tree + 1 small understory + 10 shrubs. Buffer NOT required for condo/townhouse use, ≤16-DU residential-only sites, or NO/LO/LR sites with ≤40 ft height cap.

**Screening, noise, design (§ 25-2-1063):** Hooded/shielded lighting; mechanical noise ≤70 dB at shared property line; refuse slab ≥15 ft from triggering property; resident-only amenities ≥25 ft. Vehicle lights from parking, rooftop mechanical, storage, refuse, common amenity areas must all be screened from the shared property line.

**Relief paths (current code):** BOA variance with hardship findings (§§ 25-2-472/474), OR site-specific amendment treated as a rezoning (§ 25-2-1054 — not available for special-purpose base districts, DB combining districts, or UNO).

### Setbacks, screening, miscellaneous

- **Standard setbacks**: § 25-2-492 by district. Industrial setbacks adjacent to residential/office/commercial: § 25-2-601 (10–50 ft depending on adjacency).
- **Lake Austin (LA) shoreline setback**: 75 ft from 492.8-ft contour; 25 ft for pre-April 22, 1982 lots where shoreline-to-front-lot-line ≤200 ft.
- **CWQZ**: 100 ft from Lady Bird Lake 429.0-ft contour or Lake Austin 492.8-ft contour (75 ft for detached SF residential).
- **Hazardous pipeline (§ 25-2-516)**: applies only to ≥8" ID pipes carrying hazardous liquid per 49 CFR § 195.2 (natural gas excluded). Restricted area 25 ft; new construction zone 200 ft requires Fire Chief determination; evacuation-assistance use restriction 500 ft requires Council resolution for 200–500 ft range.
- **Fence height**: 6 ft standard, 7 ft with grade change ≥1 ft, 8 ft under § 25-2-899(F)–(H). Post-July 2023 design restrictions in § 25-2-899(I).
- **Parking area screening**: § 25-6-563 — 4 ft fence non-residential parking abutting residential; 6 ft for residential parking >10 spaces abutting residential property.

### Site plan procedural triggers

- **Site Plan Lite (Phase 1)** — recently launched DSD admin track for small residential projects (3–16 units) streamlining site plan review. Confirm current applicability with DSD Development Assistance Center; criteria and process are evolving.
- **F1/F2 staging** — DSD administrative; two case numbers, no phasing fees. Distinct from formal § 25-5-21 phasing.
- **Land Status Determination (LSD)** — required when legal description is "a portion of" a lot, metes-and-bounds without plat reference, or unplatted tract. Must be a Director-signed letter with case number.
- **Demolition permit + 120-day tenant notification** for multifamily ≥5 units (BCM 16.3(F); LDC § 25-1-712); 270-day notification for mobile home parks (operates at site plan stage).

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **HOME Initiative Phase 1 (Ord. 20231207-001, eff. December 2023)**: in single-family residential zoning (SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, SF-4A, SF-4B, SF-5, SF-6), now allows up to 3 units per lot on what were SF-only lots, reduces minimum lot sizes, and recalibrates setbacks for missing-middle infill. Most relevant to small/infill developers; not a multifamily entitlement. Check current code for any Council amendments since adoption.
- **HOME Initiative Phase 2 (Ord. 20240516-008, eff. mid-2024)**: further reduces minimum lot size for new SF-3 lots to ~1,800 sf with corresponding development standards, enabling small-lot SF subdivisions. Coupled with the Phase 2 Article 10 replacement, opens previously infeasible infill sites.
- **ETOD Phase 1 / DBETOD**: layered density bonus along Project Connect transit corridors. Subdistrict 1 stations (e.g., Orange/Blue Line stops) allow 60/90/120 ft tiers in exchange for affordability. Pair with Affordability Unlocked for deepest entitlement.
- **Site Plan Lite (Phase 1)**: small residential infill (typically 3–16 units) bypasses full Consolidated Site Plan review for a faster admin track. Useful for HOME-aligned projects.
- **Citywide parking minimum elimination (Nov 13, 2023)**: parking is a free variable for almost all projects — design for utility, not for code. Plan for unbundled or shared parking if multifamily; small-format infill no longer carries parking cost.
- **Density bonus programs** (decide before site plan submittal):
  - **DDBP (downtown, § 25-2-586)** — FAR/height above primary entitlement in exchange for menu of community benefits (affordable housing, open space, public art, streetscape). Must obtain Director's written notice **before site plan submittal**.
  - **DB90 (suburban commercial)** — +30 ft height + dimensional relief on CS/CS-1/GR/LR/GO/LO. Requires rezone to add DB90 combining district.
  - **Affordability Unlocked (AU)** — most affordability-intensive: ≥50% units affordable. Type I = 1.25× base height; Type II = 1.5× base. **Exempt from Article 10 compatibility** (§ 25-2-518(D)(1)) and all parking minimums (§ 25-6-471(G)).
  - **VMU 60% parking reduction** with affordability compliance (§ 4.3.3.F).
  - **NBG Development Bonus** — SMART Housing + 10% of bonus area affordable; fee-in-lieu at $6/sf (NHCD Director approval; Council NOT required).
  - **Plaza Saltillo TOD bonus** — 25% sf affordable; fee-in-lieu requires **City Council** approval.
  - **Rainey Street WO** — 8:1 FAR for 5% residential GFA at ≤80% MFI (40-yr rental / 99-yr ownership covenant).
  - **SMART Housing** — fee waivers (25/50/75/100% by reasonably-priced unit share), parkland exemption, reduced tree mitigation ($75/in vs $200/in). 1-yr owner / 5-yr rental affordability — NOT a 40-yr covenant.
- **Redevelopment exception (§§ 25-8-25/26/27)** — sites whose existing development exceeds current watershed IC may retain that IC in redevelopment. Section depends on watershed: 25-8-25 (urban/suburban, no trip cap), 25-8-26 (BSZ, commercial only, Council if >2,000 trips/day), 25-8-27 (WSR/WSS).
- **Alternative Equivalent Compliance (Subch. E § 1.5)** — design-flex pathway for §§ 2.2, 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 2.8, Article 3. Requires Director-issued concept plan approval (3-yr expiration, one-year extension available).
- **VMU streetscape ROW credit toward open space** (Subch. E § 2.7.3.D.9) — except clear zone area or where City participates in streetscape cost.
- **Pre-application meetings** — DSD intake conferences can lock in expectations and identify deal-breakers before formal application; valuable when overlays stack or PUD is in play.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **zoning-pathway.md** — Base district, all suffixes (MU, V/VMU, CO, NP, NCCD, ETOD, DB90, UNO, WO, CVC, AO), watershed classification, jurisdiction (full purpose / limited purpose / ETJ), DDZ vs DWPZ.
- **neighborhood-plan.md** — NP combining district notes, FLUM designation (note: policy only).
- **overlays.md** — All overlay layers from COA GIS (Capitol View, Capitol Dominance, Hill Country, Airport, WO subdistrict if applicable, TOD subdistrict, ETOD subdistrict, HCRC intensity zone).
- **adjacency.md** — Adjacent parcels' zoning *and* dwelling unit counts within 75 ft (for Article 10 triggering property test); existing structure heights and locations on triggering properties.
- **programs.md** — DDBP eligibility (downtown Figure 2), DB90 eligibility, VMU/V opt-in status, AU eligibility, SMART Housing eligibility, ETOD subdistrict, NBG/ERC/Plaza Saltillo TOD status, ERC Hub status.
- **property-records.md** — Recorded restrictive covenants (height, use, parking), Unified Development Agreement, prior approved site plans (may impose tighter standards than current zoning), conditional overlay ordinances, NCCD ordinance.
- **case-history.md (AMANDA)** — Prior cases, pending amendments, Vested Rights Determination (written Director determination required to operate a Chapter 245 vesting claim), Land Status Determination case number.
- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — Proposed use(s) by LDC name, building dimensions per building, total GFA, unit count by bedroom type, parking count, building footprint, IC/coverage estimates.

## Output structure

```markdown

- Procedural path: <admin | conditional use | rezoning | density bonus + admin>

## Zoning capacity table
| Standard | Code limit | Modifier (overlay, bonus) | Effective limit | Proposed | Status |
| Use | <permitted list> | <CO restrictions> | <effective> | <use> | <pass/conditional/prohibited> |
| Height | <ft from § 25-2-492> | <CVC plane, AU bonus, DB90, Compatibility cap> | <effective ft> | <proposed ft> | <pass/fail/data-gap> |
| FAR | <X:1 from § 25-2-492> | <DDBP/DB90/VMU exemption> | <effective> | <proposed> | ... |

| Setbacks (front / side / rear / street side) | <§ 25-2-492 / § 25-2-601> | <Compatibility § 25-2-1062, WO setback> | ... | ... | ... |

## Findings
```

## Severity heuristics

| Finding type | Severity |
|---|---|
| Proposed use is prohibited in base district and no rezoning path exists | `significant` |
| Proposed use conditional (Large Retail, late-hours CL, Child Care General); LUC/PC approval adds 4–9 months | `moderate` |
| Building height/FAR exceeds limit by >10% without identified density bonus | `significant` |
| Building height/FAR exceeds limit by ≤10% and a density bonus is plausibly available | `moderate` |
| Article 10 height limit (40 ft within 50 ft; 60 ft within 75 ft) violated and no AU exemption | `significant` |
| Article 10 compatibility buffer violated (encroachment of vertical structure, parking, or mechanical in 10-ft screening zone) | `moderate` |
| CVC plane elevation exceeded by any element (incl. mechanical — no § 25-2-531 exception) | `significant` |
| Hill Country natural-area minimum (40%) not met | `significant` |
| WO primary setback violated (e.g., 150 ft from Town Lake in Rainey) | `significant` |
| WO secondary setback IC >30% | `moderate` |
| Hazardous pipeline 200-ft new construction zone, no Fire Chief determination | `significant` |
| HOME Phase 1/2 eligibility unlocks 2–3 unit infill on what looks like an SF-only lot | `opportunity` |
| Citywide parking elimination — concept plan still showing minimums | `opportunity` (drop the parking; reclaim site area) |
| ETOD Subdistrict 1 eligibility with 90–120 ft height tier | `opportunity` |
| AU eligibility (≥50% affordable) unlocks 1.5× height and Article 10 exemption | `opportunity` |
| VMU 60% parking reduction available with affordability covenant | `opportunity` |
| DDBP available but FAR/height already at primary entitlement (no bonus needed) | `note` |
| Overlay adds design-review with predictable conditions (e.g., PARD WO review, ABIA AO review) | `note` |
| Adjacent dwelling-unit count not in GIS — Article 10 triggering test requires field verification | `data-gap` |
| Zoning case recently approved but not yet on GIS | `data-gap` |
| PUD ordinance not in Bureau or NCCD adopting ordinance not retrievable | `data-gap` |
| Vested rights claimed without written Director determination | `data-gap` |

## Common pitfalls

- **Confusing FLUM (Imagine Austin policy) with zoning.** FLUM does not establish zoning; rezones still require § 25-2-281 process.
- **Applying repealed Article 10 (50/100/300/540 ft bands)** to post-July 2024 plans. Current code: 50 ft and 75 ft only. Compatibility waivers under former §§ 25-2-1081/1082 no longer exist.
- **Citing § 25-2-1064 / 25-2-1066 / 25-2-1067** for lighting, parking screening, or noise — all repealed; current authority is § 25-2-1063.
- **Treating SF-6 as a triggering property.** SF-6 is less restrictive than SF-5. Only LA, RR, SF-1 through SF-5 qualify, AND the lot must contain 1–3 dwelling units.
- **Applying parking minimums anywhere except inside a PUD with a parking exhibit, or under UNO (where it's a maximum).** Minimums were eliminated November 13, 2023.
- **Citing "Type CT" site plan designation.** Abolished November 13, 2023 along with parking minimums. Only relevant for amendments to pre-Nov 2023 plans.
- **Measuring building height from finished floor or from the lowest grade.** § 25-1-21(50) requires the *average* of highest and lowest adjacent grades at the building perimeter.
- **Citing § 25-2-531 height exceptions on CVC sites.** Inapplicable per § 25-2-642(B). All rooftop elements (mechanical, parapets, elevator overruns) count against the CVC plane.
- **Confusing § 25-2-641 (Capitol Dominance) with § 25-2-642 (CVC).** They are different overlays with different geometry.
- **Counting overlay setbacks as additive to base setbacks** when the overlay replaces them, or vice versa. Check the overlay text — usually the more restrictive governs (§ 25-2-492(B)) but PUDs/regulating plans may supersede.
- **Including atria airspace or enclosed loading berths in GFA.** § 25-1-21(47) excludes them. Loading docks (not berths) ARE included.
- **Treating bulk-purpose GFA and parking-calculation GFA as the same number.** Bike rooms and shower facilities only reduce GFA for parking purposes (§ 25-6-472(C)), not for FAR or benchmarking.
- **Subtracting floodplain, CWQZ, or slopes from Gross Site Area for FAR.** GSA is the unmodified site area; only formally dedicated ROW is excluded.
- **Treating SMART Housing as a 40-year covenant.** SMART Housing affordability is 1 yr owner / 5 yr rental (§ 25-1-705). 40-year obligations come from UNO, VMU, AU, DDBP, NBG, Plaza Saltillo, or Rainey programs.
- **Submitting a Conditional Approval letter from Austin Energy Green Building in place of the Letter of Intent at site plan stage.** LOI must be co-signed by AEGB staff at site plan stage (BCM 7.1.3.2).
- **Asserting Chapter 245 vesting in a narrative without a Director's written Vested Rights Determination under § 25-1-541.** The claim is inoperative until issued.
- **Citing a PUD ordinance number without confirming it is the most recently amended version.** Tracking tables (DU, IC, GFA, VTD/PHT) must reflect the current ordinance after all amendments.
- **Assuming Subchapter E categorically does not apply to PUD sites.** Subch. E § 1.2.5(B) is provision-by-provision; commercial/retail/mixed-use PUDs were required to comply with Subch. E as a Tier One condition (§ 2.3.2(A)).
- **Citing the wrong IFC edition in fire-related notes.** Austin adopted the **2024 IFC** per Ord. 20250410-039, effective July 10, 2025 (superseded 2021 IFC).
- **Using the form "Watershed Protection and Development Review Department," "PDRD," or other predecessor names** in approval blocks or AW construction notes — the department name is **Development Services Department**.

    30→| Light rail corridor proximity (Project Connect) | UROP consultation; Downtown Rail Corridor Permit for 4th St corridor | CapMetro / DSD | Site-specific |
    31→| Hill Country Roadway Corridor (1,000 ft of Loop 360, RM 620, RM 2222, RM 2244, SW Pkwy) | All on-site utilities underground unless utility provider requires otherwise | DSD | At site plan |
    32→| New streets, private drives, or new addresses | 911 Addressing / AMS reservation and addressing plan approval | Address Management Services | 2–4 weeks; gates site plan approval |
    33→
    34→Note: ESPA is normally submitted **after** DSD site plan approval, not before (AEDC 1.4.2.7.A). Build the AE design into the diligence timeline as a post-approval, pre-permit critical path item — not as a parallel-with-site-plan item.
    35→
    36→## Constraints to evaluate
    37→
    38→### Overhead clearance & undergrounding
    39→
    40→- **Building footprint vs. 15-ft radial / 7.5-ft sky-to-ground clearance** from any AE overhead distribution conductor on or adjacent to the site (UCM § 1.10.3). Both apply simultaneously; the outer conductor (not pole centerline) is the datum. Evaluate whether the desired building envelope physically clears overhead lines along the relevant frontage, and if not, whether undergrounding the offending span is feasible and at what cost.
    41→- **10-ft overhead utility zone** from energized conductor where overhead lines remain on a Core Transit Corridor or Urban Roadway frontage (LDC Subchapter E § 2.2.2.B.3.b; § 2.2.3.B.3). Same 10-ft zone applies inside Plaza Saltillo TOD (§ 3.3.2.A.3.b) and NBG (§ 3.3.2.B.4.b). Confirm whether the frontage street triggers Subchapter E or a regulating plan, then whether overhead is feasible to underground vs. relocate to rear-of-site.
    42→- **Building-to-property-line undergrounding** mandatory on all CTC, Urban Roadway, Plaza Saltillo TOD, NBG, and Hill Country Roadway Corridor frontages (LDC Subchapter E § 2.2.2.B.3.a, § 2.2.3.B.3; Plaza Saltillo TOD § 3.3.2.A.3 / .3.3.A.3 / .3.4.A.3; NBG § 3.3.2.B.4.a; LDC § 25-2-1125). Budget service-lateral undergrounding cost.
    43→- **ROW undergrounding "to the maximum extent practicable"** on the same frontages (same citations). This is judgment-driven; expect AE to negotiate which existing overhead is left in place vs. relocated to rear of site. Identify the existing overhead pattern early.
    44→- **Transmission proximity** (60 kV+: 69 / 138 / 345 kV AE circuits): clearance envelopes are site-specific and require AE engineering (UCM § 1.14.3.1); circuits cannot be de-energized for nearby work. If a transmission line or labeled transmission easement abuts the site, treat as a binding envelope constraint and engage AE Transmission before locking massing. 25-ft × 16-ft vertical ROW access corridor must be preserved throughout construction (UCM § 1.14.4); plat notes per AEDC 1.16.0(8) become mandatory.
    45→- **Service-drop vertical clearance** over driveways and access — 16 ft (no-truck) / 18 ft (truck/public street) (UCM § 1.10.6.2). Constrains canopy/porte-cochère height and loading-dock geometry.
    46→
    47→### Underground routing & easements
    48→
    49→- **AW planting-zone prohibition** (UCM § 2.9.1.C): no AW main, service, or appurtenance within the ROW street-tree planting zone. Root barriers required 7 ft from trunk; 2-ft AW offset from barrier; minimum 8-ft Street Tree Utility Gap between zones. Constrains where water service can leave the building when street trees are required.
    50→- **No parallel routing within AE / public utility easement** (UCM § 2.9.1.A.3) — only perpendicular or up to 45° crossings. Constrains site utility layout when easements bisect the parcel.
    51→- **Easement encroachment**: no permanent structures, pools, or buildings in AE easements (UCM § 1.10.10.2); landscaping/paving/walls in private AE easements require License Agreement from AE Public Involvement (UCM § 1.10.10.3); same items in public utility easements / public ROW require Chapter 14 license (§ 14-11-41). Evaluate whether the desired site plan crosses easements and whether the licensing pathway is workable.
    52→- **Transformer pad siting** (UCM §§ 1.5.2.6, 1.10.4): hot-stick (padlocked) side 10 ft from any adjacent building; non-operator sides 3 ft from fence; operator side 5 ft; pad within 6 ft of paved truck-accessible surface; pad must be on customer property (not ROW or parkland); dedicated AE easement encumbers the pad. Reserve ~150–250 sf of usable frontage for the pad early in concept design.
    53→- **AE truck access** (UCM § 1.3.16): 12-ft horizontal × 16-ft vertical clear path to AE equipment, with 20 × 35 ft set-up area at 35-ft vertical clearance. AE facilities normally at front of property or adjacent to paved surface (UCM § 1.3.15).
    54→- **AE underground separations** (UCM § 1.10.5.A): 12 in min from other utilities at perpendicular crossings; 36 in from ≥60 psi gas. Joint trench with other utilities requires written AE agreement.
    55→- **Water/wastewater main crossings** (UCM § 2.9.1.B.3, § 2.9.2.B.17): 12 in (AW above) / 18 in (AW below) for open-cut; trenchless = greater of 2× excavation diameter or 36 in.
    56→- **ROW assignment / 24-in proximity** (§ 14-11-180(C)): facilities within 24 in of an existing ROW facility require AULCC ROW assignment change approval — a process, not a prohibition, but it consumes time.
    57→- **Light rail corridors**: UCM § 5.2.2 Downtown Rail Corridor Permit for E-W 4th Street corridor (IH-35 to Seaholm); UROP consultation for other Project Connect alignments. Materially affects feasibility for parcels along Project Connect.
    58→- **Moonlight towers** (downtown / central Austin): 25-ft ROW-installation prohibition (§ 14-11-205); 100-ft permit threshold for any construction near tower or guy wire (§ 14-11-201). Locations are not mapped in code — confirm by field survey early if site is in downtown or central Austin.
    59→
    60→### Drainage-utility interactions
    61→
    62→- **SCM staging area + maintenance access drive vertical clearance**: 14 ft from existing/proposed vegetation at maturity (DCM § 1.2.4.E.2.e and § 1.2.4.E.1.e.ii). Applies to COA-maintained and residential-development SCMs above 5,000 cf / 3-ft depth thresholds. Constrains canopy planting along maintenance routes.
    63→- **No utility routing under detention/retention ponds** (reviewer convention; common-violation pattern). Affects site utility layout when ponds dominate the site.
    64→- **Storm drain manhole vs. AE pole separation**: minimum 5 ft horizontal between storm drain manholes and AE overhead poles (reviewer convention). Constrains drainage outfall layout where existing poles are present.
    65→- **Encasement under roads/structures** (UCM § 2.9.1.D): encased crossings under roadways require material, dimensional, and longitudinal extent specifications on plans. Budget bored/encased crossings on any utility leaving the site under a public street.
    66→
    67→### Construction-phase impacts
    68→
    69→- **Transmission demolition sequence** (UCM § 1.14.9): pre-construction safety meeting ≥48 hr before work; barricades 10 ft from all transmission structures including guys/anchors; warning signs under overhead facilities; no spoils or materials in transmission easement; crane and temporary-structure setbacks so they cannot fall within 20 ft of transmission. Forces an alternate spoils/laydown area when transmission abuts the site.
    70→- **Work-zone vertical clearance below overhead** (UCM § 1.10.6.2; § 1.3.16): 18 ft where truck traffic is anticipated; 16 ft for affirmatively non-truck driveways; 35 ft set-up area in front of AE equipment. Affects crane staging and tilt-up sequencing.
    71→
    72→### Connectivity & frontage
    73→
    74→- **Table B utility-in-drive-aisle option** (LDC Subchapter E § 2.3.1.B.2): on subject sites (≥3 ac nonresidential, or surface parking between building and principal street), site must select ≥2 Table B options (3 if parking >125% of formerly required). Routing utilities under parking stalls is only a deficiency if utility-in-drive-aisle is the selected option but not implemented, or if Table B count is otherwise short. Evaluate whether the site can hit its Table B count without forcing utilities under parking.
    75→
    76→### Administrative & service-capacity
    77→
    78→- **AE Service Availability Letter** (AEDC § 1.4.1) — only where it is unclear which utility serves the site. Confirm AE service area on edge-of-territory parcels before design.
    79→- **Service capacity**: AE Design has sole authority over available voltage / service characteristics (AEDC § 1.3.2). For large loads (>320 A continuous → instrument-rated CT service per AEDC § 1.4.0; or any Network Area service downtown), engage AE Design early; available capacity at the nearest feeder may itself be a constraint.
    80→- **Street lighting**: AE develops the lighting installation plan. Developer responsibilities differ by location (AEDC §§ 1.6.4–1.6.7). Inside the Great Streets boundary (MLK / Lady Bird Lake / IH-35 / Lamar), Chapter 6 dictates fixture type (Gardco Circa/Form 10; Kim ERA), spacing (8 poles/block), and mounting heights (24-ft street / 12-ft pedestrian) — non-standard poles permitted at developer cost differential.
    81→- **Four mandatory Standard AE Plan Notes** (verbatim) plus AEDC § 1.16.0(7) site-specific notes. Missing or altered text = rejection. Low-effort compliance issue but a frequent rejection cause.
    82→- **AULCC Completeness Letter** gates ROW Review approval.
    83→- **Addressing plan approval** (AMS) — distinct from an Address Validation Letter; AVL is **not** an approved addressing plan (common confusion). Gates site plan approval when new addresses or street names are involved.
    84→
    85→## Opportunities to evaluate
    86→
    87→- **Frontage selection on corner lots**: CTC designation takes priority as principal street; if a non-CTC corner is the practical service frontage, undergrounding cost may concentrate there. Conversely, choosing the non-CTC face for the building front can avoid the 10-ft overhead zone constraint on the CTC frontage entirely.
    88→- **CTC short-lot alternative tree exception** (LDC Subchapter E § 2.2.2.B.3.c; Plaza Saltillo TOD § 3.3.2.A.3.c): on lots ≤120 ft deep, utility-compatible alternative tree species may be used **beneath** the overhead utilities rather than offset from them. Avoids removing/relocating street trees to clear an overhead corridor.
    89→- **Plaza Saltillo TOD § 3.3.2.A.3.c facade-setback alternative**: same alternative-tree path also available when full compliance would push the facade ≥30 ft beyond the curb face. Material on tight TOD parcels.
    90→- **AE relocation at customer expense** (UCM § 1.3.19): AE will relocate facilities at the customer's expense where feasible; build the cost into the pro forma rather than treating overhead as immovable. Note that AE will not relocate to an adjacent property without that owner's written consent — that consent is a feasibility variable.
    91→- **UCM § 2.9.6 waiver pathway**: applicants who cannot meet UCM § 2 requirements have a formal waiver route. Worth evaluating on constrained urban sites instead of forcing a redesign.
    92→- **Sub-AULCC-threshold scoping**: if ROW utility work can be kept below 300 LF citywide (or 25 LF in DAPCZ), with no pole relocations and no main assignments, AULCC review is avoided entirely. On small infill projects this can compress the schedule by 2–4 months — evaluate whether trenching can be confined to private property.
    93→- **Rear-of-site undergrounding** vs. front-frontage undergrounding: where alley or rear access exists, "maximum extent practicable" can be argued for relocation to the rear, sometimes reducing the lateral length compared with undergrounding the entire frontage span.
    94→- **Service-Only ESPA path**: keeping the total load under 350 A single-phase / 225 A three-phase (non-network) keeps the project on the Service-Only path and out of Design Services — a meaningful schedule compression where load can be managed.
    95→- **AE License Agreement vs. easement relocation**: many AE-easement encroachments (paving, retaining walls, landscaping) can be resolved through a License Agreement from AE Public Involvement (UCM § 1.10.10.3) rather than relocating the easement. Faster and cheaper, when AE will agree.
    96→- **Plat-note compliance for transmission easements**: where a transmission easement crosses the site, the AEDC § 1.16.0(8) plat notes (AE tree pruning, additional easement provision, erosion control, NESC clearance, 24-hr AE access, 48,000-lb axle load roads, 48-hr notice) are mandatory but can be added to the plat at low cost — treat as administrative, not feasibility-blocking, unless coupled with a physical envelope conflict.

    98→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
    99→
   100→- **environmental.md** / **GIS** — Plaza Saltillo TOD boundary, NBG boundary, CTC/Urban Roadway frontage classification, Hill Country Roadway Corridor proximity (1,000 ft of named roadways), DAPCZ boundary (Code § 14-11-161(7)), Great Streets boundary, light rail corridor proximity, parkland boundaries.
   101→- **utility-survey.md** — existing overhead and underground AE facilities on or adjacent to site (poles, conductors, vaults, transformers, guys/anchors); transmission easement boundaries; existing AE easements / PUEs; existing ROW utilities (AW mains, gas, telecom); existing moonlight towers if downtown/central.
   102→- **transportation.md** — frontage street classifications; truck-access expectations (for service-drop 16 vs. 18 ft determination); driveway locations.
   103→- **property-records.md** — recorded easements (private AE, PUE, transmission, drainage); plat notes referencing transmission easement obligations.
   104→- **zoning.md** — base zoning + any regulating-plan overlay (Plaza Saltillo TOD subdistrict, NBG subdistrict prefix TOD/CMU/NMU/NR/WMU/CI, UNO, ERC, downtown).
   105→- **program intent** — service-load estimate (amps / phase), continuous-load expectation, presence of vaults or generators, exterior wall modifications (for BSPA trigger).
   106→
   107→## Output structure
   108→
   109→Standard discipline output shape — see `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.
   110→
   111→## Severity heuristics
   112→
   113→| Finding | Severity |
   114→|---|---|
   115→| Transmission line on or abutting site with envelope conflict that cannot be cleared without relocating the line | `significant` |
   116→| AE service capacity insufficient at the nearest feeder for projected load (Network Area downtown or large industrial) | `significant` |
   117→| Required overhead-to-underground conversion along entire CTC/Urban Roadway frontage materially impacts pro forma | `significant` |
   118→| Site within 25 ft of a moonlight tower (ROW prohibition) blocking proposed ROW work | `significant` |
   119→| 10-ft overhead utility zone (Subchapter E / Plaza Saltillo / NBG) crosses desired building footprint with no short-lot alternative-tree exception | `significant` |
   120→| AULCC trigger met (≥300 LF citywide, ≥25 LF DAPCZ, pole relocation, main assignment) — adds 2–4 months schedule | `moderate` |
   121→| Hill Country Roadway Corridor — all on-site utilities must go underground; cost adder vs. mixed-mode | `moderate` |
   122→| Transformer pad placement constrains frontage usable width or requires AE easement reservation | `moderate` |
   123→| AW planting-zone routing conflict requires re-routing water service away from frontage | `moderate` |
   124→| Site within 100 ft of moonlight tower or guy wire — permit required, no prohibition | `moderate` |
   125→| Light rail corridor proximity (non-4th Street) — UROP consultation required | `moderate` |
   126→| Service-load size pushes project from Service-Only to Design Services ESPA path | `note` |
   127→| Standard AE plan notes verbatim compliance | `note` |
   128→| Addressing plan / street-name reservation required for new private drives | `note` |
   129→| Existing AE facility locations not field-verified (only AE record-drawing data) | `data-gap` |
   130→| Moonlight tower proximity unknown (downtown / central Austin site without field survey) | `data-gap` |
   131→| AE Service Availability uncertain at parcel (edge of service territory) | `data-gap` |
   132→
   133→## Common pitfalls
   134→
   135→- Treating "the utility provider operates overhead in the vicinity" as authorization to leave the building-to-property-line service overhead on a CTC, Urban Roadway, Plaza Saltillo TOD, NBG, or Hill Country frontage — undergrounding is mandatory regardless.
   136→- Anchoring overhead clearance dimensions to the **pole centerline** rather than the **outermost conductor** — on three-phase configurations the outer conductor may be several feet offset; clearances that appear adequate on plan can be non-compliant in the field.
   137→- Conflating the UCM § 1.10.3 universal 7.5-ft / 15-ft clearances (apply everywhere overhead AE exists) with the LDC Subchapter E 10-ft overhead utility zone (applies only on CTC / Urban Roadway / Plaza Saltillo / NBG). Both can apply simultaneously on those frontages; only UCM 1.10.3 applies elsewhere.
   138→- Assuming AULCC is universal — it is only triggered by the four specific thresholds. Small infill projects often slide under and shouldn't carry AULCC time in the schedule.
   139→- Citing **§ 14-11-205** for the 100-ft moonlight tower permit — that section is the 25-ft ROW prohibition. The 100-ft permit threshold is **§ 14-11-201**.
   140→- Citing **LDC § 25-9-173** for service availability — this section does not exist; correct authority is AEDC §§ 1.4.1 / 1.3.2.
   141→- Accepting an Address Validation Letter (AVL) as an approved addressing plan — they are distinct; the addressing plan must be separately approved by AMS before site plan approval.
   142→- Assuming Hill Country undergrounding applies near US 183 or US 290 West — LDC § 25-2-1104(A) carves these out; only the five named Hill Country Roadways trigger § 25-2-1125.
   143→- Drawing transformer pad in the public ROW or labeling its area as parkland — both prohibited; the pad must be on customer property within a dedicated AE easement.
   144→- Treating UCM § 2.9.1.A.1 as the basis for pole/transmission separation rules — that section governs easement width, not pole placement; the pole-placement requirement currently lacks a confirmed code anchor and should be coordinated with AE directly.
   145→- Routing non-electrical utilities parallel within an AE / public utility easement boundary — only perpendicular (up to 45°) crossings are permitted.
   146→- Failing to budget post-approval ESPA time — ESPA is submitted after site plan approval; AE design can run 6–12 weeks (Service-Only) to 16+ weeks (Design Services / Network Area) before an Electric Permit number is issued, gating downstream work.
   147→- Confusing the Building Service Planning Application (BSPA — required for building permits with exterior modifications) with the ESPA (required for new/modified electric service). Both can apply.
   148→- Sizing transformer pads to a "standard" 10×10 dimension — pad dimensions are determined by AE Design based on the customer's AutoCAD submittal (UCM § 1.5.2.6); no universal fixed dimension exists in code text.
   149→- Showing a vault near overhead power lines with a plan note "vault approved by AE Design" but no AE written clearance letter in the project file — UCM § 1.10.3 requires the letter to be filed, not merely referenced.
   150→- Routing AE underground conduit in a joint trench with other utilities without a written AE joint-trench agreement (UCM § 1.10.5.A) — the 12-in separation rule covers perpendicular crossings only; parallel/joint runs require the separate agreement.
   151→

# Electrical & Utility Feasibility — Austin

## Domain

Electrical utility service (Austin Energy), street lighting, overhead conductor clearances, underground utility routing, easement and ROW coordination, AULCC clearance, moonlight tower buffers, and addressing. Excludes water/wastewater main sizing (covered in `wwp`), drainage facilities themselves (covered in `sduf`/`fwp`), and tree/landscape conflicts (covered in `eptp`). This discipline determines whether the desired massing, frontage, and parking layout can be served by AE under the applicable corridor/regulating-plan framework — and what coordination timelines that triggers.

## Authoritative sources

- Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual (AEDC): §§ 1.3, 1.4, 1.6, 1.16
- Utility Criteria Manual (UCM): §§ 1.3, 1.5, 1.10, 1.14, 2.5.1.F, 2.9, 3.2, 3.4, 3.8, 5.2
- Land Development Code (LDC): Subchapter E §§ 2.2.2.B.3, 2.2.3.B.3, 2.3.1.B.2; §§ 25-2-1103, 25-2-1104(A), 25-2-1125
- Drainage Criteria Manual (DCM): § 1.2.4.E (SCM clearances)
- COA Code Title 14 (ROW): §§ 14-11-41, 14-11-180(C), 14-11-201, 14-11-205
- Plaza Saltillo TOD Regulating Plan §§ 3.3.2–3.3.4
- North Burnet/Gateway (NBG) Regulating Plan § 3.3.2.B.4
- Great Streets Master Plan, Chapter 6 (lighting)
- City of Austin Addressing Standards (AMS / 911 Addressing)
- External: OSHA 1910.333; Texas H&S Code § 752.004; NESC

## Regulatory pathway

| Trigger | Path | Decision body | Typical duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Any new/modified electric service | Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) to AE; resubmit after Electric Permit issuance | Austin Energy Design | 6–12 weeks after site plan approval |
| Service >350 A single-phase / >225 A three-phase, or any service in downtown Network Area | ESPA via Design Services (full AE Design involvement) | AE Design Services | Add 4–8 weeks vs. Service-Only |
| AE facilities proposed on private property | Electrical easement dedication on standard City forms before AE installs | AE Public Involvement | 4–6 weeks |
| ≥300 LF ROW utility work citywide; ≥25 LF in DAPCZ; any pole relocation; main assignments | AULCC review → Completeness Letter | AULCC (multi-utility committee) | 8–16 weeks; gates ROW Review approval |
| ≥48-hour pre-construction notice + safety meeting near transmission | AE Transmission engineering | AE Transmission | Per-event |
| Within 100 ft of moonlight tower or guy wire | COA § 14-11-201 permit (building official for private; director for ROW) | Building Official / Director | Concurrent with permitting |
| Light rail corridor proximity (Project Connect) | UROP consultation; Downtown Rail Corridor Permit for 4th St corridor | CapMetro / DSD | Site-specific |
| Hill Country Roadway Corridor (1,000 ft of Loop 360, RM 620, RM 2222, RM 2244, SW Pkwy) | All on-site utilities underground unless utility provider requires otherwise | DSD | At site plan |
| New streets, private drives, or new addresses | 911 Addressing / AMS reservation and addressing plan approval | Address Management Services | 2–4 weeks; gates site plan approval |

### Construction-phase impacts

- **Transmission demolition sequence** (UCM § 1.14.9): pre-construction safety meeting ≥48 hr before work; barricades 10 ft from all transmission structures including guys/anchors; warning signs under overhead facilities; no spoils or materials in transmission easement; crane and temporary-structure setbacks so they cannot fall within 20 ft of transmission. Forces an alternate spoils/laydown area when transmission abuts the site.
- **Work-zone vertical clearance below overhead** (UCM § 1.10.6.2; § 1.3.16): 18 ft where truck traffic is anticipated; 16 ft for affirmatively non-truck driveways; 35 ft set-up area in front of AE equipment. Affects crane staging and tilt-up sequencing.

### Connectivity & frontage

- **Table B utility-in-drive-aisle option** (LDC Subchapter E § 2.3.1.B.2): on subject sites (≥3 ac nonresidential, or surface parking between building and principal street), site must select ≥2 Table B options (3 if parking >125% of formerly required). Routing utilities under parking stalls is only a deficiency if utility-in-drive-aisle is the selected option but not implemented, or if Table B count is otherwise short. Evaluate whether the site can hit its Table B count without forcing utilities under parking.

### Administrative & service-capacity

- **AE Service Availability Letter** (AEDC § 1.4.1) — only where it is unclear which utility serves the site. Confirm AE service area on edge-of-territory parcels before design.
- **Service capacity**: AE Design has sole authority over available voltage / service characteristics (AEDC § 1.3.2). For large loads (>320 A continuous → instrument-rated CT service per AEDC § 1.4.0; or any Network Area service downtown), engage AE Design early; available capacity at the nearest feeder may itself be a constraint.
- **Street lighting**: AE develops the lighting installation plan. Developer responsibilities differ by location (AEDC §§ 1.6.4–1.6.7). Inside the Great Streets boundary (MLK / Lady Bird Lake / IH-35 / Lamar), Chapter 6 dictates fixture type (Gardco Circa/Form 10; Kim ERA), spacing (8 poles/block), and mounting heights (24-ft street / 12-ft pedestrian) — non-standard poles permitted at developer cost differential.
- **Four mandatory Standard AE Plan Notes** (verbatim) plus AEDC § 1.16.0(7) site-specific notes. Missing or altered text = rejection. Low-effort compliance issue but a frequent rejection cause.
- **AULCC Completeness Letter** gates ROW Review approval.
- **Addressing plan approval** (AMS) — distinct from an Address Validation Letter; AVL is **not** an approved addressing plan (common confusion). Gates site plan approval when new addresses or street names are involved.

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **Frontage selection on corner lots**: CTC designation takes priority as principal street; if a non-CTC corner is the practical service frontage, undergrounding cost may concentrate there. Conversely, choosing the non-CTC face for the building front can avoid the 10-ft overhead zone constraint on the CTC frontage entirely.
- **CTC short-lot alternative tree exception** (LDC Subchapter E § 2.2.2.B.3.c; Plaza Saltillo TOD § 3.3.2.A.3.c): on lots ≤120 ft deep, utility-compatible alternative tree species may be used **beneath** the overhead utilities rather than offset from them. Avoids removing/relocating street trees to clear an overhead corridor.
- **Plaza Saltillo TOD § 3.3.2.A.3.c facade-setback alternative**: same alternative-tree path also available when full compliance would push the facade ≥30 ft beyond the curb face. Material on tight TOD parcels.
- **AE relocation at customer expense** (UCM § 1.3.19): AE will relocate facilities at the customer's expense where feasible; build the cost into the pro forma rather than treating overhead as immovable. Note that AE will not relocate to an adjacent property without that owner's written consent — that consent is a feasibility variable.
- **UCM § 2.9.6 waiver pathway**: applicants who cannot meet UCM § 2 requirements have a formal waiver route. Worth evaluating on constrained urban sites instead of forcing a redesign.
- **Sub-AULCC-threshold scoping**: if ROW utility work can be kept below 300 LF citywide (or 25 LF in DAPCZ), with no pole relocations and no main assignments, AULCC review is avoided entirely. On small infill projects this can compress the schedule by 2–4 months — evaluate whether trenching can be confined to private property.
- **Rear-of-site undergrounding** vs. front-frontage undergrounding: where alley or rear access exists, "maximum extent practicable" can be argued for relocation to the rear, sometimes reducing the lateral length compared with undergrounding the entire frontage span.
- **Service-Only ESPA path**: keeping the total load under 350 A single-phase / 225 A three-phase (non-network) keeps the project on the Service-Only path and out of Design Services — a meaningful schedule compression where load can be managed.
- **AE License Agreement vs. easement relocation**: many AE-easement encroachments (paving, retaining walls, landscaping) can be resolved through a License Agreement from AE Public Involvement (UCM § 1.10.10.3) rather than relocating the easement. Faster and cheaper, when AE will agree.
- **Plat-note compliance for transmission easements**: where a transmission easement crosses the site, the AEDC § 1.16.0(8) plat notes (AE tree pruning, additional easement provision, erosion control, NESC clearance, 24-hr AE access, 48,000-lb axle load roads, 48-hr notice) are mandatory but can be added to the plat at low cost — treat as administrative, not feasibility-blocking, unless coupled with a physical envelope conflict.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **environmental.md** / **GIS** — Plaza Saltillo TOD boundary, NBG boundary, CTC/Urban Roadway frontage classification, Hill Country Roadway Corridor proximity (1,000 ft of named roadways), DAPCZ boundary (Code § 14-11-161(7)), Great Streets boundary, light rail corridor proximity, parkland boundaries.
- **utility-survey.md** — existing overhead and underground AE facilities on or adjacent to site (poles, conductors, vaults, transformers, guys/anchors); transmission easement boundaries; existing AE easements / PUEs; existing ROW utilities (AW mains, gas, telecom); existing moonlight towers if downtown/central.
- **transportation.md** — frontage street classifications; truck-access expectations (for service-drop 16 vs. 18 ft determination); driveway locations.
- **property-records.md** — recorded easements (private AE, PUE, transmission, drainage); plat notes referencing transmission easement obligations.
- **zoning.md** — base zoning + any regulating-plan overlay (Plaza Saltillo TOD subdistrict, NBG subdistrict prefix TOD/CMU/NMU/NR/WMU/CI, UNO, ERC, downtown).
- **program intent** — service-load estimate (amps / phase), continuous-load expectation, presence of vaults or generators, exterior wall modifications (for BSPA trigger).

## Output structure

Standard discipline output shape — see `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.

## Severity heuristics

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| Transmission line on or abutting site with envelope conflict that cannot be cleared without relocating the line | `significant` |
| AE service capacity insufficient at the nearest feeder for projected load (Network Area downtown or large industrial) | `significant` |
| Required overhead-to-underground conversion along entire CTC/Urban Roadway frontage materially impacts pro forma | `significant` |
| Site within 25 ft of a moonlight tower (ROW prohibition) blocking proposed ROW work | `significant` |
| 10-ft overhead utility zone (Subchapter E / Plaza Saltillo / NBG) crosses desired building footprint with no short-lot alternative-tree exception | `significant` |
| AULCC trigger met (≥300 LF citywide, ≥25 LF DAPCZ, pole relocation, main assignment) — adds 2–4 months schedule | `moderate` |
| Hill Country Roadway Corridor — all on-site utilities must go underground; cost adder vs. mixed-mode | `moderate` |
| Transformer pad placement constrains frontage usable width or requires AE easement reservation | `moderate` |
| AW planting-zone routing conflict requires re-routing water service away from frontage | `moderate` |
| Site within 100 ft of moonlight tower or guy wire — permit required, no prohibition | `moderate` |
| Light rail corridor proximity (non-4th Street) — UROP consultation required | `moderate` |
| Service-load size pushes project from Service-Only to Design Services ESPA path | `note` |
| Standard AE plan notes verbatim compliance | `note` |
| Addressing plan / street-name reservation required for new private drives | `note` |
| Existing AE facility locations not field-verified (only AE record-drawing data) | `data-gap` |
| Moonlight tower proximity unknown (downtown / central Austin site without field survey) | `data-gap` |
| AE Service Availability uncertain at parcel (edge of service territory) | `data-gap` |

## Common pitfalls

- Treating "the utility provider operates overhead in the vicinity" as authorization to leave the building-to-property-line service overhead on a CTC, Urban Roadway, Plaza Saltillo TOD, NBG, or Hill Country frontage — undergrounding is mandatory regardless.
- Anchoring overhead clearance dimensions to the **pole centerline** rather than the **outermost conductor** — on three-phase configurations the outer conductor may be several feet offset; clearances that appear adequate on plan can be non-compliant in the field.
- Conflating the UCM § 1.10.3 universal 7.5-ft / 15-ft clearances (apply everywhere overhead AE exists) with the LDC Subchapter E 10-ft overhead utility zone (applies only on CTC / Urban Roadway / Plaza Saltillo / NBG). Both can apply simultaneously on those frontages; only UCM 1.10.3 applies elsewhere.
- Assuming AULCC is universal — it is only triggered by the four specific thresholds. Small infill projects often slide under and shouldn't carry AULCC time in the schedule.
- Citing **§ 14-11-205** for the 100-ft moonlight tower permit — that section is the 25-ft ROW prohibition. The 100-ft permit threshold is **§ 14-11-201**.
- Citing **LDC § 25-9-173** for service availability — this section does not exist; correct authority is AEDC §§ 1.4.1 / 1.3.2.
- Accepting an Address Validation Letter (AVL) as an approved addressing plan — they are distinct; the addressing plan must be separately approved by AMS before site plan approval.
- Assuming Hill Country undergrounding applies near US 183 or US 290 West — LDC § 25-2-1104(A) carves these out; only the five named Hill Country Roadways trigger § 25-2-1125.
- Drawing transformer pad in the public ROW or labeling its area as parkland — both prohibited; the pad must be on customer property within a dedicated AE easement.
- Treating UCM § 2.9.1.A.1 as the basis for pole/transmission separation rules — that section governs easement width, not pole placement; the pole-placement requirement currently lacks a confirmed code anchor and should be coordinated with AE directly.
- Routing non-electrical utilities parallel within an AE / public utility easement boundary — only perpendicular (up to 45°) crossings are permitted.
- Failing to budget post-approval ESPA time — ESPA is submitted after site plan approval; AE design can run 6–12 weeks (Service-Only) to 16+ weeks (Design Services / Network Area) before an Electric Permit number is issued, gating downstream work.
- Confusing the Building Service Planning Application (BSPA — required for building permits with exterior modifications) with the ESPA (required for new/modified electric service). Both can apply.
- Sizing transformer pads to a "standard" 10×10 dimension — pad dimensions are determined by AE Design based on the customer's AutoCAD submittal (UCM § 1.5.2.6); no universal fixed dimension exists in code text.
- Showing a vault near overhead power lines with a plan note "vault approved by AE Design" but no AE written clearance letter in the project file — UCM § 1.10.3 requires the letter to be filed, not merely referenced.
- Routing AE underground conduit in a joint trench with other utilities without a written AE joint-trench agreement (UCM § 1.10.5.A) — the 12-in separation rule covers perpendicular crossings only; parallel/joint runs require the separate agreement.
