# Floodplain & Waterway Protection Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Austin's FWP discipline encompasses three overlapping regulatory regimes that any waterway-adjacent or low-lying parcel must navigate: (1) federal FEMA SFHA / FIRM compliance, (2) the City of Austin's **stricter** fully-developed-conditions floodplain (with Atlas 14 rainfall data in updated watersheds), and (3) the environmental buffer system — Critical Water Quality Zone (CWQZ), Water Quality Transition Zone (WQTZ), Erosion Hazard Zone (EHZ), and Critical Environmental Feature (CEF) buffers — that surrounds classified waterways. Also in scope: floodplain modification analysis, no-rise certification for the COA floodway, finished floor elevation / freeboard, ASCE 24 structural compliance, watershed impervious cover limits, and the variance pathways (administrative, LUC, Council) that unlock relief.

Bridges to other disciplines: CWQZ overlaps with `el` (Environmental Landscape); impervious cover and water quality treatment overlap with `sde` (Site Drainage & Environmental); building elevations and FFE overlap with `sduf` (Site Development & Utilities Framework).

## Authoritative sources

- **FEMA FIRM panels** — current effective panels via msc.fema.gov; preliminary FIRMs if a watershed restudy is in progress
- **COA fully-developed 100-year floodplain** — derived from approved City regulatory hydraulic models intersected with site-specific topo (DCM 1.2.6.B); shown on COA GIS layer alongside FEMA
- **COA 25-year floodplain (= COA floodway)** — Atlas 14 areas: 25-yr fully developed; non-Atlas 14 areas: 100-yr fully developed pre-Atlas 14 (LDC § 25-12-52(11))
- **Land Development Code (LDC) Chapter 25-7** — Drainage / floodplain regulation (definitions § 25-7-2; calculation methods § 25-7-6; encroachment variances § 25-7-92; exceptions §§ 25-7-93, 25-7-95, 25-7-96; easement requirements § 25-7-152)
- **Land Development Code (LDC) Chapter 25-8** — Water Quality (CWQZ § 25-8-261; floodplain modification § 25-8-263; CWQZ uses § 25-8-281; cut/fill §§ 25-8-341 / 25-8-342; interbasin diversion § 25-8-365; admin variances § 25-8-42; LUC variances § 25-8-41)
- **LDC Chapter 25-12** — Floodplain administration (design flood elevation § 25-12-52; FFE / freeboard / floodproofing § 25-12-53; floodway no-rise / encroachment variances § 25-12-54)
- **Drainage Criteria Manual (DCM)** — Floodplain delineation methodology (§ 1.2.6); hydraulic study requirements (§§ 1.2.4–1.2.5); EHZ analysis procedure (Appendix E); Atlas 14 / TP40-TP49 (§ 2.3.1); dam safety (§ 8.3.3.B); culvert headwater limits (§ 1.2.4.C/D)
- **Environmental Criteria Manual (ECM)** — Floodplain modification criteria (§ 1.7); FAFH (§ 1.7.4 + App. X); restoration ratios (§ 1.7.5); CWQZ buffer averaging (§ 1.5.2.D); EARZ basin liners (§ 1.6.2.C); CEF setbacks (§ 1.10); admin variance form (§ 1.3.3)
- **Rule R161-20.01** — Atlas 14 compliance (effective 2019-11-25)
- **ASCE 24-14** — Flood Resistant Design and Construction (referenced by LDC § 25-12-53)
- **Property records** — recorded drainage easements, plat notes, prior CLOMR/LOMR documentation, prior variance approvals

## Regulatory pathway

| Pathway | Decision body | Typical timeline | When triggered |
|---|---|---|---|
| Floodplain Development Permit | WPD / DSD floodplain administrator | concurrent with site plan | Any development in or affecting the 100-yr or 25-yr floodplain |
| CLOMC / CLOMR (FEMA) | FEMA + COA acknowledgment | 6–12 months for review; CLOMC acknowledgment required **before preliminary plan or site plan permit** | Pre-construction map revision (e.g. fill, channel work that alters FEMA SFHA) |
| LOMR (FEMA) | FEMA | 6–12 months; final acceptance required **before CO** | Post-construction map revision |
| Administrative environmental variance (LDC § 25-8-42) | WPD Director, no hearing | weeks; ECM 1.3.3 form required | Enumerated items only: cut/fill 4–8 ft in DDZ, CEF buffer reduction, interbasin diversion below threshold, etc. |
| LUC environmental variance (LDC § 25-8-41) | Land Use Commission after Environmental Commission recommendation | 3–6 months | Cut/fill >8 ft, cut/fill in DWPZ, CWQZ encroachment, floodplain modification with adverse impact, slopes >15%, within 100 ft of classified waterway |
| Floodplain encroachment variance (LDC § 25-7-92) | Council (or LUC under some scenarios) | 6+ months | Buildings or parking in 25-yr or 100-yr floodplain not covered by §§ 25-7-93 / 25-7-96 exceptions |
| Floodway encroachment variance (LDC § 25-12-54) | Council | 6+ months; **cannot be granted if any flood-level rise results** (§ 25-12-54(F)(5)) | Any work in COA 25-yr floodplain (floodway) with rise |
| Save Our Springs (Article 13) | **No variance available** | — | Any project in the Barton Springs Zone — SOS is inviolable |

Project file must show CLOMC acknowledgment letter from FEMA **before** preliminary plan / site plan permit issues; LOMC acknowledgment **before** final acceptance / BP; LOMR final acceptance **before** CO.

## Constraints to evaluate

### Mapping & delineation

- **Two floodplains, not one.** Always map both the FEMA SFHA (copy directly from current FIRM shapefile per DCM 1.2.6.B — do not re-delineate to onsite topo) and the COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain (derived from approved City hydraulic models intersected with site topo). For pre-feasibility, assume the COA boundary is larger than FEMA wherever Atlas 14 has been applied.
- **Hydraulic study trigger:** any creek, channel, or area of concentrated flow with ≥64 acres contributing drainage area requires a COA floodplain delineation (DCM 1.2.6.A.1). Below 64 acres, no COA floodplain is defined unless City or FEMA already mapped it.
- **Preliminary FIRM in process?** Check whether the watershed has a pending FEMA restudy. Using an effective FIRM when a preliminary is published is a common deficiency.

### Floodway (COA 25-yr) — the hardest constraint

- **0.00-ft rise standard.** Any encroachment in the COA 25-yr floodplain requires PE-certified zero rise, delivered as a **separate** sealed letter (LDC § 25-12-54(D)(11)) — not just the WSE comparison table.
- **Council cannot grant variance for floodway encroachment if any rise would result** (LDC § 25-12-54(F)(5)). Buildings, parking, or fill in the floodway with rise are categorically infeasible — design must avoid the floodway.

### 100-yr floodplain — buildings & parking

- Buildings and parking are prohibited in both 25-yr and 100-yr floodplains absent an enumerated exception (§ 25-7-93 for 100-yr; § 25-7-96 for 25-yr) or a Council encroachment variance (§ 25-7-92(C)) finding all seven criteria.
- **§ 25-7-93 exception conditions:** ≥2 ft above 100-yr WSE, volume compensation (compensatory storage), no additional adverse impact. Five enumerated categories (e.g. parking <5,000 sq ft with director "no adverse effect" determination).
- **Finished floor elevation:** minimum 2-ft freeboard above design flood elevation (LDC § 25-12-53(C)(1)). Design flood elevation = higher of Atlas 14 100-yr or FEMA 500-yr WSEL.
- **Safe access:** building access at or above 1 ft above DFE, equivalent to the Regulatory Flood Datum (LDC § 25-12-53(C)(4)(a)).
- **ASCE 24-14 certification** required for structures in the floodplain — separate engineer-sealed letter per structure type (retaining walls, fill, culverts, bridges, piers, fencing, buildings).
- **Below-grade structures, MEP equipment elevation, flood openings for enclosed areas, safe refuge space** — all separately addressed by LDC § 25-12-53.
- **Post-construction elevation certificate** (FEMA Form 086-0-33) by licensed surveyor — required prior to CO.

### Floodplain modification

- Any fill, grading, or channel work in the regulatory floodplain triggers LDC § 25-8-263 modification analysis: no-rise WSE, no increase in downstream peak flows, no loss of floodplain storage. WSE comparison table for 2/10/25/100-yr storms required.
- **Functional Assessment of Floodplain Health (FAFH)** per ECM 1.7.4 + Appendix X required for modifications. Zone-specific.
- **Restoration ratios (ECM 1.7.5):** Outside CWQZ (Zone 1): 2:1 / 3:1 / 4:1 for Poor / Fair / Good-or-Excellent condition (Good+ requires LUC variance). Inside CWQZ (Zone 2): 4:1 / 6:1 / 8:1 — all require LUC variance.
- **Note re ECM cross-reference:** ECM § 1.7.1 still references the repealed § 25-8-364; current governing provision is LDC § 25-8-263.

### Critical Water Quality Zone (CWQZ) — the buffer system

- **Suburban watersheds — fixed buffer widths from centerline:** 100 ft (minor, 64–320 ac); 200 ft (intermediate, 320–640 ac); 300 ft (major, >640 ac). Buffer averaging permitted per ECM 1.5.2.D.
- **CWQZ is largely undevelopable.** Most encroachments require an LUC variance under the enhanced § 25-8-41(B) standard (must prevent reasonable, economic use of the **entire** property).
- Ponds, fill, retaining walls, parking, buildings, and spray irrigation are prohibited in CWQZ outright in most cases. Trails permitted at ≥50 ft from CEF edge under § 25-8-281(C)(3) without variance.
- WQTZ is less restrictive but still constrains pond siting and stormwater controls.

### Erosion Hazard Zone (EHZ)

- EHZ analysis triggered when development is within 100 ft of a classified waterway centerline (≥64 acres drainage) or 200 ft of the Colorado River OHWM downstream of Longhorn Dam (LDC § 25-7-32(C)).
- Seven-step DCM Appendix E procedure: meander belt delineation (if sinuosity ≥1.2), bankfull geometry, incision depth, side slope projections to 100 ft max (steep terrain) or 20 ft min setback from tops of bank.
- WPD/ERM concurrence on protective works required.

### Critical Environmental Features (CEFs)

- 150-ft standard setback (LDC § 25-8-281). Reduction requires administrative variance under § 25-8-42(B)(5) only if all CEF characteristics can be preserved.
- Point recharge features (caves, sinkholes) — admin variance minimum 50 ft, with 12 ECM 1.10.4.B conditions precluding further reduction.
- Canyon rimrock / bluff admin variance unavailable on upslope grade ≥15% or average grade ≥10% — LUC variance required.
- Cave footprint assumption: 300 ft from entrance when subsurface extent unmapped (ECM 1.10.3.C).

### Cut / fill grading limits

- **4-ft standard limit** in non-urban watersheds (LDC §§ 25-8-341 / 25-8-342); urban watersheds exempt.
- **8-ft administrative variance maximum** in the Desired Development Zone (DDZ); ECM 1.3.3 form. Unavailable on slopes >15% or within 100 ft of a classified waterway, or anywhere in the Drinking Water Protection Zone (DWPZ — Barton Springs Zone, Barton Creek watershed, all water supply rural and suburban watersheds), except for public primary/secondary educational facilities.
- **>8 ft cut/fill** anywhere, or **any** cut/fill above 4 ft in DWPZ: LUC variance under § 25-8-41 required.
- **Cover sheet citation watch:** flag any reference to "§ 25-8-42(B)(6)" — that subsection was renumbered to (B)(7) by Ord. No. 20221027-045 (effective 2022-11-07).

### Watershed impervious cover limits

- **Urban IC:** set by zoning code (LDC § 25-2-492); gross site area; no Q-1/Q-2 tables.
- **Suburban IC:** 45–80% gross site area depending on use type and whether transfer of development intensity is used (LDC § 25-8-392).
- **Barton Springs Zone IC:** 15% over EARZ/recharge; 20% Barton Creek contributing zone; 25% remainder of BSZ contributing zone (net site area; LDC § 25-8-514). **No variance available — Save Our Springs (Article 13).**
- **Interbasin diversion threshold:** lesser of 20% of gross site area or 1 acre (LDC § 25-8-365). Above this, admin variance via § 25-8-42(B)(9) or LUC variance.

### Drainage easement

- Regulatory 100-yr floodplain must be **entirely contained** within a drainage easement on the plat. Easement dedication variances available at LDC § 25-7-152(E) for full-purpose city limits only.

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **Redevelopment Exception (LDC §§ 25-8-25 / -26 / -27).** Existing developed sites in Urban or Suburban watersheds may retain existing impervious cover that exceeds current limits. Substantive eligibility requires water quality treatment for the full 0.5" / 1.0" capture and other procedural conditions. Often decisive for infill projects.
- **CLOMR / LOMR.** Where the FEMA boundary is conservative relative to actual topography, a no-rise modification + LOMR can remove parts of the parcel from SFHA, unlocking buildable area. Budget 6–12 months for FEMA review and stage CLOMC acknowledgment before site plan permit.
- **Compensatory storage / fill in 100-yr (non-floodway).** Cut/fill to raise pad elevation can work in the 100-yr floodplain (outside the floodway) with proper no-rise + volume compensation + 2-ft freeboard. Not available in floodway.
- **Buffer averaging in CWQZ (ECM 1.5.2.D).** Suburban watersheds allow buffer width averaging so long as total area is preserved — can free up usable land while still meeting CWQZ obligations.
- **Atlas 14 watershed amendment status.** Watersheds not yet updated to Atlas 14 may still produce smaller COA boundaries than updated neighbors. Verify status; the boundary you map at concept may grow before site plan.
- **Conservation easements / parkland dedication.** Floodplain-encumbered area unsuitable for development can satisfy parkland dedication or conservation easement obligations, potentially yielding fee credits.
- **Public-facility cut/fill pathway.** Public primary/secondary educational facilities have a unique exemption to the DWPZ ban on cut/fill admin variances (AISD Interlocal Agreement § 10.2.4.1 / LDC § 25-2-835).
- **TIRZ / Waller Creek tunnel exception.** Sites discharging directly to Lady Bird Lake, Lake Travis, Lake Austin, the Colorado River, or Waller Creek below the tunnel inlet within the TIRZ are exempt from no-increased-peak-flow-rate requirements (DCM 1.2.2.F).
- **ECM 1.7.3 floodplain-modification exemptions** from restoration ratios: (A) public health/safety necessity (with WPD Director letter); (B) significant demonstrable environmental benefit; (C) conditionally-allowed CWQZ development. Useful when restoration ratios would otherwise make a project infeasible.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **environmental.md** — FEMA flood zone determination, FIRM panel number + effective date, COA fully-developed floodplain extent, CWQZ / WQTZ / EHZ overlay results, classified waterway proximity, EARZ status, Barton Springs Zone status, CEF inventory from ERI or GIS, watershed classification (Urban / Suburban / Water Supply Suburban / Water Supply Rural / Barton Springs Zone), Atlas 14 amendment status for the watershed.
- **property-records.md** — recorded drainage easements, plat conditions referencing flood/drainage, prior CLOMR/LOMR letters, prior environmental or floodplain variance approvals (check expiration under LDC § 25-1-217 — variances expire 1 year after effective date unless associated with an approved plan).
- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed grading depths, building footprint relative to mapped floodplain boundaries, proposed FFE, pond locations (water quality + detention), driveway/parking layout relative to CWQZ and EHZ, proposed disturbance area relative to CEF buffers.
- **adjacent-context.md** — upstream/downstream conditions for no-adverse-impact framing; nearby preliminary FIRMs in process.

## Output structure

Standard discipline output shape. See `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.

## Severity heuristics

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| Building footprint or parking within COA 25-yr floodplain (floodway) | `significant` — 0.00-ft rise required; Council variance unavailable if any rise results |
| Project in Barton Springs Zone exceeding 15% IC (or 20% / 25% per sub-zone) | `significant` — SOS Article 13, no variance available |
| Building footprint within FEMA SFHA + COA 100-yr, freeboard + compensatory storage achievable | `moderate` |
| Building or parking within FEMA SFHA but outside COA fully-developed boundary, freeboard achievable | `moderate` — § 25-7-93 exception pathway likely |
| COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain materially larger than FEMA SFHA, encroaches on developable area | `moderate` to `significant` depending on coverage |
| Site within 100 ft of classified waterway centerline, cut/fill needed >4 ft | `moderate` — administrative variance unavailable; LUC variance required |
| CWQZ encroachment proposed for parking, pond, or building | `significant` — enhanced § 25-8-41(B) standard (must prevent reasonable economic use of entire property) |
| EHZ overlaps proposed disturbance | `moderate` — analysis required; protective works concurrence with WPD/ERM |
| CEF setback reduction needed for non-wetland CEF | `moderate` — admin variance pathway via ECM 1.3.3 |
| Cut/fill 4–8 ft in DDZ, slopes <15%, >100 ft from classified waterway | `moderate` — admin variance available |
| Cut/fill >8 ft anywhere, or cut/fill in DWPZ | `significant` — LUC variance only; not available in BSZ for cut/fill on slopes >15% |
| Watershed has pending preliminary FIRM (effective FIRM in transition) | `moderate` — boundary may grow before site plan; design to preliminary |
| Floodplain study not yet performed for ≥64-acre waterway on or adjacent to site | `moderate` — Phase 3 cannot finalize FP boundary without it |
| Parcel entirely outside FEMA SFHA, COA 100-yr, CWQZ, EHZ, and CEF buffers | `note` |
| LOMA / LOMR pathway available for portion of parcel | `opportunity` |
| Redevelopment Exception eligibility for IC | `opportunity` |
| Buffer averaging in CWQZ unlocks developable area while preserving total buffer | `opportunity` |
| TIRZ / Waller Creek tunnel discharge exception applies | `opportunity` |

## Common pitfalls

- **Citing only FEMA SFHA.** The COA fully-developed floodplain is broader in Atlas 14 watersheds — design only to FEMA and you will land in COA-floodplain encroachment at site plan review.
- **Treating COA 25-yr as a "minor" boundary.** The COA 25-yr floodplain **is** the COA floodway. 0.00-ft rise is required; Council cannot grant variance if any rise results. It is the hardest line on the map.
- **Re-delineating FEMA boundary to onsite topo.** FEMA must be copied directly from the FIRM panel shapefile. Re-delineating is a deficiency signature.
- **COA boundary matching FEMA exactly.** Indicates the engineer used FEMA data rather than the City's regulatory hydraulic model — also a violation signature.
- **Stale code citations.** Cover sheet referencing "§ 25-8-42(B)(6)" for cut/fill admin variance (renumbered to (B)(7) in 2022); plans or variance letters citing repealed §§ 25-8-691 through 25-8-696 for notification requirements (repealed 2022-11-07); ECM § 1.7.1 cross-reference to repealed § 25-8-364 (now § 25-8-263).
- **Assuming compensatory storage anywhere.** Volume compensation works for fill in the 100-yr floodplain outside the floodway; it does **not** create a pathway through the floodway.
- **Conflating EHZ with CWQZ.** Different boundaries, different rules. The EHZ may extend beyond the CWQZ in steep terrain (up to 100-ft setback) or be contained within it.
- **Missing the 64-acre threshold.** Below 64 acres of contributing drainage area, no COA floodplain is required to be delineated — but if City or FEMA has already mapped one, it still applies.
- **Missing the Atlas 14 watershed status check.** Watersheds updated post-2019-11-25 require Atlas 14 rainfall (Rule R161-20.01); older models in non-updated watersheds will be rejected for new floodplain studies.
- **Assuming variance pathways exist in the Barton Springs Zone.** Save Our Springs (Article 13) cannot be varied — not by admin variance, not by LUC variance, not by Council.
- **Variance expiration.** Variances expire 1 year after effective date (LDC § 25-1-217) unless a plan/permit application was timely filed. Old approval letters on a parcel may already be void.
- **Drainage easement scope.** The regulatory 100-yr floodplain must be **entirely contained** within a drainage easement on the plat — a partial easement is a deficiency.
- **CLOMC timing.** FEMA CLOMC acknowledgment letter must be in the project file **before** preliminary plan or site plan permit issues — not after. Budget 6–12 months.
- **PE no-rise certification format.** Floodway no-rise must be a **separate** PE-sealed letter (LDC § 25-12-54(D)(11)), not implied by the WSE comparison table.
- **ASCE 24-14 letters.** One per structure type in the floodplain — bridges, culverts, retaining walls, structural fill, piers, fencing, buildings. A single combined letter is a common deficiency.

1→# Subdivision & Development Engineering Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Drainage analysis, stormwater detention and water quality controls, grading, retaining walls, easements, storm drain design, subdivision platting, standard details, and construction inspection for City of Austin and Austin ETJ projects. Bridges with `wwp` (water/wastewater), `fwp` (floodplain & creek buffers), `ta` (transportation/ROW), and `el` (environmental — CEFs, EARZ, watershed classification).
     6→
     7→SDE is the largest discipline by code volume; expect to coordinate findings across most of the other disciplines.
     8→
     9→## Authoritative sources
    10→
    11→- **Drainage Criteria Manual (DCM)** — Watershed Protection Department; governs drainage design, easements, ponds, RSMP
    12→- **Environmental Criteria Manual (ECM)** — water quality controls (SCMs/GSI), grading, IWM, CEFs, EARZ liners
    13→- **Land Development Code (LDC) Title 25** — chapters 25-7 (drainage), 25-8 (environmental/water quality), 25-4/30-2 (subdivision)
    14→- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM) §13.2** — retaining wall structural and ROW requirements
    15→- **Utilities Criteria Manual (UCM) §2.5** — construction plan content, PE seal, sheet standards
    16→- **City of Austin Standard Specifications & Standard Drawings (SSM/Std Specs)** — 508S outlet structures, 661 series WQ details, 594S gabions, 414S waterstops, 623S dry-stack rock, 658S void mitigation
    17→- **RSMP Participation Handbook (FY24, effective July 15, 2024)** — Regional Stormwater Management Program
    18→- **General Site Plan Notes for COA** and **Environmental Review Requirements** — cover sheet and plan note templates
    19→
    20→Atlas 14 rainfall is mandatory for submittals on/after Nov 25, 2019 (DCM 2.3.0). Approved drainage modeling software: HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, PondPack, StormCAD, CivilStorm (DCM 1.2.5).
    21→
    22→## Regulatory pathway
    23→
    24→| Action | Path | Typical timeline |
    25→|---|---|---|
    26→| Concept/feasibility review | Optional Pre-Development Consultation; RSMP Feasibility Meeting if pursuing RSMP | 4–8 weeks |
    27→| Subdivision | Preliminary Plan → Subdivision Construction Plans → Final Plat | 6–18 months |
    28→| Site Plan (commercial / multifamily) | SDP application → Completeness Check → Update Cycles → Approval | 9–18 months in current cycle times |
    29→| RSMP participation | Feasibility Meeting **before** Completeness Check → Application Package → Approval Letter → Agreement → Payment | 3–6 months to Approval Letter; payment before permit issuance |
    30→| Construction permit | Site Development Permit issued after plan approval; pre-construction conference required (LDC § 25-1-282) | 2–6 weeks post-approval |
    31→| Inspection / acceptance | DSD/WPD inspection through construction; engineer certifications before CO; SCM acceptance for SF/duplex (City takes maintenance); restrictive covenant for commercial/MF (owner maintains) | continuous |
    32→
    33→Key sequencing trap: **RSMP feasibility meeting must occur before formal Completeness Check.** If RSMP is in play, schedule that meeting at the start of design.
    34→
    35→## Constraints to evaluate
    36→
    37→### Drainage performance standard (DCM 1.2.2.D)
    38→
    39→- **No-increase rule** at every point of discharge for the 2-, 10-, 25-, and 100-year storms. Existing and proposed conditions modeled separately.
    40→- **Exception:** direct discharge into Lady Bird Lake, Lake Austin, Lake Travis, the Colorado River, or qualifying Waller Creek TIRZ properties (DCM 1.2.2.F).
    41→- **Atlas 14 rainfall** for all submittals after Nov 25, 2019. Pre-Atlas 14 phased developments may use DCM 1.2.2.H hybrid criteria.
    42→- Off-site contributing areas modeled at **existing IC** for pond performance (DCM 8.3.2.A) but **fully developed** for spillway/embankment design (DCM 8.3.3.A). Both apply to the same pond.
    43→
    44→### Water quality controls (LDC § 25-8-211; ECM 1.6)
    45→
    46→- **Trigger:** any new + redeveloped IC > 8,000 SF outside BSZ; **all** development in the Barton Springs Zone (no threshold).
    47→- **Green Stormwater Infrastructure (GSI) mandatory** since Nov 7, 2022 (LDC § 25-8-213(C)). Conventional sed/filtration ponds and wet ponds require a documented exemption: highly contaminated runoff land use, off-site treatment ≥ 10 acres of currently untreated developed area, or site IC > 90% gross area (LDC § 25-8-213(D)).
    48→- **WQV formula** (ECM 1.6.2.A): WQV = (0.5 in + 0.1 in per 10% IC over 20%) × DA (ac) × 3,630. Drawdown within 48 hours. Applies to all IC on site, not just new IC.
    49→- **EARZ controls (LDC § 25-8-213(A)(2); ECM 1.6.2.C):** impermeable liner required — geomembrane (≥ 30 mils, UV resistant) or concrete (basins < 1,000 SF). Clay liners (Std Detail 661-2) **prohibited** over EARZ regardless of permeability testing. Vegetative filter strips are the only exemption.
    50→- **Rain garden cap:** 2 acres contributing drainage area (ECM 1.6.7.H). Larger = biofiltration basin (ECM 1.6.7.C). Recommended max 50 acres per WQ control (ECM 1.6.2.A).
    51→- **Wet pond minimum permanent pool:** > 0.5 ac (21,780 SF) (ECM 1.6.6.A.1).
    52→- **IWM (Innovative Water Management):** commercial sites with required landscape area must irrigate ≥ 50% with stormwater or leave undisturbed (LDC § 25-2-1008; ECM 2.4.9). 1:2 minimum drainage-to-landscape ratio.
    53→
    54→### Stormwater detention
    55→
    56→- **2-year on-site control required regardless of RSMP** (LDC § 25-7-61(A)(5)(c); ECM 1.6.8).
    57→- **Detention drawdown:** max 24 hr for flood detention (DCM 8.3.2.C).
    58→- **Regional pond threshold:** > 64 ac contributing drainage area triggers WPD project-by-project review and geotechnical-based slope design (DCM 8.3.2.B; DCM 8.3.3.F).
    59→- **Dam classification:** SWM pond embankment ≥ 6 ft at any point along the perimeter → dam (DCM 8.3.3.B.1). Triggers PMF design, 20-ft clear zone (no trees/woody vegetation upstream and downstream of toe), and TCEQ jurisdiction concerns.
    60→- **Storm drain connection** required when within 300 ft of an existing storm drain system (DCM 1.2.3.C, as amended 9-8-2025). RSMP does **not** waive this.
    61→
    62→### Grading and slopes
    63→
    64→- General cut/fill side slopes: max 3H:1V (DCM 8.3.3.F; DCM 6.4.1.D). Rock slopes steeper than 3:1 require geotechnical stability report.
    65→- Wet pond earthen slopes max 3:1 (ECM 1.6.6.C.6); vegetated bench between 3:1 and 4:1 (or 4:1–5:1 for ponds ≥ 2 ac, ECM Table 1-9B).
    66→- WQ facility maintenance drives: ≤ 15% longitudinal, ≤ 5% transverse (DCM 1.2.4.E.1.e).
    67→- Temporary ESC slopes 2:1 or flatter (ECM 1.4.5). Final slopes > 15% require erosion control matting at toe and top.
    68→- Elevations must be NAVD88 (or equivalent absolute datum), not site-relative. BCM 4.4.3.1 requires a permanent benchmark on the plot plan.
    69→
    70→### Retaining walls (TCM § 13.2)
    71→
    72→- **< 2 ft (minor structure):** no PE, no geotech, no separate building permit. Construction waiver available unless wall supports roadway embankment.
    73→- **≥ 2 ft:** licensed PE design + geotechnical investigation required.
    74→- **≥ 4 ft:** structural plan submittal + calculations before site plan approval + separate **building permit** (IBC). Cover sheet note required.
    75→- **> 10 ft and supporting roadway embankment:** 20-ft truck-accessible maintenance zone at base (TCM 13.2.9).
    76→- **In/adjacent to ROW:** D1 ≤ H1 rule triggers full §13.2 review. 5-ft minimum face-to-back-of-curb. External components (geogrid, soldier piles) need ≥ 36 in cover. Private walls **not allowed in ROW** without encroachment agreement (City Council approval).
    77→- **Drainage easement walls:** not categorically prohibited — Director approval + license/encroachment agreement + utility encasement.
    78→- **Inside SCMs:** dry-stacked rock prohibited (ECM 1.6.3.B.7). Grouted rock walls inside SCMs require impermeable barrier. Waterstops required at expansion joints (ECM 1.6.3.B.6; Std Spec 414S.4.E).
    79→- **Safety rails:** not a universal "> 4 ft" trigger. Triggered when wall supports roadway embankment adjacent to sidewalk/roadway, OR when wall is adjacent to park/playground/SF/MF residential with backslope toward wall (TCM 13.2.10).
    80→
    81→### Easements (LDC § 25-7-151, -152; DCM 1.2.4)
    82→
    83→- Open drainage easement: min 25 ft (DCM 1.2.4.G.1).
    84→- Enclosed system: per pipe-diameter/invert-depth table — min 20 ft for shallowest/smallest pipes; up to 40 ft for large-diameter deep inverts. **No 15-ft minimum in current DCM.** Half-width allowed outside ROW when parallel to ROW (Note 2).
    85→- Easement extends to the **larger of** the COA fully-developed 100-yr WSE or DCM minimum widths (DCM 1.2.4.F). COA floodplain typically broader than FEMA.
    86→- COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain delineation required when contributing DA ≥ 64 ac (DCM 1.2.6.A.1).
    87→- **Document types** (City administrative practice): Public Drainage Easement; Drainage Easement w/ Required Maintenance (private maintenance); Drainage Easement w/ Required Maintenance and Permitted Obstructions (combined flows or authorized structures).
    88→- **Water Quality Easement** required for irrigation/infiltration fields of retention/irrigation SCMs (ECM 1.6.7.A.4.c) — distinct from drainage easement.
    89→- **Shared infrastructure** (DCM 1.2.4.E.3): Restrictive Covenant, UDA, or Drainage Easement w/ Required Maintenance when serving multiple lots. UDA must be City Legal–approved and recorded before site plan approval.
    90→- **Dam clear zone:** 20-ft tree-free zone within dedicated easement for dam-classified ponds (DCM 8.3.3.B.5).
    91→- Buildings and parking **may not encroach** on the 25- or 100-yr floodplain (LDC § 25-7-92).
    92→
    93→### RSMP — Regional Stormwater Management Program (DCM 8.2)
    94→
    95→- Alternative to **on-site detention only.** Does not waive: 2-yr on-site control, storm drain connection, WQ SCMs, existing storm drain condition verification (DCM 5.3.6), or any other code.
    96→- **Three pathways:**
    97→  - **DCM 1.2.2.G (Simplified):** commercial/MF/mixed-use ≤ 0.5 ac, **or** SF subdivision ≤ 1 ac (no preliminary plan). All four criteria all-or-nothing.
    98→  - **DCM 8.2.2 (General):** larger sites in participating watersheds within COA full-purpose. Requires three-scenario HEC-HMS model (existing; proposed w/ conceptual pond; proposed w/o detention), downstream capacity demonstration for fully developed 100-yr, drainage easement for unconditional 100-yr conveyance.
    99→  - **Prior RSMP Participation:** redevelopment under existing executed RSMP Agreement bound to the land; case-by-case O-Type Approval Letter.
   100→- **Order of preference** (DCM 8.2.2.B): (1) improvement of downstream system/SCMs, (2) off-site detention, (3) easement dedication/land donation, (4) payment in lieu. Payment selection must be justified or RSMP Team must accept the departure.
   101→- **Categorically unavailable:** subdivisions in the Travis County ETJ. For non-subdivision ETJ projects, a Travis County Detention Waiver is required first.
   102→- **Watershed eligibility** confirmed via RSMP Feasibility Viewer or Austin Watersheds List — not determinable from plan sheets alone.
   103→- **Payment rate** updated annually on October 1 (ENR-CCI indexed). Current calculation at austintexas.gov/RSMP.
   104→- **SMART Housing discount:** 10–50% RSMP payment discount for 10–50% SMART Housing units maintained ≥ 40 yr (requires SMART Housing Certification Letter).
   105→- Special coordination: **PARD** acceptance if discharging onto/through parkland (Chapter 26 process if charter-protected); **TxDOT District Engineer** letter if discharging onto/across TxDOT ROW or connecting to TxDOT storm drains; **downstream jurisdiction** approval if watershed drains out of Austin's jurisdiction.
   106→
   107→### Interbasin diversion (LDC § 25-8-365)
   108→
   109→- Minor diversion threshold: < 20% of gross site area **AND** < 1 ac (both must be met).
   110→- ≥ 20% **or** ≥ 1 ac → Administrative Environmental Variance required (LDC § 25-8-42(B)(9)).
   111→- Pre-development watershed regs apply pre-diversion; only WQ treatment follows post-development receiving watershed (ECM 1.2.3).
   112→
   113→### Erosion Hazard Zone (DCM Appendix E)
   114→
   115→- EHZ analysis required when within 100 ft of a waterway centerline with DA ≥ 64 ac, or within 100–200 ft OHWM of the Colorado River below Longhorn Dam, or where significant erosion is present (LDC § 25-7-32(C)).
   116→- **Exception:** site separated from triggering waterway by a public roadway (LDC § 25-7-32(B)).
   117→- Level 1 analysis projects 4H:1V slopes from future toe of bank (incision = existing depth × 3), min 20 ft setback from top of bank, max 100 ft in steep terrain.
   118→
   119→### EARZ / Void Mitigation (ECM 1.12)
   120→
   121→- EARZ sites require verbatim cover sheet note (ECM 1.12.3(A)(2)): trenching > 5 ft must be inspected by a Texas P.G. or representative.
   122→- Trenching/excavation in EARZ engages the Void and Water Flow Mitigation Rule and Std Spec 658S.
   123→
   124→### Plan set & standard details
   125→
   126→- SDP sheet size 24"×36" (DSD); AWU plans 22"×34" minimum (UCM 2.5.1.E.3).
   127→- PE seal required (preliminary seals not accepted; UCM 2.5.1.E.1).
   128→- Q1/Q2 IC tables (ECM App. Q) required in Suburban, Water Supply Rural/Suburban, and BSZ watersheds; **not** required in Urban watersheds (LDC § 25-8-62(F)).
   129→- Required standard details: 508S outlet structures, 661-1 (sed/filtration sand bed), 661-2 (wet pond clay liner — **prohibited over EARZ**), 661-3 (biofiltration), 662S-2 (pond maintenance road), DCM App. D Figs. 4-1 through 4-7 (inlets), 594S (gabion gradation), 414S (waterstops), 623S (dry-stack rock).
   130→
   131→### Construction / inspection
   132→
   133→- Pre-construction conference required (LDC § 25-1-282; waivable by Director).
   134→- Engineer of record certification before CO (General Site Plan Notes Construction Note 6).
   135→- **Pond perimeter signage** required only for residential or City-maintained SCMs; **exempt** if combined SCM storage ≤ 5,000 CF **AND** max ponding depth ≤ 3 ft (DCM 1.2.4.E.10).
   136→- BSZ commercial/MF water quality facilities require an **annual operating permit** (LDC § 25-8-233).
   137→- Subsurface commercial SCMs require **SPMP + annual PE inspection report** to WPD (LDC § 25-7-153(F); ECM 1.6.2.E).
   138→
   139→## Opportunities to evaluate
   140→
   141→- **RSMP payment in lieu of on-site detention** (DCM 8.2.2). Frees up developable area; current rate is on RSMP payment calculator. Eligibility depends on watershed (Feasibility Viewer) and order-of-preference justification. SMART Housing affordability stack yields 10–50% RSMP discount.
   142→- **DCM 1.2.2.G Simplified RSMP** for small sites (≤ 0.5 ac commercial/MF/mixed-use, or ≤ 1 ac SF subdivision) — skips three-scenario modeling.

# Subdivision & Development Engineering Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Drainage analysis, stormwater detention and water quality controls, grading, retaining walls, easements, storm drain design, subdivision platting, standard details, and construction inspection for City of Austin and Austin ETJ projects. Bridges with `wwp` (water/wastewater), `fwp` (floodplain & creek buffers), `ta` (transportation/ROW), and `el` (environmental — CEFs, EARZ, watershed classification).

SDE is the largest discipline by code volume; expect to coordinate findings across most of the other disciplines.

## Authoritative sources

- **Drainage Criteria Manual (DCM)** — Watershed Protection Department; governs drainage design, easements, ponds, RSMP
- **Environmental Criteria Manual (ECM)** — water quality controls (SCMs/GSI), grading, IWM, CEFs, EARZ liners
- **Land Development Code (LDC) Title 25** — chapters 25-7 (drainage), 25-8 (environmental/water quality), 25-4/30-2 (subdivision)
- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM) §13.2** — retaining wall structural and ROW requirements
- **Utilities Criteria Manual (UCM) §2.5** — construction plan content, PE seal, sheet standards
- **City of Austin Standard Specifications & Standard Drawings (SSM/Std Specs)** — 508S outlet structures, 661 series WQ details, 594S gabions, 414S waterstops, 623S dry-stack rock, 658S void mitigation
- **RSMP Participation Handbook (FY24, effective July 15, 2024)** — Regional Stormwater Management Program
- **General Site Plan Notes for COA** and **Environmental Review Requirements** — cover sheet and plan note templates

Atlas 14 rainfall is mandatory for submittals on/after Nov 25, 2019 (DCM 2.3.0). Approved drainage modeling software: HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, PondPack, StormCAD, CivilStorm (DCM 1.2.5).

## Regulatory pathway

| Action | Path | Typical timeline |
|---|---|---|
| Concept/feasibility review | Optional Pre-Development Consultation; RSMP Feasibility Meeting if pursuing RSMP | 4–8 weeks |
| Subdivision | Preliminary Plan → Subdivision Construction Plans → Final Plat | 6–18 months |
| Site Plan (commercial / multifamily) | SDP application → Completeness Check → Update Cycles → Approval | 9–18 months in current cycle times |
| RSMP participation | Feasibility Meeting **before** Completeness Check → Application Package → Approval Letter → Agreement → Payment | 3–6 months to Approval Letter; payment before permit issuance |
| Construction permit | Site Development Permit issued after plan approval; pre-construction conference required (LDC § 25-1-282) | 2–6 weeks post-approval |
| Inspection / acceptance | DSD/WPD inspection through construction; engineer certifications before CO; SCM acceptance for SF/duplex (City takes maintenance); restrictive covenant for commercial/MF (owner maintains) | continuous |

Key sequencing trap: **RSMP feasibility meeting must occur before formal Completeness Check.** If RSMP is in play, schedule that meeting at the start of design.

## Constraints to evaluate

### Drainage performance standard (DCM 1.2.2.D)

- **No-increase rule** at every point of discharge for the 2-, 10-, 25-, and 100-year storms. Existing and proposed conditions modeled separately.
- **Exception:** direct discharge into Lady Bird Lake, Lake Austin, Lake Travis, the Colorado River, or qualifying Waller Creek TIRZ properties (DCM 1.2.2.F).
- **Atlas 14 rainfall** for all submittals after Nov 25, 2019. Pre-Atlas 14 phased developments may use DCM 1.2.2.H hybrid criteria.
- Off-site contributing areas modeled at **existing IC** for pond performance (DCM 8.3.2.A) but **fully developed** for spillway/embankment design (DCM 8.3.3.A). Both apply to the same pond.

### Water quality controls (LDC § 25-8-211; ECM 1.6)

- **Trigger:** any new + redeveloped IC > 8,000 SF outside BSZ; **all** development in the Barton Springs Zone (no threshold).
- **Green Stormwater Infrastructure (GSI) mandatory** since Nov 7, 2022 (LDC § 25-8-213(C)). Conventional sed/filtration ponds and wet ponds require a documented exemption: highly contaminated runoff land use, off-site treatment ≥ 10 acres of currently untreated developed area, or site IC > 90% gross area (LDC § 25-8-213(D)).
- **WQV formula** (ECM 1.6.2.A): WQV = (0.5 in + 0.1 in per 10% IC over 20%) × DA (ac) × 3,630. Drawdown within 48 hours. Applies to all IC on site, not just new IC.
- **EARZ controls (LDC § 25-8-213(A)(2); ECM 1.6.2.C):** impermeable liner required — geomembrane (≥ 30 mils, UV resistant) or concrete (basins < 1,000 SF). Clay liners (Std Detail 661-2) **prohibited** over EARZ regardless of permeability testing. Vegetative filter strips are the only exemption.
- **Rain garden cap:** 2 acres contributing drainage area (ECM 1.6.7.H). Larger = biofiltration basin (ECM 1.6.7.C). Recommended max 50 acres per WQ control (ECM 1.6.2.A).
- **Wet pond minimum permanent pool:** > 0.5 ac (21,780 SF) (ECM 1.6.6.A.1).
- **IWM (Innovative Water Management):** commercial sites with required landscape area must irrigate ≥ 50% with stormwater or leave undisturbed (LDC § 25-2-1008; ECM 2.4.9). 1:2 minimum drainage-to-landscape ratio.

### Stormwater detention

- **2-year on-site control required regardless of RSMP** (LDC § 25-7-61(A)(5)(c); ECM 1.6.8).
- **Detention drawdown:** max 24 hr for flood detention (DCM 8.3.2.C).
- **Regional pond threshold:** > 64 ac contributing drainage area triggers WPD project-by-project review and geotechnical-based slope design (DCM 8.3.2.B; DCM 8.3.3.F).
- **Dam classification:** SWM pond embankment ≥ 6 ft at any point along the perimeter → dam (DCM 8.3.3.B.1). Triggers PMF design, 20-ft clear zone (no trees/woody vegetation upstream and downstream of toe), and TCEQ jurisdiction concerns.
- **Storm drain connection** required when within 300 ft of an existing storm drain system (DCM 1.2.3.C, as amended 9-8-2025). RSMP does **not** waive this.

### Grading and slopes

- General cut/fill side slopes: max 3H:1V (DCM 8.3.3.F; DCM 6.4.1.D). Rock slopes steeper than 3:1 require geotechnical stability report.
- Wet pond earthen slopes max 3:1 (ECM 1.6.6.C.6); vegetated bench between 3:1 and 4:1 (or 4:1–5:1 for ponds ≥ 2 ac, ECM Table 1-9B).
- WQ facility maintenance drives: ≤ 15% longitudinal, ≤ 5% transverse (DCM 1.2.4.E.1.e).
- Temporary ESC slopes 2:1 or flatter (ECM 1.4.5). Final slopes > 15% require erosion control matting at toe and top.
- Elevations must be NAVD88 (or equivalent absolute datum), not site-relative. BCM 4.4.3.1 requires a permanent benchmark on the plot plan.

### Retaining walls (TCM § 13.2)

- **< 2 ft (minor structure):** no PE, no geotech, no separate building permit. Construction waiver available unless wall supports roadway embankment.
- **≥ 2 ft:** licensed PE design + geotechnical investigation required.
- **≥ 4 ft:** structural plan submittal + calculations before site plan approval + separate **building permit** (IBC). Cover sheet note required.
- **> 10 ft and supporting roadway embankment:** 20-ft truck-accessible maintenance zone at base (TCM 13.2.9).
- **In/adjacent to ROW:** D1 ≤ H1 rule triggers full §13.2 review. 5-ft minimum face-to-back-of-curb. External components (geogrid, soldier piles) need ≥ 36 in cover. Private walls **not allowed in ROW** without encroachment agreement (City Council approval).
- **Drainage easement walls:** not categorically prohibited — Director approval + license/encroachment agreement + utility encasement.
- **Inside SCMs:** dry-stacked rock prohibited (ECM 1.6.3.B.7). Grouted rock walls inside SCMs require impermeable barrier. Waterstops required at expansion joints (ECM 1.6.3.B.6; Std Spec 414S.4.E).
- **Safety rails:** not a universal "> 4 ft" trigger. Triggered when wall supports roadway embankment adjacent to sidewalk/roadway, OR when wall is adjacent to park/playground/SF/MF residential with backslope toward wall (TCM 13.2.10).

### Easements (LDC § 25-7-151, -152; DCM 1.2.4)

- Open drainage easement: min 25 ft (DCM 1.2.4.G.1).
- Enclosed system: per pipe-diameter/invert-depth table — min 20 ft for shallowest/smallest pipes; up to 40 ft for large-diameter deep inverts. **No 15-ft minimum in current DCM.** Half-width allowed outside ROW when parallel to ROW (Note 2).
- Easement extends to the **larger of** the COA fully-developed 100-yr WSE or DCM minimum widths (DCM 1.2.4.F). COA floodplain typically broader than FEMA.
- COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain delineation required when contributing DA ≥ 64 ac (DCM 1.2.6.A.1).
- **Document types** (City administrative practice): Public Drainage Easement; Drainage Easement w/ Required Maintenance (private maintenance); Drainage Easement w/ Required Maintenance and Permitted Obstructions (combined flows or authorized structures).
- **Water Quality Easement** required for irrigation/infiltration fields of retention/irrigation SCMs (ECM 1.6.7.A.4.c) — distinct from drainage easement.
- **Shared infrastructure** (DCM 1.2.4.E.3): Restrictive Covenant, UDA, or Drainage Easement w/ Required Maintenance when serving multiple lots. UDA must be City Legal–approved and recorded before site plan approval.
- **Dam clear zone:** 20-ft tree-free zone within dedicated easement for dam-classified ponds (DCM 8.3.3.B.5).
- Buildings and parking **may not encroach** on the 25- or 100-yr floodplain (LDC § 25-7-92).

### RSMP — Regional Stormwater Management Program (DCM 8.2)

- Alternative to **on-site detention only.** Does not waive: 2-yr on-site control, storm drain connection, WQ SCMs, existing storm drain condition verification (DCM 5.3.6), or any other code.
- **Three pathways:**
  - **DCM 1.2.2.G (Simplified):** commercial/MF/mixed-use ≤ 0.5 ac, **or** SF subdivision ≤ 1 ac (no preliminary plan). All four criteria all-or-nothing.
  - **DCM 8.2.2 (General):** larger sites in participating watersheds within COA full-purpose. Requires three-scenario HEC-HMS model (existing; proposed w/ conceptual pond; proposed w/o detention), downstream capacity demonstration for fully developed 100-yr, drainage easement for unconditional 100-yr conveyance.
  - **Prior RSMP Participation:** redevelopment under existing executed RSMP Agreement bound to the land; case-by-case O-Type Approval Letter.
- **Order of preference** (DCM 8.2.2.B): (1) improvement of downstream system/SCMs, (2) off-site detention, (3) easement dedication/land donation, (4) payment in lieu. Payment selection must be justified or RSMP Team must accept the departure.
- **Categorically unavailable:** subdivisions in the Travis County ETJ. For non-subdivision ETJ projects, a Travis County Detention Waiver is required first.
- **Watershed eligibility** confirmed via RSMP Feasibility Viewer or Austin Watersheds List — not determinable from plan sheets alone.
- **Payment rate** updated annually on October 1 (ENR-CCI indexed). Current calculation at austintexas.gov/RSMP.
- **SMART Housing discount:** 10–50% RSMP payment discount for 10–50% SMART Housing units maintained ≥ 40 yr (requires SMART Housing Certification Letter).
- Special coordination: **PARD** acceptance if discharging onto/through parkland (Chapter 26 process if charter-protected); **TxDOT District Engineer** letter if discharging onto/across TxDOT ROW or connecting to TxDOT storm drains; **downstream jurisdiction** approval if watershed drains out of Austin's jurisdiction.

### Interbasin diversion (LDC § 25-8-365)

- Minor diversion threshold: < 20% of gross site area **AND** < 1 ac (both must be met).
- ≥ 20% **or** ≥ 1 ac → Administrative Environmental Variance required (LDC § 25-8-42(B)(9)).
- Pre-development watershed regs apply pre-diversion; only WQ treatment follows post-development receiving watershed (ECM 1.2.3).

### Erosion Hazard Zone (DCM Appendix E)

- EHZ analysis required when within 100 ft of a waterway centerline with DA ≥ 64 ac, or within 100–200 ft OHWM of the Colorado River below Longhorn Dam, or where significant erosion is present (LDC § 25-7-32(C)).
- **Exception:** site separated from triggering waterway by a public roadway (LDC § 25-7-32(B)).
- Level 1 analysis projects 4H:1V slopes from future toe of bank (incision = existing depth × 3), min 20 ft setback from top of bank, max 100 ft in steep terrain.

### EARZ / Void Mitigation (ECM 1.12)

- EARZ sites require verbatim cover sheet note (ECM 1.12.3(A)(2)): trenching > 5 ft must be inspected by a Texas P.G. or representative.
- Trenching/excavation in EARZ engages the Void and Water Flow Mitigation Rule and Std Spec 658S.

### Plan set & standard details

- SDP sheet size 24"×36" (DSD); AWU plans 22"×34" minimum (UCM 2.5.1.E.3).
- PE seal required (preliminary seals not accepted; UCM 2.5.1.E.1).
- Q1/Q2 IC tables (ECM App. Q) required in Suburban, Water Supply Rural/Suburban, and BSZ watersheds; **not** required in Urban watersheds (LDC § 25-8-62(F)).
- Required standard details: 508S outlet structures, 661-1 (sed/filtration sand bed), 661-2 (wet pond clay liner — **prohibited over EARZ**), 661-3 (biofiltration), 662S-2 (pond maintenance road), DCM App. D Figs. 4-1 through 4-7 (inlets), 594S (gabion gradation), 414S (waterstops), 623S (dry-stack rock).

### Construction / inspection

- Pre-construction conference required (LDC § 25-1-282; waivable by Director).
- Engineer of record certification before CO (General Site Plan Notes Construction Note 6).
- **Pond perimeter signage** required only for residential or City-maintained SCMs; **exempt** if combined SCM storage ≤ 5,000 CF **AND** max ponding depth ≤ 3 ft (DCM 1.2.4.E.10).
- BSZ commercial/MF water quality facilities require an **annual operating permit** (LDC § 25-8-233).
- Subsurface commercial SCMs require **SPMP + annual PE inspection report** to WPD (LDC § 25-7-153(F); ECM 1.6.2.E).

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **RSMP payment in lieu of on-site detention** (DCM 8.2.2). Frees up developable area; current rate is on RSMP payment calculator. Eligibility depends on watershed (Feasibility Viewer) and order-of-preference justification. SMART Housing affordability stack yields 10–50% RSMP discount.
- **DCM 1.2.2.G Simplified RSMP** for small sites (≤ 0.5 ac commercial/MF/mixed-use, or ≤ 1 ac SF subdivision) — skips three-scenario modeling.
- **Fee-in-lieu of water quality controls** (LDC § 25-8-214(C); ECM 1.6.4; App. T) — **Urban Watersheds only**, with prior WPD Director approval. Unavailable in BSZ, Water Supply Suburban, and Water Supply Rural watersheds.
- **Redevelopment Exception** to GSI / impervious cover increases:
  - Urban/Suburban Redevelopment Exception (LDC § 25-8-25): no IC increase; unpermitted post-1992 development may be cured by removal.
  - BSZ Redevelopment Exception (LDC § 25-8-26): commercial only; no pathway to cure unpermitted post-1992 development.
- **Vested rights exemption from GSI/WQ** for development predating May 18, 1986 or previously permitted with WQ controls (ECM 1.9.2.A).
- **Direct discharge to receiving water bodies** (Lady Bird, Austin, Travis, Colorado River, Waller TIRZ): no-increase standard does not apply (DCM 1.2.2.F).
- **Shared SCMs / off-site treatment** — joint maintenance covenants (LDC § 25-7-153(C)) and UDAs let multiple lots share a single pond, reducing per-site footprint.
- **Innovative stormwater practices** approved by the Director under LDC § 25-8-151 — non-standard SCMs with technical justification.
- **Standard wall / SCM details from City Std Drawings** — using the published catalog (508S series, 661 series) avoids review back-and-forth on custom designs.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **`environmental.md`** — watershed classification (Urban / Suburban / BSZ / Water Supply Rural / Water Supply Suburban), EARZ status (in/out, NEARZ vs SEARZ), CEFs within 500 ft, water quality transition zone, IC limits by watershed, slope categories
- **`floodplain.md` / `fwp` output** — FEMA + COA fully-developed 100-yr extents, regulatory floodplain, BFE, EHZ triggers, creek buffer
- **`transportation.md`** — adjacent ROW geometry, ASMP classification, TxDOT vs city street, sidewalk widths, drive approach standards
- **`wwp.md`** — adjacent utility easements (water/WW), required AW easement widths, conflicts with proposed grading
- **`property-records.md`** — recorded easements (drainage, access, utility), restrictive covenants, prior RSMP Agreement, UDAs, plat notes
- **`phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md`** — proposed IC, building footprint, parking, pond/SCM locations, grading extents, retaining wall heights and locations
- **`programs/rsmp.md`** — eligibility flag and pathway determination
- **`programs/smart-housing.md`** — if RSMP discount is being claimed

## Output structure

Standard discipline output shape per `references/phase3-disciplines.md`. Findings list with severity, evidence, citation, and recommended action. Group by sub-topic where many findings overlap (drainage analysis, WQ controls, easements, walls, RSMP).

## Severity heuristics

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| No viable drainage outfall — no downstream system within 300 ft and ROW cannot contain 100-yr fully developed flows | `significant` |
| Site in COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain extending across proposed building/parking with no easement adjustment path | `significant` |
| Dam-classified pond (≥ 6 ft embankment) required by site constraints without adequate clear zone | `significant` |
| RSMP needed but project is a subdivision in Travis County ETJ (categorically ineligible) | `significant` |
| EARZ site relying on clay liner (prohibited) — must redesign for geomembrane/concrete | `significant` if cost-prohibitive; otherwise `moderate` |
| WQ control footprint + detention exceeds available pad area after setbacks/easements | `significant` |
| Retaining wall > 10 ft supporting embankment without 20-ft maintenance zone | `moderate` |
| Retaining wall ≥ 4 ft not flagged for separate building permit | `moderate` |
| Wall proposed in drainage easement without Director approval pathway noted | `moderate` |
| Interbasin diversion at/above threshold — variance required | `moderate` (timeline + Council exposure) |
| Off-site SCM/shared pond proposed without joint maintenance covenant or UDA | `moderate` |
| Subsurface commercial SCM proposed without SPMP + annual PE inspection commitment | `moderate` |
| RSMP available and reduces on-site pond footprint | `opportunity` |
| Fee-in-lieu of WQ available (Urban watershed) | `opportunity` |
| SMART Housing stack yields RSMP payment discount | `opportunity` |
| Urban/Suburban Redevelopment Exception preserves IC | `opportunity` |
| Site discharges directly to Lady Bird/Lake Austin/Travis/Colorado River — no-increase rule waived | `opportunity` |
| Standard configuration with adequate easements and downstream capacity | `note` |
| Atlas 14 + COA fully-developed model needed but data available | `note` |

## Common pitfalls

- **Assuming RSMP waives the 2-year on-site storm control.** It doesn't (LDC § 25-7-61(A)(5)(c); ECM 1.6.8). Always require a separate 2-yr analysis.
- **Assuming RSMP waives the 300-ft storm drain connection requirement** (DCM 1.2.3.C). Three narrow exceptions only.
- **Citing the FEMA floodplain when COA fully-developed governs.** COA is typically broader; the drainage easement must extend to the COA WSE per DCM 1.2.4.F.
- **Using clay liner over the EARZ.** Prohibited regardless of permeability (ECM 1.6.2.C). Don't list Std Detail 661-2 on EARZ plan sets.
- **Treating "15 ft easement" as a minimum for enclosed pipes.** Not in current DCM 1.2.4.G — minimum is 20 ft.
- **Same offsite IC assumption used in pond performance and spillway calcs.** Performance = existing IC; spillway = fully developed (DCM 8.3.2.A vs 8.3.3.A).
- **Rain garden serving > 2 ac contributing area.** Must be designed as biofiltration basin (ECM 1.6.7.C/H) regardless of label.
- **Counting only new IC in WQV.** WQV applies to 100% of IC, new + redeveloped (ECM 1.6.2.A).
- **Trying to use RSMP for a Travis County ETJ subdivision.** Categorically unavailable.
- **Trying to use WQ fee-in-lieu in the BSZ or Water Supply watersheds.** Urban Watersheds only.
- **Assuming the BSZ Redevelopment Exception works for residential redevelopment.** Commercial only, and unpermitted post-1992 development cannot be cured.
- **Underestimating retaining wall building-permit overhead.** Walls ≥ 4 ft trigger a separate IBC permit on a different review track.
- **Universal "4 ft and accessible = safety rail" rule for retaining walls.** Not how TCM 13.2.10 works — function- and adjacent-use-driven.
- **Missing the dam threshold at any point of perimeter.** A pond is a dam if any single point of the embankment reaches 6 ft (DCM 8.3.3.B.1); the whole facility is reclassified.
- **Forgetting agency coordination for RSMP** — PARD parkland discharge, TxDOT ROW discharge, downstream jurisdiction approval can extend the schedule materially.
- **Combining the existing and proposed drainage area maps on one sheet.** Must be separate sheets at the same scale for direct comparison.
- **Citing superseded standards** — UBC (now IBC), "Watershed Engineering Division" (now "Office of the Director"), pre-Atlas 14 rainfall, BCM 15.4/15.10 for resubmittal/site plan requirements.
- **Skipping the pre-Completeness-Check RSMP Feasibility Meeting.** A development cannot pass Completeness Check without it.

    37→### ROW dedication (existing vs. future)

An informal "infeasible" note on plans does **not** satisfy. ATD usually conditions waiver on a recorded alternative easement (sidewalk or public access).

    51→### TIA threshold and likely findings
    52→
    53→- Threshold uses **unadjusted ITE daily trips** — no pass-by, internal capture, or TDM reductions for threshold determination. Only existing on-site occupied uses with documented occupancy may be subtracted.
    54→- < 2,000 trips: no study, but sub-threshold mitigation (sidewalks, signals, traffic calming, bike lanes, RRFB/PHB, urban trails, ROW, TDM) within ¼ mile (or ¾ mile to schools/bus stops/major roads) can still be required under LDC § 25-6-101(B).
    55→- 2,000–4,999 trips: **Transportation Assessment + TDM Plan** (LDC § 25-6-113; TCM 10.2.1).

    69→- **Spacing minimums** from intersections, adjacent driveways, drainage inlets — confirm via TCM 7.6. Throat storage length per land use.
    70→- **Joint-use driveway** requires a recorded easement with maintenance assigned (TCM 7.6.4) — built into the title package.

    74→### Scenic Roadway constraints
    75→

The bureau guides cite § 25-10-7 / § 25-10-81 / § 25-10-124 for the **sign district**, and Hill Country Roadway development standards at LDC § 25-2-1025 / § 25-2-1127 for the *development* envelope. Confirm the controlling section against current code before drafting findings.

    82→

    85→- **Bus stop integration**: CapMetro coordination required where a stop fronts the site; floating bus stop platforms (where bike lane runs behind the stop) carry specific TCM dimensions.

    87→- **Accessible parking** is the only motor-vehicle parking minimum that survived the November 2023 elimination of general parking minimums (LDC §§ 25-6-471(B), 25-6-474(A)(3)). Calculated at 100% Appendix A → Building Code table; van-accessible 1 per 6 (IBC 1106.5).

    89→### Street Impact Fees
    90→
    91→- Applies to virtually all building-permit development (LDC § 25-6-662). Independent of TIA — a TIA waiver does *not* waive SIF.

Reference: LDC 25-6-662."*

    98→## Opportunities to evaluate
    99→
   100→- **TIA-driven public improvements**: TIAs frequently identify intersection improvements that the city or TxDOT may co-fund or accelerate; coordinate with TDS during scoping.
   101→- **Sub-threshold projects can structure SIF offsets** by constructing on-Roadway-Capacity-Plan improvements (LDC § 25-6-669) rather than paying full SIF.
   102→- **Fee-in-lieu of sidewalk** under LDC § 25-6-354 / TCM 4.1.6 — useful where physical sidewalk install conflicts with trees, drainage, or existing utilities.
   103→- **TIA waiver** under LDC § 25-6-117 — does not waive mitigation, but can streamline timeline if scope is genuinely limited.
   104→- **Cross-access / shared driveway** with neighboring sites reduces driveway count, can satisfy joint-use easement (TCM 7.6.4), and is preferred by ATD on arterials.
   105→- **Regulating plan bonuses**: ERC, NBG, and TOD districts include reduced parking maxima and active-edge incentives that can be leveraged in concept design.
   106→- **Project Connect / ETOD proximity** — ETOD-zoned sites (LDC § 25-2-182) carry density bonuses tied to transit corridor presence; verify against ETOD subdistrict layer.
   107→
   108→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   109→
   110→- **transportation.md** — for each street frontage: existing ROW width (survey), ASMP Street Level + target half-width, Bicycle Priority Network status, AADT (TxDOT for state-maintained), functional class, posted speed, Project Connect / scenic / Hill Country flags.
   111→- **property-records.md** — recorded street deeds, existing access easements, joint-use driveway easements, vacated street documentation, prior ROW dedication instrument numbers.
   112→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed land use mix (with ITE codes), gross square footage / unit counts, proposed driveway locations + count, design vehicle (WB-50 vs. WB-62), parking garage proposed (high-capacity driveway?).
   113→- **zoning / overlays** — regulating plan membership (NBG, ERC, MLK TOD, Plaza Saltillo, Lamar/Justin Lane), Hill Country Roadway corridor flag, Scenic Roadway flag, UNO / NCCD overlays, ETOD subdistrict.
   114→- **adjacent_context** (surveyor `property_profile` + `adjacent_context`) — abutting ASMP/AMTP segments, neighbor zoning for NTA frontage test.
   115→
   116→## Output structure
   117→
   118→Standard discipline output shape; cite `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.
   119→
   120→## Severity heuristics
   121→
   122→| Finding | Severity |
   123→|---|---|
   124→| Future ROW dedication consumes > 10% of gross site OR > 15% of any one frontage's developable depth | `significant` |
   125→| Project triggers Full TIA (≥ 5,000 unadjusted trips) with likely off-site mitigation obligations | `significant` |
   126→| TxDOT frontage with unresolved 200-ft long-term ROW reservation (IH-35, US-290, SH-71, Parmer) | `significant` |
   127→| Orange Line / Project Connect corridor reservation plausibly applies (Guadalupe, Lavaca, Congress) | `significant` (flag for human verification) |
   128→| Project triggers Transportation Assessment (2,000–4,999 trips) with TDM Plan | `moderate` to `significant` |
   129→| Proposed driveway location conflicts with TCM 7.6 spacing or Type I prohibited on Level 3/4 | `moderate` |
   130→| NTA likely triggered (≥ 300 net new trips + residential frontage) | `moderate` |
   131→| Hill Country Roadway corridor frontage (Loop 360, RM 620/2222/2244, SW Parkway) | `moderate` |
   132→| Site within 200 ft of a § 25-10-7 Scenic Roadway (sign + character constraints) | `moderate` |
   133→| Bicycle Priority Network frontage requiring AAA facility ROW beyond standard | `moderate` |
   134→| Site requires sidewalk fee-in-lieu or shared-access agreement | `note` to `moderate` |
   135→| Adequate existing ROW + sub-2,000-trip use + no overlay frontage | `note` |
   136→
   137→## Common pitfalls
   138→
   139→- **Citing existing ROW instead of future ASMP ROW** when sizing setbacks or area calculations. The legal dedication obligation is from centerline to ASMP target half-width, not from the existing property line.
   140→- **Applying pass-by, internal-capture, or TDM reductions to TIA threshold trips.** Threshold determination uses *unadjusted* ITE rates only. Reductions can be claimed in the TIA itself, never in the determination.
   141→- **Treating SIF as paid at site plan approval.** SIF is **collected at building permit issuance** per LDC § 25-6-663(B). Cover sheet notes asserting otherwise are a checklist deficiency.
   142→- **Submitting applicant-engineer SIF worksheet as the § 25-6-23 proportionality determination.** The determination must be a City-issued memo signed by a City-retained PE.
   143→- **Starting TIA work before TDS-signed scope.** Studies prepared before scope approval will not be reviewed.
   144→- **Confusing functional class with jurisdictional ownership.** ASMP Level 5 = TxDOT; streets prefixed IH/US/SH = TxDOT-maintained. ASMP Level 4 includes service roads/ramps, which surveyor data flags as *not* highways.
   145→- **Missing Scenic Roadway Sign District** — applies up to 200 ft from any of 23 named roadways and 1,000 ft from Hill Country Roadway corridors. Easy to miss because the *sign* district lives in Chapter 25-10 rather than the transportation chapter.
   146→- **Confusing Scenic Roadway sign rules (Ch. 25-10) with Hill Country Roadway development rules (LDC §§ 25-2-1025, 25-2-1127).** Different overlays, different impacts — site can be in one but not the other.
   147→- **Citing 65 ft / 130 ft Orange Line reservation as a Bureau-codified requirement.** It is not in TCM or LDC; it comes from the Project Connect System Plan map. Always flag for external verification.
   148→- **Type I driveway proposed on a Level 3 or Level 4 street.** Always prohibited regardless of use (TCM 7.3.1.C).
   149→- **Plat used to dedicate easements** (sidewalk, sight distance, public access). Plat approval is not acceptance of dedication (LDC § 30-2-39); separate easement instruments using City templates are required.
   150→- **Assuming general motor-vehicle parking minimums still apply.** Austin eliminated minimums in November 2023; only accessible parking + bicycle parking minimums survive.
   151→- **Ignoring the 5-year TIA validity window.** Older TIAs need TDS written confirmation of continued validity or an updated study (TCM 10.4.3).
   152→

- **Waiver**: LDC § 25-6-81 — formal written waiver required if full dedication is infeasible; available when ≥ 15% of property is subject to ROW reservation. An informal "infeasible" note on plans does **not** satisfy. ATD usually conditions waiver on a recorded alternative easement (sidewalk or public access).
- **IC math**: ROW pavement counts as IC; sidewalks in ROW or public easement are excluded (LDC § 25-8-63(C)(1)). On Hill Country Roadway sites, ROW > 60 ft from centerline counts in IC denominator (LDC § 25-2-1127), and 40% natural area is measured excluding dedicated ROW (LDC § 25-2-1025).

### TIA threshold and likely findings

- Threshold uses **unadjusted ITE daily trips** — no pass-by, internal capture, or TDM reductions for threshold determination. Only existing on-site occupied uses with documented occupancy may be subtracted.
- < 2,000 trips: no study, but sub-threshold mitigation (sidewalks, signals, traffic calming, bike lanes, RRFB/PHB, urban trails, ROW, TDM) within ¼ mile (or ¾ mile to schools/bus stops/major roads) can still be required under LDC § 25-6-101(B).
- 2,000–4,999 trips: **Transportation Assessment + TDM Plan** (LDC § 25-6-113; TCM 10.2.1).
- ≥ 5,000 trips: **Full TIA + TDM Plan**.
- All TIA work requires a **TDS-approved scope** signed by both the applicant's consultant and the TDS Lead Development Review Engineer *before* the study starts (TIA Guidelines § 4.3.2). Studies prepared without an approved scope will not be reviewed.
- Approved TIAs are valid **5 years** from final memo date or assumed build-out, whichever is earlier (TCM 10.4.3). Plan trip-budgeting accordingly.
- **TIA Compliance Letter** is a separate document from the TIA itself; if a prior TIA exists, expect a TIA Tracking Table on the cover sheet showing allowed/used/remaining VTDs and a 7-element compliance letter.
- **NTA** triggers when project accesses a non-arterial street with ≥ 50% SF-5+ frontage within 1,500 ft AND adds ≥ 300 net new daily trips (or is a public K-12). TDS writes the memo; applicant submits 24-hr tube counts.
- **Table 10-6** (TCM 10.4.4) sets nexus standards for required mitigations by category and study type — review before committing to off-site work.
- **Fiscal surety** under LDC § 25-1-112 must be posted before site plan approval for any unbuilt TIA-required improvements; below-market cost estimates without director approval will be rejected.

### Driveway and access management

- **Driveway type by use + street level** (TCM 7.3.1–7.3.2): Type I (residential) is **prohibited on ASMP Level 3 or 4 streets** regardless of use. Multi-family > 4 units requires Type II.
- **Max driveway width** (TCM 7.5.1.2, Table 7-2): Level 1 typical 20 ft (industrial 25 ft); Level 2 w/ 3-lane fire access 25 ft; high-capacity driveway serving a garage capped at 32 ft. Other Level 2/3/4 widths: verify against current TCM (Bureau data incomplete).
- **Driveway count per frontage** is capped; **opposing-driveway offset** rules can force right-in/right-out only.
- **Spacing minimums** from intersections, adjacent driveways, drainage inlets — confirm via TCM 7.6. Throat storage length per land use.
- **Joint-use driveway** requires a recorded easement with maintenance assigned (TCM 7.6.4) — built into the title package.
- **Hill Country Roadway** corridors (Loop 360 US-290W to US-183; RM 620 SH-71 to Anderson Mill; RM 2222 Highland Hills to RM 620; RM 2244 Loop 360 to SH-71; Southwest Parkway) impose extra access-spacing, grade, curve, and sight-distance restrictions (covered under guide 31).
- **Curb return radii** per TCM Table 7-1; downtown / ERC / UNO / NBG have overlay-specific values.

### Scenic Roadway constraints

- **Scenic Roadway Sign District** (LDC § 25-10-81(3); LDC § 25-10-124) — applies to land within **1,000 ft of a Hill Country Roadway corridor** OR **200 ft of any of the 23 Scenic Roadways** enumerated in LDC § 25-10-7 (e.g., Barton Springs Rd, Lake Austin Blvd, MoPac, Loop 360, RM 2222, RM 2244, William Cannon, Riverside Dr, SH 130). Governs sign size, height, lighting, setback.
- Historic and expressway sign districts override scenic per LDC § 25-10-82.
- Note: the user prompt referenced LDC § 25-2-871 (scenic roadway). The bureau guides cite § 25-10-7 / § 25-10-81 / § 25-10-124 for the **sign district**, and Hill Country Roadway development standards at LDC § 25-2-1025 / § 25-2-1127 for the *development* envelope. Confirm the controlling section against current code before drafting findings.
- For **Hill Country Roadway** sites the more material development constraints are the 40% natural-area requirement (excluding dedicated ROW; LDC § 25-2-1025), grade/cut-fill limits along the corridor, and ROW > 60 ft from centerline counting in IC denominator (LDC § 25-2-1127).

### Sidewalk, transit, and bike obligations

- **Sidewalk required on every street frontage** unless approved fee-in-lieu (LDC § 25-6-354; TCM 4.1.6). Minimum clear widths: Level 1 = 5 ft; Level 2 = 6 ft (constrained 5 ft w/ approval). Downtown Great Streets = 18 ft total streetscape zone; Core Transit Corridors = 15 ft total zone.
- **Bicycle facilities** on the ASMP Bicycle Priority Network must be AAA-grade (Protected Bike Lane, Shared Use Path, or Neighborhood Bikeway per TCM 5.1.4). Planting-zone width: 8 ft (Level 2–3 recommended), 10 ft (Level 4 recommended), 6.5 ft constrained.
- **Bus stop integration**: CapMetro coordination required where a stop fronts the site; floating bus stop platforms (where bike lane runs behind the stop) carry specific TCM dimensions.
- **Bicycle parking** required citywide under LDC § 25-6-477 regardless of motor-vehicle parking; short-term + long-term split by use; TOD overlays add requirements.
- **Accessible parking** is the only motor-vehicle parking minimum that survived the November 2023 elimination of general parking minimums (LDC §§ 25-6-471(B), 25-6-474(A)(3)). Calculated at 100% Appendix A → Building Code table; van-accessible 1 per 6 (IBC 1106.5).

### Street Impact Fees

- Applies to virtually all building-permit development (LDC § 25-6-662). Independent of TIA — a TIA waiver does *not* waive SIF.
- **Assessed** at plat or building permit application; **collected** at building permit issuance (LDC § 25-6-663(B)). Plan notes stating SIF is paid at site plan approval are incorrect.
- Process: applicant submits SIF Estimator Worksheet via ATD KNACK portal → TDS Engineering issues SIF Formal Calculation Memo → payment at each building permit.
- SIF can be used as the proportionality measure under § 25-6-23.
- Offset agreements available under § 25-6-669 for developer-constructed Roadway Capacity Plan improvements.
- Required cover-sheet note: *"Development of structures that require a building permit within this Site Plan, or revisions thereof, are required to comply with the City of Austin Street Impact Fee Ordinances, as applicable, and must be paid upon completion of the building permit plan review for each building. Reference: LDC 25-6-662."*

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **TIA-driven public improvements**: TIAs frequently identify intersection improvements that the city or TxDOT may co-fund or accelerate; coordinate with TDS during scoping.
- **Sub-threshold projects can structure SIF offsets** by constructing on-Roadway-Capacity-Plan improvements (LDC § 25-6-669) rather than paying full SIF.
- **Fee-in-lieu of sidewalk** under LDC § 25-6-354 / TCM 4.1.6 — useful where physical sidewalk install conflicts with trees, drainage, or existing utilities.
- **TIA waiver** under LDC § 25-6-117 — does not waive mitigation, but can streamline timeline if scope is genuinely limited.
- **Cross-access / shared driveway** with neighboring sites reduces driveway count, can satisfy joint-use easement (TCM 7.6.4), and is preferred by ATD on arterials.
- **Regulating plan bonuses**: ERC, NBG, and TOD districts include reduced parking maxima and active-edge incentives that can be leveraged in concept design.
- **Project Connect / ETOD proximity** — ETOD-zoned sites (LDC § 25-2-182) carry density bonuses tied to transit corridor presence; verify against ETOD subdistrict layer.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **transportation.md** — for each street frontage: existing ROW width (survey), ASMP Street Level + target half-width, Bicycle Priority Network status, AADT (TxDOT for state-maintained), functional class, posted speed, Project Connect / scenic / Hill Country flags.
- **property-records.md** — recorded street deeds, existing access easements, joint-use driveway easements, vacated street documentation, prior ROW dedication instrument numbers.
- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed land use mix (with ITE codes), gross square footage / unit counts, proposed driveway locations + count, design vehicle (WB-50 vs. WB-62), parking garage proposed (high-capacity driveway?).
- **zoning / overlays** — regulating plan membership (NBG, ERC, MLK TOD, Plaza Saltillo, Lamar/Justin Lane), Hill Country Roadway corridor flag, Scenic Roadway flag, UNO / NCCD overlays, ETOD subdistrict.
- **adjacent_context** (surveyor `property_profile` + `adjacent_context`) — abutting ASMP/AMTP segments, neighbor zoning for NTA frontage test.

## Output structure

Standard discipline output shape; cite `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.

## Severity heuristics

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| Future ROW dedication consumes > 10% of gross site OR > 15% of any one frontage's developable depth | `significant` |
| Project triggers Full TIA (≥ 5,000 unadjusted trips) with likely off-site mitigation obligations | `significant` |
| TxDOT frontage with unresolved 200-ft long-term ROW reservation (IH-35, US-290, SH-71, Parmer) | `significant` |
| Orange Line / Project Connect corridor reservation plausibly applies (Guadalupe, Lavaca, Congress) | `significant` (flag for human verification) |
| Project triggers Transportation Assessment (2,000–4,999 trips) with TDM Plan | `moderate` to `significant` |
| Proposed driveway location conflicts with TCM 7.6 spacing or Type I prohibited on Level 3/4 | `moderate` |
| NTA likely triggered (≥ 300 net new trips + residential frontage) | `moderate` |
| Hill Country Roadway corridor frontage (Loop 360, RM 620/2222/2244, SW Parkway) | `moderate` |
| Site within 200 ft of a § 25-10-7 Scenic Roadway (sign + character constraints) | `moderate` |
| Bicycle Priority Network frontage requiring AAA facility ROW beyond standard | `moderate` |
| Site requires sidewalk fee-in-lieu or shared-access agreement | `note` to `moderate` |
| Adequate existing ROW + sub-2,000-trip use + no overlay frontage | `note` |

## Common pitfalls

- **Citing existing ROW instead of future ASMP ROW** when sizing setbacks or area calculations. The legal dedication obligation is from centerline to ASMP target half-width, not from the existing property line.
- **Applying pass-by, internal-capture, or TDM reductions to TIA threshold trips.** Threshold determination uses *unadjusted* ITE rates only. Reductions can be claimed in the TIA itself, never in the determination.
- **Treating SIF as paid at site plan approval.** SIF is **collected at building permit issuance** per LDC § 25-6-663(B). Cover sheet notes asserting otherwise are a checklist deficiency.
- **Submitting applicant-engineer SIF worksheet as the § 25-6-23 proportionality determination.** The determination must be a City-issued memo signed by a City-retained PE.
- **Starting TIA work before TDS-signed scope.** Studies prepared before scope approval will not be reviewed.
- **Confusing functional class with jurisdictional ownership.** ASMP Level 5 = TxDOT; streets prefixed IH/US/SH = TxDOT-maintained. ASMP Level 4 includes service roads/ramps, which surveyor data flags as *not* highways.
- **Missing Scenic Roadway Sign District** — applies up to 200 ft from any of 23 named roadways and 1,000 ft from Hill Country Roadway corridors. Easy to miss because the *sign* district lives in Chapter 25-10 rather than the transportation chapter.
- **Confusing Scenic Roadway sign rules (Ch. 25-10) with Hill Country Roadway development rules (LDC §§ 25-2-1025, 25-2-1127).** Different overlays, different impacts — site can be in one but not the other.
- **Citing 65 ft / 130 ft Orange Line reservation as a Bureau-codified requirement.** It is not in TCM or LDC; it comes from the Project Connect System Plan map. Always flag for external verification.
- **Type I driveway proposed on a Level 3 or Level 4 street.** Always prohibited regardless of use (TCM 7.3.1.C).
- **Plat used to dedicate easements** (sidewalk, sight distance, public access). Plat approval is not acceptance of dedication (LDC § 30-2-39); separate easement instruments using City templates are required.
- **Assuming general motor-vehicle parking minimums still apply.** Austin eliminated minimums in November 2023; only accessible parking + bicycle parking minimums survive.
- **Ignoring the 5-year TIA validity window.** Older TIAs need TDS written confirmation of continued validity or an updated study (TCM 10.4.3).
