# Zoning Pathway Analysis

**Property:** 12713 Cinchring Ln, Austin, TX 78727
**Legal:** Lot 12, Block M, Scofield Subdivision, Travis County
**Proposed Use:** Demolish existing single-family house; construct ground-up duplex (2 units)
**Date of Research:** 2026-06-03

---

## Base District

The property is zoned **SF-2 (Single-Family Residential -- Standard Lot)** per the Austin Land Development Code. SF-2 is the standard single-family district with a minimum lot size of 5,750 sq ft. The lot is approximately 0.18 acres (~7,840 sq ft), which exceeds the SF-2 minimum and the 7,000 sq ft minimum lot area historically required for duplex use.

Under pre-HOME zoning, SF-2 did **not** permit duplex or two-family residential use. That changed with HOME Phase 1 (see Recent Ordinances below).

**Citation:** Austin LDC Title 25, Ch. 25-2, Subchapter C, Art. 2, Div. 1, Section 25-2-492 (Site Development Regulations Table); [Municode -- LDC Ch. 25-2](https://library.municode.com/tx/austin/codes/land_development_code?nodeId=TIT25LADE_CH25-2ZO)

---

## Duplex Permissibility Under HOME Phase 1

**HOME Phase 1** (Ordinance No. 20231207-001, effective February 5, 2024) amended the LDC to allow up to three dwelling units -- including duplexes, two-unit residential, and three-unit residential uses -- on any lot zoned SF-1, SF-2, or SF-3.

Key provisions:

- **Unit count:** Up to 3 dwelling units permitted on SF-1/SF-2/SF-3 lots. A duplex (2 units) is permitted by right.
- **Minimum lot area for duplex/two-unit:** 5,750 sq ft (the lot at ~7,840 sq ft qualifies).
- **Minimum lot width:** 50 ft (per LDC duplex standards; verify against plat).
- **Removes primary/secondary distinction:** All dwelling units are treated equally; no unit is an "accessory."
- **Removes unrelated-adult occupancy limits.**
- **Each dwelling unit requires a unique address.**

**Citation:** [HOME Amendments -- Austin Development Services](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/home-amendments); Ordinance 20231207-001

---

## Dimensional Envelope

### Pre-HOME SF-2 Base Standards (LDC Section 25-2-492)

| Standard | SF-2 Requirement |
|---|---|
| Minimum lot area | 5,750 sq ft |
| Minimum lot width | 50 ft |
| Maximum height | 35 ft |
| Maximum building coverage | 40% |
| Maximum impervious cover | 45% |
| Floor-to-area ratio (FAR) | 0.40:1 |
| Front yard setback | 25 ft |
| Side yard setback | 5 ft (15 ft on street side of corner lot) |
| Rear yard setback | 10 ft |

**Citation:** LDC Section 25-2-492(D); [Site Plan Creator -- Austin TX](https://www.siteplancreator.com/site-plans/austin-tx)

### HOME Phase 1 Modified Standards for Two-Unit / Duplex

HOME Phase 1 incorporated the advantageous setbacks previously available only under Subchapter F (Residential Design and Compatibility Standards) and extended them to all SF-district properties building two- or three-unit uses:

| Standard | HOME Phase 1 (Duplex/Two-Unit) |
|---|---|
| Front yard setback | **15 ft** (reduced from 25 ft) |
| Street side yard setback | **10 ft** (reduced from 15 ft) |
| Interior side yard setback | **5 ft** (unchanged) |
| Rear yard setback | **5 ft** (reduced from 10 ft), excl. easements |
| Maximum height | **35 ft** |
| Maximum building coverage | **40%** |
| Maximum impervious cover | **45%** (or watershed limit, whichever is more restrictive) |
| FAR | **0.40:1** |
| Building separation (zoning) | **None required by zoning**; must comply with IRC fire-separation requirements |

**Citation:** [HOME Amendments -- Austin Development Services](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/home-amendments); [AIA Austin HOME Phase 1 Summary](https://aiaaustin.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/HOME_Summary-FAQ_20240126-1039.pdf); [Maxable -- HOME Initiative](https://maxablespace.com/austins-home-initiative-shakes-up-adu-regulations-in-2024/)

### Practical Envelope on This Lot (~7,840 sq ft)

| Metric | Calculation |
|---|---|
| Max building footprint (40%) | ~3,136 sq ft |
| Max impervious cover (45%) | ~3,528 sq ft |
| Max gross floor area (0.40:1 FAR) | ~3,136 sq ft |

**Preservation Bonus:** If the existing house were preserved (moved, not demolished), the preserved structure's GFA would be exempt from FAR calculations. Since the plan is demolition, this bonus does not apply.

---

## 25-Foot Platted Building Line

The recorded plat for Scofield Subdivision shows a **25-foot building line** on the front of Lot 12.

**Interaction with HOME Phase 1 setbacks:**

- HOME Phase 1 reduces the zoning front setback to 15 ft for two-unit/duplex uses.
- However, a platted building line is a deed restriction recorded against the land. Under Austin practice, **the more restrictive requirement controls** -- meaning the 25 ft platted building line governs over the 15 ft zoning setback.
- To use the 15 ft front setback, the owner would need to **replat or amend the plat** to remove or reduce the building line, which requires subdivision review.

**Recommendation:** Confirm whether Austin treats the platted building line as enforceable through the permitting process or only as a private covenant. If enforceable, factor a 25 ft front setback into the building envelope. If a variance or replat is viable, the 15 ft setback could unlock additional depth.

**Citation:** [Global Land Surveying -- Building Setbacks: Plats, Zoning, and Covenants](https://gls-inc.com/3-building-setbacks-plats-zoning-and-covenants/); Austin LDC subdivision standards

---

## Overlays

### Neighborhood Plan / NCCD

Scofield Farms (78727) is a 1990s-era suburban subdivision in north Austin. Based on research, **no Neighborhood Conservation Combining District (NCCD) overlay applies** to this area. NCCDs in Austin are concentrated in older central neighborhoods (Hyde Park, Heritage, etc.) that were substantially built out over 30 years before adoption.

No Neighborhood Plan (NP) combining district appears to apply to this part of 78727.

### Conditional Overlay (CO)

No conditional overlay was identified in search results for this address. Verify via Austin's Property Profile or GIS map.

### Historic Landmark / Historic District

No historic designation was identified. The house was built in 1993 and is not eligible for local landmark status (typically requires 50+ years of age or exceptional significance).

### Watershed Overlay

The property is in the **Walnut Creek watershed**, classified as a **suburban watershed** in the Austin Watershed Protection Ordinance. For suburban watersheds:

- Single-family residential impervious cover: governed by zoning (45% for SF-2)
- The watershed ordinance impervious cover limit for suburban watersheds is generally 40-55% depending on use category
- The **more restrictive** of zoning or watershed limits applies
- For this property, the 45% zoning limit is likely the controlling standard

**Citation:** [WGI -- Austin Impervious Cover Limits](https://wginc.com/the-city-of-austin-impervious-cover-limits-for-mixed-use-buildings/); Austin LDC Ch. 25-8 (Environmental)

### Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI)

Scofield Farms may fall within or near the WUI boundary. As of November 16, 2024, HOME Phase 2 applications are accepted citywide including WUI areas. HOME Phase 1 (duplex) was not initially restricted by WUI. Confirm WUI status via Austin GIS.

---

## Parking

Austin City Council voted 8-2 on **November 2, 2023** (effective November 12, 2023) to **eliminate all minimum parking requirements** citywide. This applies to all use types including single-family, duplex, multifamily, commercial, and office.

**What this means for this duplex project:**

- **No minimum parking spaces are required by code.**
- ADA-accessible parking must still comply with federal law if applicable.
- As a practical matter, most duplex developers in suburban locations still provide **2 spaces per unit** (4 total) via driveways and/or garages, since market expectations in north Austin neighborhoods include vehicle parking.

**Citation:** [Texas Tribune -- Austin Drops Parking Minimums](https://www.texastribune.org/2023/11/02/austin-minimum-parking-requirements-housing-shortage/); [KUT -- Austin Ends Parking Requirements](https://www.kut.org/austin/2023-11-02/austin-becomes-one-of-the-largest-cities-in-the-country-to-get-rid-of-parking-requirements); Ordinance C20-2023-010

---

## Procedural Pathway

### Site Plan Exemption

Under Austin LDC, **residential uses of four or fewer units are exempt from site plan requirements**. A duplex (2 units) qualifies for this exemption. No administrative site plan is required.

### Building Permit

The duplex can proceed via a **residential building permit** application through Austin Development Services (DSD). Under HOME Phase 1, applications have been accepted since February 5, 2024.

**Permit review path:**

1. **Residential Plan Review** -- submit building plans through Austin DSD
2. Plans reviewed for compliance with LDC dimensional standards, IRC/IBC building codes, and applicable environmental/drainage requirements
3. No zoning change, conditional use permit, or Board of Adjustment variance is needed (assuming the lot meets dimensional standards)

### Site Plan Lite (HOME Phase 2 -- March 2025)

Site Plan Lite is a streamlined review process adopted March 6, 2025, primarily for HOME Phase 2 subdivision and small-lot projects. It is **not required** for a duplex on an existing lot that already meets SF-2 minimum lot size. However, if the owner later pursues subdivision of the lot (e.g., into two small lots), Site Plan Lite would apply.

### Demolition Permit

A separate **demolition permit** is required to remove the existing house. Austin DSD processes demo permits administratively; typical turnaround is 2-4 weeks. Asbestos survey may be required for pre-2000 construction (this house was built 1993).

### Tree Permits

Austin's tree ordinance (LDC Ch. 25-8, Subchapter B) protects trees with trunk diameter >= 19 inches (heritage trees >= 24 inches). A tree survey may be required, and mitigation fees or replacement may apply if protected trees must be removed.

**Citation:** [Austin DSD -- Residential Plan Review](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/residential-plan-review); [Austin DSD -- Site Plans and Exemptions](https://www.austintexas.gov/siteplans); [HOME Amendments Page](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/home-amendments)

---

## Recent Ordinances

| Ordinance | Effective | Impact on This Project |
|---|---|---|
| **HOME Phase 1** (Ord. 20231207-001) | Feb 5, 2024 | Permits duplex/two-unit on SF-2 lots; reduces front setback to 15 ft, rear to 5 ft |
| **Parking Minimums Elimination** (C20-2023-010) | Nov 12, 2023 | No minimum parking required for duplex |
| **HOME Phase 2** (adopted May 2024) | Nov 16, 2024 (citywide) | Allows small-lot SF down to 1,800 sq ft; not directly required for duplex but enables future subdivision |
| **Site Plan Lite & Infill Plat** (March 2025) | June 16, 2025 | Streamlined review for subdivisions; not required for duplex on existing lot |

---

## Open Questions

1. **Confirm base zoning via Austin GIS/Property Profile.** While research strongly indicates SF-2, the official zoning should be verified on the [Austin Zoning Map](https://www.austintexas.gov/page/zoning-resources-site-regulations) or via the Property Profile tool. One listing source referenced "residential multi family" which may reflect HOME-amended permitted uses rather than the base district code.

2. **Platted building line enforcement.** Does Austin DSD enforce the 25 ft platted building line through the building permit process, or is it treated as a private covenant enforceable only by adjacent lot owners? If enforced, the front setback is 25 ft (not 15 ft), reducing the buildable envelope by ~10 ft of depth.

3. **Lot width.** Confirm the lot width meets the 50 ft minimum required for duplex use. At 0.18 acres (~7,840 sq ft), the lot geometry needs verification from the plat.

4. **Watershed impervious cover.** Confirm the Walnut Creek suburban watershed impervious cover limit for this specific parcel. The 45% zoning limit is likely controlling, but verify via Austin's watershed GIS layer.

5. **HOA restrictions.** Scofield Farms has an HOA ($125/quarter per listing data). HOA covenants, conditions, and restrictions (CC&Rs) may prohibit or restrict duplex construction, impose architectural review, or set additional setback/height/design requirements independent of city zoning. Review the recorded CC&Rs and any deed restrictions on Lot 12, Block M.

6. **Tree survey.** Confirm whether any protected or heritage trees exist on the lot that would require mitigation.

7. **Drainage review.** For demolition and new construction on an existing lot (not a new subdivision), confirm whether drainage/grading plan review is required or if the project falls under the four-unit residential exemption.

8. **WUI status.** Confirm whether the property is within the Wildland-Urban Interface boundary, which may impose additional fire-resistant construction standards.

---

## Summary Assessment

A ground-up duplex at 12713 Cinchring Ln is **permitted by right** under HOME Phase 1 on this SF-2 lot. The project can proceed via **residential building permit only** -- no rezoning, conditional use permit, site plan, or Board of Adjustment action is required. Key constraints are the 40% building coverage / 0.40 FAR cap, the 45% impervious cover limit, and the potential 25 ft front building line from the plat (versus the 15 ft HOME setback). The most significant non-zoning risk is the Scofield Farms HOA CC&Rs, which should be reviewed before design proceeds.

- [Imagine Austin Growth Concept Map (ArcGIS)](https://www.arcgis.com/apps/webappviewer/index.html?id=3c602527fd7146129d14aad9db223959)
- [Imagine Austin Activity Centers and Corridors Conceptual View (PDF)](https://nwaca.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Imagine-Austin-Activity-Centers-and-Corridors-Conceptual-View.pdf)

## 5. Station-Area / Transit-Oriented Plans

**Finding: No TOD overlay applies. No Project Connect station is planned near this parcel.**

The Project Connect Orange Line runs along the North Lamar/Guadalupe corridor, roughly 2 miles east of MoPac. The nearest planned station in the initial investment is the North Lamar Transit Center (at Lamar and US-183), approximately 4 miles south of this property. Future extension stations at Parmer Lane and Tech Ridge are along the I-35/North Lamar alignment, not MoPac, and are not included in the initial investment phase -- they will operate as MetroRapid bus stops until light rail is extended (estimated 2040s).

No Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) overlay district has been adopted for any area near this parcel. The City of Austin's equitable TOD planning efforts have focused on the Blue Line (east-west) and the initial Orange Line corridor segments, none of which reach the Scofield area.

- [Project Connect by CapMetro](https://www.projectconnect.com/)
- [Orange Line Station Locations (Community Impact)](https://communityimpact.com/austin/central-austin/transportation/2021/06/17/project-connect-orange-line-design-reveals-proposed-locations-for-rail-stations-in-north-south-austin/)
- [CapMetro - Project Connect Initial Investment Map (PDF)](https://www.capmetro.org/docs/default-source/project_connect/home-page/project-connect-initial-investment-servicelevelmap.pdf)

## 6. Active Neighborhood Associations

**Finding: The Scofield Farms ROA is the primary community organization. No public posture on density/duplex development was identified.**

The **Scofield Residential Owners Association (ROA)** governs approximately 574 homes in the Scofield Farms community. It is managed by Inframark and led by a 5-member Board of Directors elected annually. The ROA maintains an Architectural Control Committee (ACC) that reviews proposed changes to homes and landscaping.

A separate organization, **The Ridge at Scofield Farms**, covers a distinct section of the broader Scofield development.

No public statements, meeting minutes, or advocacy positions regarding infill density, duplex construction, or zoning changes were identified on the ROA's website or in public records. The ACC's purview is limited to aesthetic and architectural standards within the existing HOA covenants, not municipal zoning or land-use entitlements.

Applicants should check the [City of Austin Community Registry](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/community-registry) to confirm which registered organizations receive notice for development applications at this address.

- [Scofield Farms ROA](https://scofieldfarms.org/)
- [The Ridge at Scofield Farms](https://www.scofieldridge.org/)
- [City of Austin - Community Registry Search](https://www.austintexas.gov/page/community-registry-search)

---

## Summary for Duplex Feasibility

| Factor | Status | Impact on Duplex |
|--------|--------|-----------------|
| Adopted neighborhood plan | None | No NP-specific land-use restrictions apply |
| NP combining district | None | No additional NP overlay standards |
| FLUM designation | Suburban residential (policy only) | Does not prohibit duplex if base zoning allows |
| Imagine Austin corridor | Near Parmer Lane Activity Corridor | Policy supports incremental density near corridors |
| TOD overlay | None | No transit-oriented standards apply |
| HOA / neighborhood group | Scofield Farms ROA | Private covenants may apply; check CC&Rs separately |

The absence of an adopted neighborhood plan and NP combining district means there are no plan-based overlay restrictions on this parcel. Duplex entitlement depends on the base zoning district and applicable LDC standards, not on neighborhood plan policy.

# Transportation Context

Property: 12713 Cinchring Ln, Austin, TX 78727 (Lot 12, Block M, Scofield Subdivision, Travis County)
Proposed use: Demolish existing single-family house; build duplex (2 units, ground-up new construction)

---

## 1. Adjacent Roadway -- Cinchring Lane

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Functional classification | Local residential street |
| ASMP street level | Level 1 |
| Ownership | City of Austin |
| Lanes | 2 (undivided) |
| Existing ROW (typical) | 50 ft |
| Future ROW (ASMP) | 50 ft (no expansion planned) |
| AADT | Not published; estimated < 500 vpd (local cul-de-sac / loop street) |
| Speed limit | 25 mph (residential default) |

Cinchring Lane is a low-volume local residential street interior to the Scofield Subdivision. Under the Austin Strategic Mobility Plan (ASMP), streets not named in the Street Network Table default to Level 1. Level 1 streets typically have a 50-ft ROW with two travel lanes and no center turn lane. No ROW expansion or street widening is anticipated.

## 2. Nearby Major Roads

| Street | ASMP Level | Functional Class | Lanes | Existing ROW | Future ROW | Est. AADT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scofield Ridge Pkwy | Level 2 | Minor collector | 2-3 | 60 ft | 66-70 ft | ~3,000-5,000 |
| Parmer Ln (FM 734) | Level 5 | Principal arterial (TxDOT) | 6 (divided) | 120+ ft | 150 ft (ASMP) | ~45,000-55,000 |
| MoPac (Loop 1) | Level 5 / Freeway | Freeway (TxDOT) | 6-8 (divided + managed lanes) | Varies (200+ ft) | N/A (state facility) | ~90,000-120,000 |

Parmer Lane (FM 734) is the primary east-west arterial serving the Scofield area. TxDOT and CAMPO are conducting the Parmer Lane Corridor Study (FM 734 from MoPac to RM 1431) to identify capacity and safety improvements. MoPac (Loop 1) runs roughly 1 mile west of the site and provides regional north-south freeway access.

## 3. ROW Dedication

Under Austin's Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM) and ASMP, ROW dedication is required when the existing ROW is narrower than the ASMP future ROW standard. For Cinchring Lane (Level 1, 50-ft standard), the existing platted ROW in the Scofield Subdivision is expected to already meet the 50-ft standard. Therefore, **no additional ROW dedication is anticipated** for this project.

If any dedication delta were identified during site plan review, the city would require a dedication along the property frontage as a condition of the building permit or site plan approval. The City of Austin's Residential Review Guidelines (rev. November 2025) govern ROW review for residential projects.

## 4. Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA)

Austin requires a TIA when a proposed development generates **2,000 or more net new vehicular trips per day**. The TIA Determination Worksheet must be submitted to the Transportation Development Services (TDS) Division.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Existing use | Single-family detached (1 unit) |
| Proposed use | Duplex (2 units) |
| Net new units | +1 unit |
| ITE trip generation (Land Use 210/220) | ~9.4 trips/day per dwelling unit |
| Net new daily trips | ~9-10 trips/day |
| TIA threshold | 2,000 trips/day |

**Conclusion: No TIA is required.** The net new trip generation (~10 trips/day) is far below the 2,000-trip threshold. No TIA Determination Worksheet filing is necessary for a project of this scale.

## 5. Access Management -- Driveway Requirements

Austin's TCM Section 7 (Driveways) governs driveway design and spacing. For a duplex on a Level 1 local street:

- **Maximum driveways**: Typically 1-2, depending on lot frontage.
- **Driveway width**: Residential driveway maximum 24 ft (two-way) per TCM.
- **Spacing**: Minimum 35 ft between driveways (edge to edge) if semicircular layout used.
- **Setback from intersection**: Minimum 30 ft from the nearest cross-street curb return.
- **Construction**: Driveway must be constructed within the street frontage of the subject property; no overlap onto adjacent property frontage without written approval.

A single shared driveway serving both duplex units is the most common configuration and satisfies all spacing requirements.

## 6. Transit Access

### Bus Service (CapMetro)

| Route | Name | Nearest Stop | Approx. Distance | Headway |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 392 | Braker | Parmer Ln at McCallen Pass / Tech Ridge | ~1.0-1.5 mi | 30-60 min |
| 243 | Wells Branch | Howard Station / Tech Ridge | ~1.5-2.0 mi | 30-60 min |

The site is not directly served by a bus route on Cinchring Lane. The nearest CapMetro bus service operates along Parmer Lane and the Tech Ridge Park & Ride area, approximately 1.0-2.0 miles from the property. Service frequency is moderate (30-60 minute headways depending on time of day).

### Project Connect Light Rail

The Project Connect Orange Line (light rail) is planned to extend north along the N. Lamar / I-35 corridor. Future stations are contemplated at Parmer Lane and Tech Ridge, but these are **not part of the initial investment phase**. They are identified as future-phase extensions, currently undergoing environmental clearance. No construction timeline has been set for these stations. The nearest planned initial-phase station (North Lamar Transit Center) is approximately 5-6 miles south of the site.

### MetroRail (Red Line)

The existing CapMetro Red Line commuter rail has a station at Howard Station (Tech Ridge area), approximately 2.5 miles east of the site.

## 7. Bicycle and Pedestrian Infrastructure

### Sidewalks
Austin's Land Development Code and Residential Review Guidelines require sidewalks as part of residential development. For a duplex redevelopment on a local street:

- **Sidewalk requirement**: A minimum 5-ft sidewalk is typically required along the property frontage within the ROW.
- **Fee-in-lieu**: If physical constraints prevent sidewalk construction, a fee-in-lieu payment may be accepted per LDE Residential Review Guidelines.
- **Existing conditions**: Cinchring Lane in the Scofield Subdivision may have existing sidewalks on one or both sides from the original subdivision plat; the project must maintain or improve frontage sidewalk to current standards.

### Bicycle Facilities
No dedicated bike lanes exist on Cinchring Lane. As a low-speed, low-volume Level 1 residential street, shared-lane (bicycle-with-traffic) operation is the applicable standard. No bike lane construction is required as part of this project.

The nearest designated bicycle infrastructure is along Parmer Lane and MoPac frontage roads, per the Austin Bicycle Plan and ASMP Active Transportation component.

## 8. Scenic Roadway Overlay

The Austin scenic roadway overlay applies to specific designated corridors including Loop 360, RM 2222 (west of MoPac), Barton Springs Road, Lake Austin Boulevard, and others. **Cinchring Lane is not a designated scenic roadway.** Neither Scofield Ridge Parkway nor Parmer Lane in this segment carries a scenic roadway overlay designation.

**No scenic roadway overlay requirements apply to this project.**

## 9. Summary of Key Findings

| Item | Finding | Action Required |
|---|---|---|
| TIA | Not required (~10 net new trips/day vs. 2,000 threshold) | None |
| ROW dedication | No delta expected (existing ROW meets Level 1 standard) | Confirm at plan review |
| Driveway permit | Required for new driveway construction | Submit driveway permit application |
| Sidewalk | May be required along frontage | Construct or pay fee-in-lieu |
| Transit | Limited; nearest bus ~1 mi on Parmer Ln | Informational only |
| Scenic overlay | Not applicable | None |
| Bike lanes | Not required on Level 1 local street | None |

---

Sources:

- Austin Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM), Sections 2, 7, and 10 (via Municode Library)
- City of Austin TIA Guidelines (June 2022) and TIA Determination Worksheet
- City of Austin LDE Residential Review Guidelines (rev. November 2025)

# Web Follow-ups: Utilities, Schools, Special Districts & Hazards

**Property:** 12713 Cinchring Ln, Austin, TX 78727 (Lot 12, Block M, Scofield Subdivision, Travis County)
**Proposed Use:** Demolish existing SFR; build duplex (2 units, ground-up new construction)
**Research Date:** 2026-06-03

---

## 1. Water -- Austin Water

Austin Water serves this address. A duplex requires a **Utility Tap Plan** prepared by a Texas-licensed PE and submitted to the Tap Plan Review team. Each unit must have a separate meter. No building permits are issued until all tap fees are paid.

**Capital Recovery (Impact) Fees** depend on when the lot was platted. Scofield was platted in the 1980s-90s, so the pre-2018 tier likely applies, but Austin Water determines the applicable tier. Current published rates (lots platted after Oct 1, 2023) are:

| Component   | Per Service Unit |
|-------------|-----------------|
| Water       | $4,800           |
| Wastewater  | $2,900           |
| **Combined**| **$7,700**       |

A duplex = 2 service units, so the combined capital recovery fees could be approximately **$15,400** (2 x $7,700) at the highest tier. Actual amount may be lower depending on plat date. Meter and inspection fees are additional.

**Source:** [Austin Water Rates and Fees](https://www.austintexas.gov/water/rates-and-fees) | [New Service Connections](https://www.austintexas.gov/water/new-service-connections)

---

## 2. Wastewater -- Austin Water

Austin Water provides sanitary sewer service. An existing **concrete sanitary sewer vault** is noted on site. Each duplex unit requires a separate clean-out. The property owner is responsible for installing yard lines (pipes between the property line and the building).

A right-of-way permit from Austin Transportation and Public Works is required before installing service connections. The existing sewer vault should be evaluated during demolition planning -- it may need to be removed, capped, or re-used depending on Austin Water's determination.

**Source:** [New Service Connections](https://www.austintexas.gov/water/new-service-connections) | [Construction Standards](https://www.austintexas.gov/water/construction-standards)

---

## 3. Electric -- Austin Energy

The property is within Austin Energy's service territory. For new duplex construction:

- File a **Building Service Planning Application (BSPA)** through Development Services.
- File a separate **Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA)** for each meter (i.e., one per unit).
- A **spot location** site visit is required to identify the point of service and verify clearances.
- A **Service Availability Letter** can be requested for financing.

Contact: 512-494-9400 or 3-1-1.

**Source:** [Austin Energy -- Apply for Electric Service](https://austinenergy.com/contractors/Construction-Renovation) | [ESPA](https://austinenergy.com/contractors/construction-renovation/electric-service-planning-application)

---

## 4. Gas -- Texas Gas Service

Texas Gas Service is the natural gas provider for the Austin/Travis County area. The 78727 zip code is within their service territory. Gas availability at this specific address should be confirmed by contacting Texas Gas Service directly.

Contact: [texasgasservice.com](https://www.texasgasservice.com/) | Office: 1301 S MoPac Expy, Suite 400, Austin, TX 78746

---

## 5. Telecom / Internet

| Provider       | Availability in 78727         | Notes                              |
|----------------|-------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Spectrum       | ~100% coverage in 78727       | Cable; plans from ~$30/mo          |
| AT&T Fiber     | Available in ~25% of area     | Up to 5 Gbps; verify at address    |
| Google Fiber   | Limited Austin coverage       | Primarily Central/East Austin; check address |

Verify address-level availability at each provider's website.

**Source:** [Allconnect -- 78727 Providers](https://www.allconnect.com/local/tx/austin/zip-78727) | [BroadbandNow -- Austin 78727](https://broadbandnow.com/Texas/Austin?zip=78727)

---

## 6. School District -- Pflugerville ISD

This property is in the **Pflugerville Independent School District** (not Austin ISD or Round Rock ISD). Scofield Farms sits at the western edge of PISD boundaries.

| Level       | School                     | Niche Grade |
|-------------|----------------------------|-------------|
| Elementary  | Parmer Lane Elementary     | B           |
| Middle      | Westview Middle School     | C+          |
| High        | Connally High School       | A- (college prep) |

**Source:** [Scofield Farms Neighborhood Guide](https://www.austinrealestatehomesblog.com/northwest-austin/scofield-farms/) | [Scofield Farms General](https://scofieldfarms.org/general/)

---

## 7. Special Districts

**MUD / PID:** No evidence that Scofield Farms is within a Municipal Utility District (MUD) or Public Improvement District (PID). The subdivision is served directly by City of Austin utilities (Austin Water, Austin Energy). The TCEQ Water Districts Map Viewer can be used to confirm: [TCEQ Map Viewer](https://www.tceq.texas.gov/gis/iwudview.html).

**ESD:** The property may be served by **Travis County Emergency Services District No. 4**, which covers neighborhoods in the Scofield area. Since the property is within Austin city limits, fire service is provided by the Austin Fire Department; the ESD designation relates to supplemental emergency services.

**TIF:** No Tax Increment Financing district was identified for this area.

**Source:** [Travis County ESDs](https://www.traviscountytx.gov/fire-marshal/esd)

---

## 8. Recent Council / Commission Actions

No pending zoning cases were identified for this specific address or the immediate Scofield area in the City of Austin zoning case database.

**Relevant citywide action -- HOME Initiative:** Austin's HOME (Home Options for Middle-income Empowerment) amendments, effective February 5, 2024, allow up to 3 dwelling units by right on SF-1, SF-2, and SF-3 lots. Phase 2 (citywide as of November 16, 2024) further reduced minimum lot sizes. A duplex is permitted by right under HOME in SF-zoned lots without rezoning. However, **HOME does not override private deed restrictions or HOA covenants** (see Section 11 below).

**Source:** [HOME Amendments](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/home-amendments) | [Texas Tribune](https://www.texastribune.org/2023/12/07/austin-zoning-single-family-housing-costs/)

---

## 9. Soil Conditions

The 78727 area of north Austin lies in the **Blackland Prairie** ecological region, characterized by deep, dark, clay-rich soils (Vertisols). Likely soil series in this area include **Houston Black clay** and related series (Altoga, Branyon, Heiden).

**Key characteristics:**
- **Shrink-swell potential:** HIGH. These "cracking clays" expand when wet and contract when dry, forming deep cracks. This is the dominant foundation risk in Austin.
- **Foundation recommendation:** Engineered slab-on-grade with post-tensioned cables or drilled piers. A geotechnical report is strongly recommended before design.
- **Septic suitability:** Poor (high-clay, low-permeability), but not relevant here as city sewer is available.

A site-specific geotechnical investigation should be conducted prior to foundation design.

**Source:** [USDA Web Soil Survey](https://websoilsurvey.nrcs.usda.gov/app/) | [Travis County Soils](https://travis-tx.tamu.edu/about-2/horticulture/soils-and-composting-for-austin/the-real-dirt-on-austin-area-soils/)

---

## 10. Wildfire / Hazard Risk

Scofield Farms is a **suburban, fully developed neighborhood** with no significant wildland-urban interface (WUI) exposure. The area is flat, urbanized, and lacks the dense cedar/juniper vegetation that drives wildfire risk in western Travis County.

Austin's wildfire risk is concentrated in the Edwards Plateau / Hill Country areas (west and southwest Austin). North Austin neighborhoods like Scofield Farms are generally classified as **low wildfire risk**.

The Texas Wildfire Risk Assessment Portal (TxWRAP) can be used for site-specific confirmation: [TxWRAP Map](https://wrap.texaswildfirerisk.com/Map/Public/)

**Source:** [City of Austin Wildfire](https://www.austintexas.gov/department/wildfire) | [TxWRAP](https://texaswildfirerisk.com/)

---

## 11. HOA -- Scofield Farms Residential Owners Association (ROA)

**THIS IS A CRITICAL FEASIBILITY ISSUE FOR THE DUPLEX.**

**HOA:** Scofield Residential Owners Association, Inc.
**Management:** Inframark (formerly Certified Management of Austin)
**Contact:** communitymanagement@inframark.com | 512-287-8000
**Dues:** Reported as under $40/month (~$480/year); includes pool access keycard.
**Website:** [scofieldfarms.org](https://scofieldfarms.org/)

**Architectural Control Committee (ACC):**
- 5-member committee reviews proposed additions and changes.
- ACC approval is required for exterior modifications; contact modifications@inframark.com.

**Deed Restrictions -- Duplex Feasibility Risk:**
Scofield Farms has a Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Deed Restrictions (with at least 8 amendments). The actual deed restriction documents are hosted on the HOA website but their full text was not publicly viewable during this research. Typical 1980s-90s subdivision CCRs in Texas **restrict lots to single-family residential use**, which would prohibit a duplex regardless of what city zoning (HOME initiative) allows.

**Key legal principle:** Under Texas law, city zoning is the floor and deed restrictions are the ceiling. The HOME initiative explicitly does not override private deed restrictions. If the Scofield Farms CCRs restrict the property to single-family use, a duplex cannot be built without either (a) obtaining a variance/waiver from the HOA, or (b) the HOA choosing not to enforce the restriction.

**Action Required:** Before proceeding with duplex design, the owner must obtain and review the Scofield Farms Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Deed Restrictions (and all amendments) to determine whether multi-family or duplex use is prohibited. This document can be requested from Inframark or found in the Travis County deed records.

**Source:** [Scofield Farms HOA](https://scofieldfarms.org/) | [HOA Rules & Regs Documents](https://scofieldfarms.org/scofield-farms-roa-rules-and-regulations-documents/) | [Community Not Commodity -- HOA & HOME](https://communitynotcommodity.com/2023/11/17/if-you-have-deed-restrictions-or-live-in-an-hoa-city-halls-h-o-m-e-rezoning-plan-impacts-you/)

---

## Summary of Key Findings

| Topic | Finding | Risk/Action |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| Water | Austin Water; tap plan + impact fees ~$15,400 for 2 units | Budget for fees |
| Wastewater | Austin Water sewer; existing vault on site | Coordinate with AW on vault disposition |
| Electric | Austin Energy; ESPA per unit | Standard process |
| Gas | Texas Gas Service; confirm at address | Verify availability |
| Telecom | Spectrum (best coverage), AT&T, Google Fiber (limited) | Check address |
| Schools | Pflugerville ISD (Parmer Lane / Westview / Connally) | Informational |
| Special Districts | No MUD/PID identified; within city limits | Low concern |
| Zoning/Council | HOME allows duplex by right in SF zones | Favorable |
| Soil | High shrink-swell clay; geotech report needed | Budget for geotech |
| Wildfire | Low risk (suburban, flat, no WUI) | Low concern |
| **HOA** | **Scofield Farms ROA -- deed restrictions likely restrict to SFR** | **CRITICAL: Review CCRs before proceeding** |
